entries.㞢: Pictogram – a cattle head with horns. In the oracle bone script, 㞢 and 之 are different characters. In early oracle bone script, 㞢 was borrowed to represent 有. In late oracle bone script, 㞢 was replaced by 又. Post-Qin dictionaries often treat 㞢 as an ancient form of 之.
entries.㞷:
According to oracle scripts and bronze inscriptions, a Phono-semantic compound: 止 (foot, semantic) + 王 (phonetic). This is the original form of 往.

According to small seal scripts, a Phono-semantic compound: 屮 (sprout, semantic) + 王 (phonetic). Xu Shen misinterpreted it as a compound of 𡳿/㞢 (now 之) + 土, influenced by 封.

See also similar but unrelated 𡴀 (now 丰) and 𤯓 (now 生).

entries.㪔:
Compound ideogram: 林 (trees, forest) + 攴 (to knock, to tap), also written with hemp stalks 𣏟 (> 𢽳) or bamboo 竹 instead of two trees. The original meanings are "to clear a place from vegetation; to kill". The character later started meaning "to dissipate, to disperse" since bamboo in particular breaks easily into pieces; eventually, the meaning shifted to "to walk around, to stroll".

This character is the original form of 散, originally written as 𣀙 as seen in the Shuowen Jiezi.
entries.㪾: Phono-semantic compound: 各 (phonetic) + 斤 (axe, semantic).
entries.㫃:
Pictogram – a flag on a pole with a decoration on top. Today, the flag (unrelated to 人) is detached from the pole with decoration, stylized as 方. Related to 倝 but both are unrelated to 朝.

The character today appears as 𭤨 when next to another component (e.g., 旅 and 游); the top component, despite its appearance, is unrelated to 伤, 乞, and 每.

entries.七:
Pictogram – a vertical stroke and a horizontal stroke bisecting each other – original character of 切.

The top-most horizontal stroke is done from left to right. The vertical stroke and bottom-most horizontal stroke are done as one stroke, from top-left to bottom-right.
entries.丈: Compound ideogram: 十 (ten) + 又 (hand) – ten chi (尺) is one zhang (丈). Similar but unrelated to 支.
entries.三:
Ideogram – - three parallel strokes. Compare with 一, one stroke meaning “one”, 二, two strokes meaning “two”, and 亖, four strokes meaning “four”.

一 (one). See also 畺. Unrelated to 丰.
entries.上: Ideogram: short horizontal above long arc (contrast 下).
entries.下: Ideogram: short horizontal below long arc (contrast 上).
entries.不:
Pictogram: the calyx of a flower. 不 was composed into a phono-semantic character with the pictograph for mouth (口), to form 否, representing “no” (negation). This composed meaning then spread back to the original character 不, making it a synonym of 否. A new character of 柎 was eventually created to represent the original meaning of calyx.

Following Shuowen’s interpretation, Karlgren and Wieger interpret it as a bird flying toward the sky (一). The sky being the limit for the bird, thus the idea of negation.
entries.丐: Corruption of 匄. Its original meaning is unknown; perhaps it was "to damage".
entries.丑:
Pictogram – a hand with emphasizing claws or fingernails.

Phonetically borrowed to represent an earthly branch. It also started meaning "ugly" as a simplified form of an unrelated character with same pronunciation, 醜.
entries.专: From cursive script (East Asia) of 專.
entries.世:
Phonetic loan: Variant form of 枼 (the original form of 葉) with the tree removed.

Shuowen interprets it as 十 triplicated: thirty years make one generation (thirty times twelve months gives 360 months).
entries.丘: Ideogram – hill. Earlier form closer to 丠, as in 虛. Compare 山. Unrelated to 兵 and 斤.
entries.丛: Simpified Chinese. A stroke was added in order to distinguish from 从. It can be analyzed as an Compound ideogram: 一 ((土) ground, floor) + 从 (two people standing together) – to make cluster.
entries.东: From cursive script (East Asia) of 東; compare 車 → 车.
entries.丝: Simplified from 絲. via variant 𢇁.
entries.丞: Compound ideogram: 卩 (kneeling person) + 廾 (both hands) + 凵 (hole) – to rescue a person from a hole. Compare 承.
entries.丟: Compound ideogram: 一 (one (once)) + 去 (to go; to remove).
entries.並: From the clerical script (隸書) of 竝, originally depicting two people standing side-by-side.
entries.丩: Pictogram: two entangled ropes – to entangle; to intertwine. Original form of 糾. See also 己.
entries.中:
Pictogram – a flagpole, as depicted in its original form 𠁩. Based on archaeological evidence, the middle box has been interpreted as a drum (建鼓). This flagpole with a drum was placed in the center of a field to gather people and to detect the direction of the wind. In addition, the pronunciation of 中 is reminiscent of the beating of a drum.

Shuowen interprets the character as a vertical stroke 丨 passing through the center of 口, indicating the center.

It has also been interpreted as an arrow in the center of a target.
entries.丮: Pictogram – A person kneeling with their hands stretched out, as if they are holding something.
entries.丳: Variant/corruption of 𠁷, which is a duplication of 串.
entries.丵: Pictogram – Derived from 辛, a chisel tool.
entries.丶: Pictogram – - A small fire on a torch, when used as the original form of 主.
entries.丹: Pictogram – of a well or mine with cinnabar inside. It can also indicate "red cinnabar" used in dyeing clothes (e.g., 彤). The original version is 𠂁.
entries.为: From cursive script (East Asia) of 為; compare Japanese 為 → ゐ.
entries.丽: Compound ideogram – - Two people. Current form resembles the upper part of 麗.
entries.乂: Pictogram – a tool similar to a knife, perhaps a sickle; see also 辛. In some other versions both on oracle bones and bronzes, it looks like a huge pair of scissors used to cut weed. The original meaning of "mow, cut weed; sickle" is preserved in 刈. Unrelated to 爻.
entries.久: Used interchangeably with 氒 in oracle bone script. Likely a Pictogram – of an arrow tip.
entries.义:
Derived from 乂. 

Originally 乂 was borrowed because of homophony and being mostly displaced by (刈). Later, to avoid confusion a stroke was added on top of 乂 to distinguish correctly. Now a homophonic character; compare 舊 → 旧
entries.之:
Compound ideogram: 止 (foot) + 一 (the beginning place), originally written as 㞢; compound meaning “to go”. Hence, the character was similar to 出.

Eventually, the footprint pointing upwards became a point, as in the right component of 往 (which, in this case, is unrelated to 主).

See also 帀, which probably comes from the inverted version of 㞢. See also 乏, which is thought to derive from a modification of the upper component 一.
entries.乍: Pictogram – an axe chopping wood. Original form of 柞.
entries.乏: Chen Jian suggests that the graph derives from ⿱口⿰止止, an ideogram shared by 範 and 圍: one 止 was omitted, and one stroke was slanted to avoid confusion with 正.
entries.乐:
Unorthodox variant Simplified from 樂. found in a Movable type#Metal movable type in China copy of 《嶺南逸事》. First attested in 《宋元以來俗字譜》, a Variant Chinese character dictionary compiled in 1930 that records unorthodox forms (俗字) that have existed since the Song dynasty. Also found as a Cursive script (East Asia) (草書) of Simplified from 樂. in 《中國書法大字典》.

Eventually adopted as an official simplified character by the People's Republic of China in the 1956 Chinese Character Simplification Scheme.
entries.乑: Pictogram: 人 (human) + 人 + 人 – many humans are standing.
entries.乖: According to Xu Shen, 𦫳 together with 𠔁.
entries.乗: Variant form of 乘 written in clerical script found in the 《魯峻碑陰》 stone tablet of the Han dynasty#Eastern Han period.
entries.乘: Pictogram – a person 大 climbing a tree 木, with the feet visible. Etymology clearer in alternative form 椉. In the form 乘, simplified to 禾 + 北.
entries.九:
Pictogram – a stylized hand, with bent wrist/forearm (hence the hook stroke at lower right). Earlier forms resemble 手, 寸. The original meaning of the glyph was “elbow”, which is now written 肘.

After the meaning “elbow” was forgotten, 九 was taken to symbolize a fist tightening to bump up against something; thus, there is a metaphorical bumping up of nine against ten, which is the last number when counting on one's fingers.
entries.乞:
Variant of 气, distinguished to indicate a phonetically borrowed meaning “to beg”.

The top component of the character is unrelated to 旅, 傷, 复, 每 as well as 人.
entries.习: Simplified from 習. (elimination of 白 and 羽 →) in the 1956 Chinese Character Simplification Scheme by the People's Republic of China. Not known to have existed prior to that.
entries.书: Simplified from 書. from cursive script with phonetic corrupted, now resembles a simpler hand holding a brush.
entries.乳: Pictogram: A kneeling woman holding and breastfeeding a child. The woman resembles the character 母.
entries.亀: Variant of 龜, Simplified from 龜. The modern Japanese usage is of reform (shinjitai) nature.
entries.亂: Phono-semantic compound: 𤔔 (phonetic) + 乙 (semantic). The left-side component 𤔔 is itself ideogrammatic, depicting the effort to comb a tangle of threads, hence the semantic link to order and disorder.
entries.了:
According to the Shuowen Jiezi, a Pictogram – of a baby without arms. Compare with 子, where the arms are visible. The Shuowen defines 了 as "the crossing of lower legs". 

In the Shuowen Jiezi Zhu, a commentary to the Shuowen Jiezi, it is said that the pictogram instead depicts entangled legs (了戾). 

Its relation with the meaning "to finish" is likely via sound loan, but an argument can be made about "entangled legs" → "tie"→ "finish".

Unrelated to 亨.
entries.予: Phonetic loan: originally written as 呂, phonetically borrowed for the meanings "I; give". Later, 亅 was added at the bottom as a distinguishing mark and the whole character was heavily stylized. See also 幻.
entries.事: Compound ideogram: 又 (hand) + 中 (a flagpole with a drum) – flag in hand > to perform one's job. Compare 吏. Furthermore, both characters are related to 史, which is a variant without the horizontal stroke on top.
entries.二: Ideogram – - two parallel strokes. Compare with 一, one stroke meaning one, 三, three strokes meaning three, and 亖, four strokes meaning four. 一 (one).
entries.亍: Simplified from 行. – the right side of the character.
entries.互: Ideogram: 牙 and a distinguishing mark. Early texts often used 互 and 牙 interchangeably.
entries.井:
Pictogram – a square well, with supports on four sides.

Some forms have a stone inside the well, as in 丼.

Alternatively, original character of 刑, 形 and 型.
entries.亘:
Simplified from 宣.

Originally 𠄢: Compound ideogram: 二 + 囘.
entries.亙:
Compound ideogram: 二 + 月 (moon).

Possibly also the original form of 恆.
entries.亞: Pictogram: an overhead view of a construction, likely a 亞-shaped tomb. Perhaps borrowed phonetically to mean "second; inferior".
entries.亡: Generally considered the original graph of 芒, evidenced by early and late Shang bronzes (in the name 亡冬) depicting a knife edge marked with a circle. However, it diverges from the oracle bone form; intermediate forms are needed to bridge the two. In the Oracle bone script, 亡 means "not have", a function later assumed by 無 (a distinct word from 亡). A few non-negative occurrences equate to 衁 (read as 嚮), which serves as a connective between day-names.
entries.交: Pictogram – a human with crossed legs. In today's writing, the upper part of the human is similar to 立, which in turn depicts a man standing. Unrelated to 父.
entries.亥: Pictogram – depiction uncertain. Some propose it depicts a plant's roots underground, possibly as the original form of 荄. Others propose it is an animal, similar in origin to 豕.
entries.亦: Ideogram – a human figure (大) with emphasis marks on the armpits — original form of 腋. Later phonetically borrowed to represent 亦.
entries.产: Simplified from 産. (a variant of 產) by removing 生.
entries.享: Pictogram – - An ancestral shrine. See also 亯 and 亨. Unrelated to 郭.
entries.京:
Pictogram – a tall building. Compare 高.

When used as a component on top of the character, the character loses the bottom part 小. (e.g., 亮 and 亭).
entries.亭: The Kangxi radical of the tower 京 (or 髙 > 高 according to its variants) with the phonetic component 丁 (nail). In the variant 𠅘, the body of the tower is more recognizable.
entries.亮: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 京 (phonetic). In the variant 𠅙, the body of the tower is more recognizable.
entries.亶: Phono-semantic compound: 㐭 (semantic) + 旦 (phonetic), originally a Compound ideogram: 㐭 (granary) + 虫 (insect).
entries.人:
Pictogram – side view of a standing man, highlighting an arm and a leg. Compare 大, 立, 卩, 夭, and 氏 according to one interpretation. See also the original version of 年.

亼 is similar but unrelated; it represents an open mouth flipped upside down and appears on top of characters such as 食, 金, 令, 龠, and 今.

It represents a roof in the characters 余, 茶, 舍, and 倉. It represents a flag on a flagpole in 㫃. Eventually, it represents two parallel mountain walls in 谷.

The stylized version to the left of the characters is 亻 (see also 千). Similar but unrelated to 彳.
entries.亻: A stylization of 人. See also 千. Similar but unrelated to 彳.
entries.亼:
Compound ideogram: 入 + 一. To gather from three sides, if connected to the ancient version of 集.

Otherwise, it's an open mouth 口 reversed upside-down and the original version of 今. This character can be seen in 合, 今, 會, 令, 侖, 食, 僉, and 龠. Unrelated to 俞, in which it represents part of a flipped vessel, 由.
entries.仂: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 力 (phonetic).
entries.仃: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (man, semantic) + 丁 (phonetic).
entries.仄: Phono-semantic compound: 厂 (cliff, semantic) + 夨 (man with crooked head, phonetic) – "oblique, slanted"
entries.仇: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 九 (phonetic) – spouse.
entries.仉: Corruption of 𤓯, an ancient form of 掌. In its current form, the left part became 亻, while the right became 几.
entries.今:
Ideogram – An inverted 曰 ("to speak"), hence 亼 with a horizontal stroke at the bottom, so the inverted mouth means "not to speak".

Another theory suggests that it depicts something in the mouth. Maybe the original form of 噤 or 吟. If so, the derivative 含 refers to the original word.
entries.介: Compound ideogram: 人 + two marks encompassing, indicating "in between". Folk etymology interprets the two marks as two components of an armor.
entries.仌:
Pictogram – two blocks of ice. Original form of 冰.

Next to a character, they are compressed and stylized as 冫 (which is unrelated to 氵 and 次).

仒
entries.从: Compound ideogram – a person (人) walking with another person in the same direction – to follow. 人. See the bottom component of 旅 (< 𣃨).
entries.仏: Used since the Northern and Southern dynasties. To avoid using the character 佛, 某 is used instead; the character is Compound ideogram: 人 + 厶, where 厶 is a variant form of 某.
entries.仓: Variant character of 倉, listed in the Shuowen Jiezi as an "odd character". This variant first appeared in Jin_(Chinese_state) bamboo slips.
entries.仔: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 子 (phonetic)
entries.仕: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 士 (a person engaged in an official position, phonetic). It is mainly used as a verb meaning "to serve."
entries.他:
Phono-semantic compound: 人 (man, semantic) + 也 (phonetic).

Corrupted form of 佗, which is found in Zuozhuan.
entries.付: Compound ideogram: 人 (person) + 又 (hand) or Compound ideogram: 人 (person) + 寸 (hand) – to deliver, to give to someone.
entries.仙:
Compound ideogram: 人 (person, semantic) + 山 (mountain, phonetic) — a person moving into a mountain to practise becoming immortal.

Originally 僊. The current form is first attested in the clerical script of the Han dynasty.
entries.代: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 弋 (phonetic)
entries.令: Compound ideogram: 亼 + 卩. The upper part is an open mouth to convey the idea of giving orders, while the bottom part is a kneeling man. Compare 兄, in which an open mouth on top of the character conveys the same idea of giving orders.
entries.以:
Pictogram – a person (人) carrying something. It is often simplified to 㠯 in pre-Qin ancient scripts. Today, the person is partly visible on the right (see also the stylization in 从).

See also 重, in which a person is carrying a bag, 央, in which a person is carrying a pole.
entries.仰: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 卬 (phonetic).
entries.仲: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 中 (middle, phonetic).
entries.价:
Phono-semantic compound: 人 (semantic) + 介 (phonetic).

Also Simplified from 價.; simplified to an existing character.
entries.仹: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (human, semantic) + 丰 (phonetic).
entries.任:
Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 壬 (phonetic) – to carry on a shoulder pole.

Note that its phonetic part 壬 may be the graphical representation of 任, depicting a shoulder pole rotated by 90 degrees.
entries.企: 人 (person) + 止 (foot) – a person standing on tiptoes.
entries.伃: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 予 (phonetic)
entries.伊: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 尹 (phonetic).
entries.伎: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 支 (phonetic).
entries.伏:
Compound ideogram: 人 (person) + 犬 (dog) – meaning “prostrate”.

A dog at the side of a person.

A person adopting the position of a dog.
entries.伐: Compound ideogram: 人 (person) + 戈 (spear). Based on the image of cutting a person’s neck with a spear, it expresses the meanings of "to cut off" or "to strike."
entries.休: Compound ideogram: 人 (man) + 木 (tree) – a man leaning against a tree, resting.
entries.伙: Phono-semantic compound (形聲) and ideogrammic compound (會意): semantic 人 (“person”) + phonetic 火/ semantic 火.
entries.会: Unorthodox variant of 會. From cursive script (East Asia).
entries.伟: From the cursive script (East Asia) of 偉//. Simplified from 偉.
entries.传: From cursive script (East Asia) of 傳. Simplified from 傳.
entries.伤: Simplified from 傷. Compare 㘯.
entries.伫:
Simplified from 佇.

The right-hand side was reduced to 㝉 (宀 + 一) to distinguish it from 宁, the simplified form of 寧.
entries.伯: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 白 (phonetic).
entries.伶: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (man; person, semantic) + 令 (phonetic)
entries.伸: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (man, semantic) + 申 (phonetic).
entries.伺: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, man, semantic) + 司 (phonetic) – a person stands beside (attends), looks in.
entries.似: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (human, semantic) + 以 (phonetic).
entries.但: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 旦 (phonetic).
entries.佇: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (man, semantic) + 宁 (phonetic).
entries.位: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (man, semantic) + 立 (stand, phonetic). Often simply written as 立 in idiomatic expressions such as 即位 in Western Zhou inscriptions.
entries.低: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (man, person, semantic) + 氐 (phonetic) – a person lowering themselves, bowing.
entries.住: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (semantic) + 主 (phonetic). See also 駐.
entries.佐: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 左 (phonetic).
entries.何:
In the oracle bone script, a Pictogram: a man carrying something on their shoulder – the original form of 荷.

The object being carried may have been 戈, in which case the character is also an Compound ideogram: 人 (person, semantic) + 戈 (dagger-axe, phonetic).

In the bronze inscriptions, some forms of the character were Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 可 (phonetic), from which the modern form derives.
entries.佗: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (human, semantic) + 它 (phonetic).
entries.佘: Derived from 余 and 舍. The character was differentiated from these two characters around the time of the Han dynasty, possibly a Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 示 (phonetic).
entries.佚: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (man; person, semantic) + 失 (phonetic)
entries.佛: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 弗 (phonetic).
entries.作: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 乍 (phonetic).
entries.佟: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (man, semantic) + 冬 (phonetic).
entries.你: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 尔 (phonetic). Alternatively, Compound ideogram: 人 (person) + 尔 (you)
entries.佤:
Simplified from 邷.

A replacement for 𱭵.
entries.佩:
A compound of 人 (person) + 凡 + 巾 (piece of cloth). Original meaning is a large sash.

The role of 凡 is unclear. Some think that it is a phonetic component, but the finals differ substantially (compare 凡 to 佩).
entries.佬: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (man; person, semantic) + 老 (phonetic).
entries.佮: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 合 (phonetic).
entries.佳: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (man; person, semantic) + 圭 (phonetic).
entries.併: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (man, semantic) + 并 (phonetic).
entries.佷: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 艮 (phonetic).
entries.佹: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 危 (phonetic).
entries.使: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (semantic) + 吏 (phonetic). However, the phonetic component should add part of the meaning since it represents a hand holding perhaps a flag to mean "representative, ambassador".
entries.侄: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (man, semantic) + 至 (phonetic).
entries.侈: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 多 (phonetic).
entries.侍: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 寺 (phonetic).
entries.侎: Li Shoukui (2015) notes that 侎 may potentially be a corruption of 屎 that later adapted an etymologically unrelated reading and meaning, on the basis that Shuowen Jiezi writes that the origin of 侎 is unknown, that 尸 and 人 were occasionally used interchangeably in oracle bone script writing, and that given 尿 was often corrupted as ⿰亻水 in ancient writing, one cannot rule out that 侎 doesn't follow the same potential origin.
entries.侏: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (human, semantic) + 朱 (phonetic).
entries.侖: Compound ideogram: 亼 + 冊 (book). The component 亼 can be interpreted as either "gather" ("to gather books" therefore "order") or as a downward mouth ("reading words as they're written" therefore "order"). Similar but unrelated to 龠.
entries.侗: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 同 (phonetic)
entries.供: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 共 (phonetic).
entries.依: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (human, semantic) + 衣 (phonetic).
entries.侮: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 每 (phonetic).
entries.侲: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 辰 (phonetic).
entries.侵: According to Shuowen Jiezi, an Compound ideogram: 人 (person) + 帚 (broom) + 又 (hand) – a person with a broom in hand.
entries.侶: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 呂 (phonetic).
entries.侻: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 兌 (phonetic).
entries.便:
According to Shuowen, an Compound ideogram: 人 (person) + 更 (to change) – to change one's posture to make oneself comfortable.

Alternatively, this may be the original character for 鞭, from 人 (person) + 𠓥 (whip), as seen in the bronze script.
entries.俄: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 我 (phonetic).
entries.俅: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (man, semantic) + 求 (phonetic)
entries.俇: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 狂 (phonetic).
entries.俈: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (man; person, semantic) + 告 (phonetic).
entries.俊: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 夋 (phonetic).
entries.俍: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 良 (phonetic).
entries.俎: Pictogram – sacrificial altar for meat. The altar's legs are on the left and the vessel is on the right.
entries.俑: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (human, semantic) + 用 (phonetic)
entries.俔: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (semantic) + 見 (to see, phonetic).
entries.俗: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 谷 (phonetic) – customs of people.
entries.俘: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 孚 (to capture, phonetic) – to capture. Originally written 孚, 人 was added later.
entries.俛: Compound ideogram: 人 (person) + 免 (to escape, avoid).
entries.俜: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 甹 (phonetic).
entries.保:
In the oracle script, this character was an Compound ideogram: 人 (person) + 子 (child) – a person carrying a child on his back; to carry (a child) > to protect. See also 好.

In early bronze inscriptions, 爪 was added to the person to emphasize that the person was carrying the child. This was later simplified into one or two strokes. The current form has two.
entries.俞:
Compound ideogram – in Shang bronze inscriptions: 舟 (a vertically placed plate, implying "to flip or change") + a "↑"-like element (an inverted 口 above "◇", depicting speaking; original form of 諭 or 喻). The whole character is the original form of 渝 or 輸.

Unrelated to 前, 刖, 巜, and 巛.
entries.俟: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 矣 (phonetic).
entries.俬: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (people, semantic) + 私 (phonetic).
entries.俯: In bronze inscriptions, Phono-semantic compound: 府 (phonetic) + 勹 (person bending over, semantic). In the modern script 勹 has changed to 亻.
entries.俳: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 非 (phonetic).
entries.俵: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 表 (phonetic).
entries.俶: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 叔 (phonetic).
entries.俸: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 奉 (phonetic).
entries.俺: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 奄 (phonetic).
entries.倀: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 長 (phonetic)
entries.倈: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 來 (phonetic).
entries.倉: In oracle bone and bronze inscriptions, Pictogram: a granary, depicting its roof (亼), a door (戶), and a pit for storing grain (口). Alternatively an Compound ideogram: 合 (gather) + 戶 (door) – a warehouse. The component 戶 corrupted into 𠁣 in Qin bamboo slips. This form was inherited in small seal script and was misinterpreted as cognate with the unrelated 食 in the Shuowen Jiezi.
entries.個: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 固 (phonetic).
entries.倌:
Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 官 (phonetic).

Possibly, Compound ideogram: 人 + 官 - a person [working] and a mansion.
entries.們: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 門 (phonetic).
entries.倓: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 炎 (phonetic).
entries.倔: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 屈 (phonetic).
entries.倗: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 朋 (phonetic).
entries.倘: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 尚 (phonetic).
entries.候: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (semantic) + 矦 (phonetic), as 𠊱. The 矦 component (modified so that ⺈ becomes 乛 on top and 丿 at left becomes 丨) is an ancient form of 侯.
entries.倝: Phono-semantic compound: 旦 (sunrise, semantic) + 㫃 (phonetic).
entries.倞: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 京 (phonetic).
entries.借: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 昔 (phonetic).
entries.倠: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 隹 (phonetic).
entries.倣: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 放 (phonetic).
entries.値: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 直 (phonetic). The character originally conveyed the meaning of "to stand upright." Associated with the character 直, it meant "to hit" or "to be correct," and by extension, it came to mean "value" or "worth."
entries.倥: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 空 (phonetic).
entries.倦: In the Chu (state) form, a Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 龹 (phonetic). In the Small Seal Script form, a Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 卷 (phonetic).
entries.倭: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 委 (phonetic).
entries.倯: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 松 (phonetic).
entries.倱: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 昆 (phonetic).
entries.偃: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (man, semantic) + 匽 (phonetic).
entries.假: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 叚 (phonetic).
entries.偈: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 曷 (phonetic).
entries.偋: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 屏 (phonetic).
entries.偌: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (man, semantic) + 若 (phonetic).
entries.偎: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (man; person, semantic) + 畏 (phonetic)
entries.偔: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (man; person, semantic) + 咢 (phonetic).
entries.偕: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (man, semantic) + 皆 (phonetic)
entries.偞: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 枼 (phonetic).
entries.偠: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 要 (phonetic).
entries.健: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 建 (phonetic).
entries.偪: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 畐 (phonetic).
entries.偲: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 思 (phonetic).
entries.偵: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 貞 (to inquire, phonetic). It expresses the idea of “asking” or “inquiring.”
entries.偶: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 禺 (phonetic) – a statue of a person, an idol.
entries.偺: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 昝 (phonetic).
entries.偽:
Simplified from 僞.

Simplified from 僞. Phono-semantic compound: 人 (man, semantic) + 為 (to make, phonetic), originally “artificial”.
entries.傀: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (human, semantic) + 鬼 (phonetic).
entries.傅: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 尃 (phonetic).
entries.傌: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 馬 (phonetic).
entries.傏: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 唐 (phonetic).
entries.傑: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 桀 (phonetic).
entries.傒: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 奚 (phonetic).
entries.傘: Pictogram – - pictographic representation of an umbrella.
entries.傛: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (man, semantic) + 容 (phonetic)
entries.傫: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (human, semantic) + 累 (phonetic).
entries.催: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 崔 (phonetic).
entries.傱: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 從 (phonetic).
entries.傲: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 敖 (phonetic).
entries.傳: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (man, semantic) + 專 (phonetic).
entries.傷:
Phono-semantic compound: 人 (semantic) + 𥏻 (phonetic).

Current form resembles 从 + 昜. The top component of the character is unrelated to 旅, 每, 复, 乞 as well as 人.
entries.傹: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 竟 (phonetic).
entries.傾: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (man, semantic) + 頃 (phonetic). Note that it is not 化 + 頁.
entries.僂: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (man; person, semantic) + 婁 (phonetic).
entries.僇: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (human, semantic) + 翏 (phonetic).
entries.僉:
Originally, Compound ideogram: 亼 + 兄 written twice. It originally indicates people answering to a call together or saying the same thing unanimously.

Since the Small Seal script version, the whole character is stylized as Compound ideogram: 亼 + 吅 + 从.
entries.僊: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 遷 (phonetic).
entries.僎: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (human, semantic) + 巽 (phonetic).
entries.像: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 象 (phonetic).
entries.僓: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (human, semantic) + 貴 (phonetic).
entries.僔: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (people, semantic) + 尊 (phonetic)
entries.僖: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 喜 (phonetic).
entries.僚: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 尞 (phonetic).
entries.僝: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (human, semantic) + 孱 (phonetic).
entries.僞: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 爲 (phonetic).
entries.僤: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (human, semantic) + 單 (phonetic).
entries.僥: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (human, semantic) + 堯 (phonetic).
entries.僧: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 曾 (phonetic) – a kind of person (a Buddhist monk).
entries.僮: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 童 (phonetic)
entries.僰: Phono-semantic compound: 棘 (phonetic) + 人 (person; people, semantic).
entries.僸: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (human, semantic) + 禁 (phonetic).
entries.價: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (semantic) + 賈 (sell, phonetic).
entries.儃: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (human, semantic) + 亶 (phonetic).
entries.儅: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (human, semantic) + 當 (phonetic).
entries.儉: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 僉 (phonetic).
entries.儌: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (human, semantic) + 敫 (phonetic).
entries.儑: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (human, semantic) + 㬎 (phonetic).
entries.儒: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (human, semantic) + 需 (phonetic).
entries.儓: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (human, semantic) + 臺 (phonetic).
entries.儡: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (man, semantic) + 畾 (phonetic)
entries.儰: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 蔿 (phonetic)
entries.儵: Phono-semantic compound: 攸 (phonetic) + 黑 (black, semantic).
entries.儷: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 麗 (phonetic).
entries.儽: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (human, semantic) + 纍 (phonetic).
entries.儿:
Pictogram – a standing person. A radical form of 人.

Also Simplified from 兒.

In the character 亮, the standing person 儿 was corrupted into 几. Unrelated to 匹.
entries.允: Pictogram – a person with the hands held behind the back, possibly the original character for 逡巡.
entries.元: Pictogram – a figure with two lines 上 for a head (one connected to body, one above it), emphasizing the head.
entries.兄: Compound ideogram: 口 + 儿 to convey the idea of giving orders. The original meaning of "elder brother" refers to the fact that the elder brother gives order to the younger brothers and his sisters. Compare 令, in which an open mouth on top of the character conveys the same idea of giving orders. Similar to 欠, in which there is a kneeling man with an open mouth.
entries.充: Compound ideogram: 𠫓 (a newborn) + 儿 (standing person) – A newborn grows to stand and become mature.
entries.兆:
Pictogram: 人 (person) + 水 (water) + 人 (person) – two people fleeing with their backs to a flood.

Some oracle bone script variants are written identically to 化 (one upright person and one upside-down person). suggests that this variant uses 化 as a phonetic component due to their phonological connection in Old Chinese.

Shuowen, without access to oracle bone script, considered it a Pictogram – of cracks formed on a heated tortoise shell or bone during divination.
entries.先: Compound ideogram: 止 (foot) + 儿 (person) – to go forward.
entries.光: Compound ideogram: 火 (fire) + 卩 (kneeling person) – fire over a person's head, emphasizing the shining of light (Shuowen).
entries.克:
Origin uncertain. Oracle bone and bronze forms consist of 由 (or simply 口) over a sideways-standing basin (see also 般).

The sideways basin may signify overturning, extending to mean "to change"—representing the word 革.
entries.兌:
In the oracle bone script, it is a Compound ideogram: 八 (speech; breath) + 口 (mouth) + 人 (person) – speech; original character of 說.

Alternatively, 八 may be interpreted as smile lines above the mouth (Gao Hongjin) or as meaning “to divide” (Lin Yiguang, i.e. the mouth is divided when smiling); in either case, the character would be the original character of 悅.

Shuowen interprets this character as a Phono-semantic compound: 㕣 (phonetic) + 儿 (person, semantic).
entries.免:
Pictogram – a man wearing a ceremonial hat. Then borrowed for abstract meanings. The derivative 冕 refers to the original word.

See also 敖, 冒, and 美.
entries.兒: Pictogram: an infant with an imperfect cranium (i.e. fontanelle).
entries.兓: Compound ideogram: duplication of 兂 ("hairpin") – sharp.
entries.兗: Originally 㕣. The current form is possibly influenced by 𧮲, ancient form of 㕣.
entries.党:
Phono-semantic compound: 尚 (phonetic) + 儿 (human, semantic).

Besides its original senses, it is used as a simplified substitute for the character 黨.
entries.兛: Compound ideogram: 克 (gram) + 千 (one thousand)
entries.兜: Compound ideogram: 𠑹 (cover) + 皃 (head): a helmet.
entries.入:
Ideogram – - an arrowhead indicating "to enter".

Compare 人.
entries.內: Compound ideogram: 冂 (city outskirts) + 入 (to enter) – entering the city through its outskirts - inside, within.
entries.全: Compound ideogram: 入 + 玉 (jade) – a whole piece of jade; pure jade.
entries.兩:
According to Shuowen Jiezi an Compound ideogram: 一 + 㒳.

 observes that, in historical forms, the character is two 丙 joined together; this would make 丙 the phonetic component in a sort of phono-ideogrammic compound (see also).

The character could be linked to the original form of 更, which represents two chariots and a whip.
entries.兪:
In oracle bone script, it was likely a Phono-semantic compound: semantic 凡 + phonetic inverted 由, hence a form vaguely similar to 甲. It's also possible that the phonetic component is instead an ancient form of 鏃.

In bronze inscriptions, 凡 corrupted into 舟, and the bottom-right subcomponent of 甲 gradually corrupted into two lines 巜 (now written 刂). The upper-right subcomponent (vaguely similar to 口) was eventually stylized as (亼) and moved to the top of the character in bamboo slips. Eventually, 舟 was further corrupted into 月, arriving at the modern form 俞.

Unrelated to 前, 刖, 巜, and 巛.
entries.八:
Pictogram: two bent lines indicating the original meaning of "to divide". This character is later borrowed to mean "eight" because of homonymy, making the original meaning obsolete (now represented by 分 and 別).

Unrelated to the bottom part of 兵, 共, 具, and 興, in which it represents two hands holding an object. Also unrelated to 只 and 兑 in which it represents air coming out of a mouth. Unrelated to 貝. Eventually, unrelated to the bottom part of 其, 真, and 典, in which it represents the legs of a table.
entries.六: Pictogram – perhaps a shed. Originally using the similar-sounding word 廬 to represent the concept “six” (Liu Xinglong). Alternatively, it may be an ancient counting symbol.
entries.兮: Originally the same character as 乎. The oracle bone form consists of 丂 and two vertical strokes above; the two strokes are parallel in most oracle bone attestations, possibly representing finer branches (i.e. the sound produced by wind blows past these branches).
entries.兵: Compound ideogram: 斤 (a short axe) + 廾 (2 hands) – a pair of hands holding a weapon. Unrelated to 丘.
entries.典:
Compound ideogram: 冊 (books) + 丌 (table) – (official) books on a table.

Unrelated to 曲 and 曹.
entries.兹:
Unorthodox variant Simplified from 茲. with 䒑 as the top component instead of 艹 found in the Ming dynasty orthographic dictionary 《俗書刊誤》.

The earliest known form of this character can be traced back to the Han dynasty 《孔宙碑》 tablet written in clerical script. 

This character became the orthodox form in mainland China based on the 1965 Table of General Used Chinese Characters for Publishing 《印刷通用漢字字形表》 where Xin Zixing (新字形#新舊字形對照表) is promulgated for the first time.
entries.兼: Compound ideogram: Hand 又 (as in 肀) holding two grain stalks 禾. Compare: 秉, a hand holding one plant.
entries.冂:
According to Shuowen Jiezi, pictogram composed by three lines that represent a territory outside the city walls and its nearby villages and green fields, a territory that belongs to the uncontaminated countryside, distant from every kind of civilization.

As an alternative, it's the original form of 堂, hence it's the profile of a building. The reversed character is 凵.
entries.冃:
Pictogram: a hat — original form of 帽, in which it appears as ⺜.

See also 敖, 免, and 美. See also the inner component of 蒙.
entries.内: Simplified from 內. Compound ideogram: 入 (to enter, semantic) + 冂 (house, semantic). It originally conveyed the meaning of "to bring into the house," and by extension, came to mean "inside" or "within."
entries.冉: Pictogram – uncertain. Possibly depicts hair hanging down (the original form of 髯) or the edge of a turtle shell (the original form of 𪚮).
entries.冊: Pictogram – bamboo slips strung together. See also 侖, 扁, and 典. Similar but unrelated to 龠. The contemporary stylized form 册 is unrelated to 朋.
entries.冋: An ancient variant of 冂, with a mouth 口 inside the character. Compare 向 and its derivative 尚. Unrelated to 高.
entries.冎:
Pictogram: bones. Original form of 骨.

It also appears as the top component of 咼, which has a distinguishing 口 added. See also its variant 另 and the top component of the simplified character 呙 (< 咼).
entries.冏: Perhaps a hut (stylized as 穴) with a mouth in the middle (口) to indicate an opening, hence a window.
entries.冒:
Phono-semantic compound: 冃 (hat, phonetic) + 目 (eyes, semantic). 冃 is the original form, 目 was added later. Original form of 帽.

See also 敖, 免, and 美.
entries.冓:
Compound ideogram – two fish (魚) with their mouths facing each other – original script of 遘.

The erroneous interpretation of "crossly accumulated woods" given in Shuowen is a result of the corruption of the form of the character after Western Zhou.
entries.冖: A cloth used to cover something. Unrelated to 写 (< 寫), 愛, 亭, 亮, 高, and 學.
entries.冗: Compound ideogram: 宀 (roof) + 儿 (person) — a person at home without work to do.
entries.冘: Pictogram – A man carrying an object on their shoulder. The original form of 儋. It should also be noted that the oracle bone character may be interpreted as 何. (Ji Xusheng, 2004)
entries.写: From cursive script (East Asia) of 寫.
entries.冞: Han compound: Kangxi radical 冖 (lid) + phonetic component 米.
entries.冟: Compound ideogram: 冖 (cover, phonetic) + 皀 (container of rice, semantic).
entries.冠:
Phono-semantic compound: 冖 (hat, semantic) + 元 (head, phonetic) + 寸 (hand, semantic) – a hand putting a hat on the head.

Earlier forms are Phono-semantic compound: 冃 (hat, semantic) + 元 (phonetic).
entries.冡: Compound ideogram: 𠔼 + 豕, a pig under either a roof or a hat. Similar to 家 (in which however the male pig acts as a phonetic component).
entries.冢: Phono-semantic compound: 勹 (wrap, semantic) + 豖 (phonetic) – wrapped in a burial shroud. Top component now simplified to 冖.
entries.冣: Phono-semantic compound: 冖 (cover, semantic) + 取 (phonetic).
entries.冥:
Originally Compound ideogram: 冖 (cloth cover) + 日 (sun) + 廾 (two hands) – "dark". The upper part of the character is 𠕾. The 廾 was later corrupted to 六.

May also be a Phono-semantic compound: 冖 (phonetic) + 日 (semantic) + 廾 (semantic) (Shuowen Jiezi).
entries.冪:
Simplified from 幎.

Originally written as 幎: Phono-semantic compound: 巾 (cloth, semantic) + 冥 (phonetic). Xu Shen indicates that the character 幎 meant 幔.

Later the 六 was corrupted to 大 and the 巾 was written under the character, giving rise to 幂.

艹 was added to form a new Phono-semantic compound: 巾 (cloth, semantic) + 幕 (phonetic). Alternatively, may also be analyzed as Compound ideogram: 冖 (cover, phonetic) + 幕 (cover; tent, semantic).
entries.冫: Radical form of 仌, in which the two blocks of ice appear compressed and stylized. Unrelated to 氵, 次, and 准.
entries.冬:
Unclear. One hypothesis derives 冬 from the antenna-like upper part of an oracle-bone graph formerly read as 鼉 (“crocodilian”) (e.g. Jiaguwen Heji 6163反, 7405反), but reinterpreted as 螽 (“katydid; locust”).

The word may be related to 統(“thread-end; leading strand of silk”) and 終.
entries.冰:
Phono-semantic compound: 仌 (phonetic) + 水 (semantic). 冫 is the original pictogram for this character, a semantic 水 was added later.

The above vulgar character in Shuowen Jiezi is 凝.
entries.冲:
An unorthodox variant Simplified from 沖. that can be found in various historical dictionaries such as the Kangxi dictionary. 

Eventually adopted as an official character by the People's Republic of China.
entries.冶:
Compound ideogram: 呂 (metal ingots) + 刀 (ladle) + 口 (a decorative component) — to cast metal.

The ingots have simplified into 冫 (compare 金 where they appear as 丷) and the 刀 and 口 have combined together, forming the phonetic component 台.
entries.冷: Phono-semantic compound: 仌 (ice, semantic) + 令 (phonetic) – cold as ice.
entries.冽: Phono-semantic compound: 仌 (ice, semantic) + 列 (phonetic).
entries.凄: Phono-semantic compound: 仌 (ice, semantic) + 妻 (phonetic).
entries.凊: Phono-semantic compound: 仌 (ice, semantic) + 青 (phonetic).
entries.凌: Phono-semantic compound: 仌 (ice, semantic) + 夌 (phonetic).
entries.凓: Phono-semantic compound: 仌 (ice, semantic) + 栗 (phonetic).
entries.凔: Phono-semantic compound: 仌 (ice, semantic) + 倉 (phonetic).
entries.凘: Phono-semantic compound: 仌 (ice, semantic) + 斯 (phonetic).
entries.凝: Phono-semantic compound: 仌 (ice, semantic) + 疑 (phonetic)
entries.凞: Found in various historical dictionaries such as 《四聲篇海》 (Jin dynasty (1115–1234)), 《篇海類篇》 and 《重訂直音篇》 (Ming dynasty) and 《字彙補》 (Qing dynasty).
entries.几:
Pictogram – a small stool viewed from the side. The original version was 𠀃, in which the horizontal stroke at the bottom represents the floor and/or the ground.

See also the bottom component of 其, 真, and 典, in which 八 is the stylization of the legs of a table.

Unrelated to 鉛, in which the top component is a stylization of 八, representing stagnant water. Also unrelated to 朵, 凡, and 殳.
entries.凡: Pictogram – origin unknown. It consists of two vertical strokes of unequal length. In oracle bone script, it was primarily used as a phonetic component in 鳳. In some oracle bone forms of 鳳, this component is written resembling 戌.
entries.凨:
Found in a Movable type#Metal movable type in China printing of the 《通俗小說》 novel. First attested in 《宋元以來俗字譜》, a Variant Chinese character dictionary compiled in 1930 that records unorthodox forms (俗字) that have existed since the Song dynasty.

Also part of the 324 simplified characters introduced by the Republic of China (Kuomintang government) in 1935 but was later retracted in 1936.
entries.凰: Originally 皇. A spurious 𠘨 was added by the assimilation with 鳳.
entries.凳: Phono-semantic compound: 登 (phonetic) + 几 (table; stool, semantic).
entries.凶: Pictogram – and/or Ideogram –- with the '凵' component representing a hole in the ground and with the '㐅' component (if an ideogram) indicating the existence of a hole and/or (if a pictogram) representing rock, mud, stone or bamboo in the hole. Alternately, could be derived from the upper component of '㚇'.
entries.凷: Compound ideogram: 土 (earth) + 凵 (pit) – a clod of dirt.
entries.出:
Compound ideogram: 止 (foot) + 凵 (cave) – to step out of a cave; to exit. Compare 各.

By the Qin dynasty, the character has lost its original shape. Based on the distorted form, Shuowen mistakenly interprets the character as a pictogram of a plant (屮) growing outwards.
entries.函: Originally 圅, a Pictogram – an upside-down arrow stored inside a box with one or two handles.
entries.刀: Pictogram – a knife. The original form was 𠚣, which can be found in a variant of 利, 𥝢 (in turn used on the top of the character 黎).
entries.刃: Ideogram: a 刀 with an emphasis mark on the blade.
entries.刅: Pictogram: a blade cutting thorns, a process that easily results in injury. Original form of 創.
entries.分: Compound ideogram: 八 (to separate) + 刀 (knife) – to separate with a knife.
entries.切: Phono-semantic compound: 七 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.刊: Phono-semantic compound: 干 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.刎: Phono-semantic compound: 勿 (phonetic) + 刀 (semantic). 勿 originally referred to this word, 刀 was added later.
entries.刑: Phono-semantic compound: 井 (phonetic) + 刀 (semantic). Originally written as 㓝, the 井 later corrupted into 幵, forming 𠛬.
entries.列:
Compound ideogram: 歹 (skeletal remains) + 刀 (knife) – to tear apart.

The seal script form can be analyzed as a Phono-semantic compound: 𡿪 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.初:
Compound ideogram: 衣 (clothes) + 刀 (knife; to cut) – start making clothes by cutting the cloth.

The various 𢀰-shaped glyphs are or are evolved from Zetian characters.
entries.刣:
Simplified from 胎.

Phono-semantic compound: 台 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.判: Phono-semantic compound: 半 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.別: Compound ideogram: 冎 (bone) + 刀 (knife), hence 𠛰 – to cut up bone and flesh. Later, the character was stylized as 別. See also 另.
entries.刨: Phono-semantic compound: 包 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.利: Compound ideogram: 禾 (grain) + 刀 (knife) – to reap grain (禾) with a knife (刀). See also the variant 𥝢, which appears on top of the character 黎.
entries.刪:
Simplified from 删.

Compound ideogram: 冊 (bamboo slips strung together) + 刀 (knife).
entries.别:
Variant of 別, where 𠮠 is replaced with the visually-similar 另.

Officially adopted as the simplified form of 彆 in the Chinese Character Simplification Scheme (s:漢字簡化方案) in 1956.
entries.到: Phono-semantic compound: 至 (to arrive, semantic) + 刀 (phonetic).
entries.制: Compound ideogram: 朱 (tree) + 刀 (knife) – to cut a tree.
entries.刷: Phono-semantic compound: 刀 (knife, semantic) + 㕞 (phonetic).
entries.券: Phono-semantic compound: 𠔉 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic) – contract. Ancient contracts were cut in half.
entries.刺: Phono-semantic compound: 朿 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.剄: Phono-semantic compound: 巠 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic)
entries.剅: Phono-semantic compound: 豆 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.則:
Compound ideogram: 鼎 (ding, a bronze cauldron for cooking or sacrificial rituals) + 刀 (knife); hence, the original version is 𠟭. Perhaps it's a reference to carving something (e.g., characters) with a knife on a bronze. Its original meaning was "rule; law".

鼎 was simplified to the unrelated 貝 in the small seal script. Compare 貞 (< 鼑), which underwent the same stylization.
entries.剌:
Originally an Compound ideogram: 禾 (cereal) + 口 + 刀 (knife, blade), meaning "to cut the cereal plants, to harvest" (Ji Xusheng 季旭昇); the original shape is linked to the character 𥞥.

On bronze inscriptions, the character was stylized into 柬 + 刀 and the original meaning evolved.
entries.前:
Originally 歬, an Compound ideogram: 止 (foot) + 舟 (boat) – a foot on a boat moving forward.

In the current form, 止 is simplified to 䒑 and 舟 to 月. The current form with an additional 刀 (𠝣 > 𣦃 > 前) is the original form of 剪.

Unrelated to 俞.
entries.剐: Unorthodox variant of 剮. Simplified from 剮.
entries.剔: Phono-semantic compound: 易 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.剖: Phono-semantic compound: 刀 (knife, semantic) + 咅 (phonetic). It expresses the idea of cutting something in two with a knife.
entries.剚: Phono-semantic compound: 事 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife; sword, semantic).
entries.剛: A Phono-semantic compound: semantic 山 and phonetic 刚, an oracle bone script form of 网 and 刀 (not the simplified form of 剛).
entries.剝: Phono-semantic compound: 彔 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.剠: Phono-semantic compound: 京 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.剡: Phono-semantic compound: 炎 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.剪: Originally 𣦃 and then stylized into 前, a Phono-semantic compound: 歬 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic). Since 前 has replaced 歬, an additional 刀 has been added.
entries.剬: Phono-semantic compound: 耑 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.剮: Phono-semantic compound: 咼 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.副: Phono-semantic compound: 畐 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.剴: Phono-semantic compound: 豈 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.創: Phono-semantic compound: 倉 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic) – wound.
entries.剺: Originally 刕. Phono-semantic compound: 𠩺 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.剼: Phono-semantic compound: 參 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.剾: Phono-semantic compound: 區 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic)
entries.剿: Phono-semantic compound: 巢 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic). Originally 劋.
entries.劁: Phono-semantic compound: 焦 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.劃: Phono-semantic compound: 畫 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.劄:
Phono-semantic compound: 答 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife; blade, semantic).

Note that historical dictionaries such as Yupian 《玉篇》 (543 AD) and Jiyun 《集韻》 (1039 AD) that predated the Kangxi dictionary (published 1716 AD) used this form.
entries.劆:
Found in the historical Jiyun 《集韻》 dictionary published during the Song dynasty (1037 AD).

Phono-semantic compound: 廉 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife; blade, semantic).
entries.劇: Phono-semantic compound: 豦 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.劈: Phono-semantic compound: 辟 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.劉:
Phono-semantic compound: 卯 (phonetic) + 金 (metal, semantic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).

Often written as 卯 in the oracle bone script.
entries.劋: Phono-semantic compound: 喿 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.劓: Compound ideogram: 鼻 (nose) + 刀 (knife) – to cut off the nose.
entries.劗: Phono-semantic compound: 贊 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.劙: Phono-semantic compound: 蠡 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.力: Pictogram – alternative interpretation, either an arm bending out from the side of the body, or a wooden plough.
entries.功: Phono-semantic compound: 工 (labour; work, phonetic) + 力 (strength, semantic).
entries.加:
Shuowen: Compound ideogram: 力 (strength) + 口 (mouth) — exaggerate; slander. 

Sun Changxu: Compound ideogram: 力 (plowing) + 口 (mouth) — to put more effort. 口 here indicates exclamations or breath associated with the effort.
entries.劣: Compound ideogram: 少 (little, less) + 力 (strength).
entries.劥: Phono-semantic compound: 亢 (phonetic) + 力 (strength, semantic).
entries.劦:
Compound ideogram: three 力 – to plough together; to cooperate.

力 (plough).
entries.助: Phono-semantic compound: 且 (phonetic) + 力 (strong arm, semantic) – to help with one’s strength.
entries.努: Phono-semantic compound: 力 (strength, semantic) + 奴 (phonetic) – exert one’s strength.
entries.劫: Phono-semantic compound: 去 (phonetic) + 力 (power, force, semantic)
entries.劾: Phono-semantic compound: 亥 (phonetic) + 力 (power, semantic).
entries.勁: Phono-semantic compound: 巠 (phonetic) + 力 (strength, semantic).
entries.勃: Phono-semantic compound: 孛 (phonetic) + 力 (power, semantic).
entries.勇: Phono-semantic compound: 甬 (phonetic) + 力 (strong, semantic) – brave and strong.
entries.勉: Phono-semantic compound: 免 (phonetic) + 力 (strong, semantic) – make a strong effort.
entries.勒: Phono-semantic compound: 革 (semantic) + 力 (phonetic). Bridles are made of leather.
entries.動: Phono-semantic compound: 重 (phonetic) + 力 (strength, semantic). However, the phonetic component is a reference to a heavy bag ready to be moved by a human being.
entries.勘: Phono-semantic compound: 力 (strong, semantic) + 甚 (phonetic) – to look at carefully, strongly.
entries.務: Phono-semantic compound: 敄 (phonetic) + 力 (strength, semantic).
entries.勝:
Phono-semantic compound: 朕 (phonetic) + 力 (strength, semantic).

Graphically, the character decomposes as 月 + 劵 (which gives rise to the simplified form 胜), though this is not the etymology.
entries.募: Phono-semantic compound: 莫 (phonetic) + 力 (strength, semantic).
entries.勠: Phono-semantic compound: 翏 (phonetic) + 力 (strength, semantic).
entries.勢: Phono-semantic compound: 埶 (phonetic) + 力 (power, semantic).
entries.勦: Phono-semantic compound: 巢 (phonetic) + 力 (power, semantic).
entries.勶: Phono-semantic compound: 徹 (phonetic) + 力 (force, semantic).
entries.勷: Phono-semantic compound: 襄 (phonetic) + 力 (power, semantic).
entries.勸: Phono-semantic compound: 雚 (phonetic) + 力 (strength, semantic).
entries.勹: Pictogram: a person bending over. Compare with 人 and 尸. In 包, it represents the placenta around a fetus 巳.
entries.勺: Ideogram: wine (丶) in the ladle or spoon (勹).
entries.勻:
Simplified from 匀.

Phono-semantic compound: 螾 (phonetic) + 呂 (two gold plates, semantic) – a unit of weight, original form of 鈞. The phonetic component is an ancient form of 螾 (see 旬), now written 勹. The component 呂 has corrupted into 二.
entries.勾: Variant of 句, via 口 → 厶.
entries.勿:
Pictogram – blood on a knife; the original character of 刎. Later Phonetic loan – for 勿 since the time of the oracle bone script.

Unrelated to the right component of a variant of 利, 𥝢, in turn used on top of the character 黎. Also unrelated to 匆.
entries.匂: Kokuji (created in Japan). Glyph origin unknown.
entries.匄: Original form of 丐 and 匃. It represents the tip of a blade 亡 inside the character that represents a knife 刀. Its original meaning is not fully clear; perhaps it was "damage".
entries.包: Pictogram – a fetus (巳) in the womb (勹), or a swaddled baby. Shuowen gives both interpretations.
entries.匆:
The original form is 悤, reinterpreted as a Phono-semantic compound: 囪 (phonetic) + 心 (semantic).

The bottom left part of top component 囪 was omitted, arriving at the variant 怱. Later, the semantic component 心 was also omitted, arriving at 匆.

Unrelated to 勿.
entries.匈: Phono-semantic compound: 勹 (semantic) + 凶 (phonetic). The derivative 胸 refers to the original word.
entries.匋: Phono-semantic compound: 勹 (person bending over, phonetic) + 缶 (clay pot, semantic) – "to make pottery; pottery". Perhaps the original character of 陶.
entries.匕: Pictogram – a spoon. Unrelated to 老, in which it represents a walking cane. Also unrelated to the top component of 眞, in which it represents a knife or dagger. Unrelated to 比, in which represents a person.
entries.化:
Compound ideogram – of two 人, one upright (亻) and one upside down (𠤎) — reversal; change. Shuowen also considers 𠤎 to be a phonetic component.

Compare 并, 比, 卬, 尼 and 北.
entries.北:
Compound ideogram – two men back to back. Originally meaning “back”; the character 背 refers to the original word.

Compare 化, 比, 卬, and 尼.
entries.匙: Phono-semantic compound: 是 (phonetic) + 匕 (spoon, semantic).
entries.匜: Phono-semantic compound: 匚 (container, semantic) + 也 (phonetic).
entries.匝: A geometrical variant of 迊 from its Cursive script (East Asia) written form.
entries.匠:
Traditionally thought to be an Compound ideogram: 匚 (box) + 斤 (axe) (e.g. Shuowen).

In more recent scholarship (e.g.;), an alternative glyph origin has been proposed, suggesting that it is a Phono-semantic compound: 匚 (phonetic) + 斤 (axe, semantic).
entries.匡: Pictogram of a square-shaped bamboo basket (perhaps originally made to contain millet and rice); the inner component is 㞷, which today retains only the bottom component 王 as a phonetic element. The inner component The original form is 匩 and the original meaning is preserved in 筐.
entries.匪: Phono-semantic compound: 匚 (box, semantic) + 非 (phonetic)
entries.匱: Phono-semantic compound: 匚 (cabinet, semantic) + 貴 (valuables, phonetic).
entries.匳: Phono-semantic compound: 匚 (container, semantic) + 僉 (phonetic).
entries.匸: A graphic sign 𠃊 to symbolize something that hides something or someone.
entries.医: Compound ideogram: 匸 (that which hides; that which stores) + 矢 (arrow).
entries.匽: Phono-semantic compound: 匸 (hiding enclosure, semantic) + 妟 (phonetic).
entries.匿: Phono-semantic compound: 匸 (to conceal, semantic) + 若 (phonetic).
entries.十:
In oracle-bone script, 十 is mostly written as a single vertical stroke; a few examples add a central dot, as in HJ 9204. Later forms added 一, making a cross.

One view identifies it as the original graph of 針, later borrowed for 十. See 針.

Another view sees it as a knotted-cord or thread-joining form, cf. 什 (三蒼 glosses it as “to gather”), 揖 (the 詩 commentary glosses 揖揖 as “gathered”), 緝 (“to join hemp fibres into thread”), and 輯 (glossed in 說文 as “to collect” and in 爾雅 as “to harmonize”).

For the sense of number ten (10), Ideogram – is identified: a vertical stroke, indicating the next digit above one.

Unrelated to 支, 卖, 直, 真, 德, 甫, and 七, but related to the original form of 丈.
entries.卂: Ideogram – derived from 飛 ("a bird flying") or depicting a person with their hands behind their back ("a prisoner of war").
entries.千:
Phono-semantic compound: 一 (one, signifying a number, semantic) + 人 (phonetic). The Old Chinese pronunciations of 千 and 人 were similar. For the component 人, compare its combining form 亻.

The traditional explanation holds that the extra line indicates an extension (see the etymologies of 年 and 延). 千 has the meaning one thousand because one thousand is a number that is reached by extending one's counting.
entries.卅: 十, repeated three times. See also 廿.
entries.卆: Unorthodox variant of 卒. Compare 雑 from 雜.
entries.升: Pictogram – of a dipper, compare 斗.
entries.午: Pictogram – a pestle (now written 杵). Unrelated to 干. See the central component of 舂 and 秦 in their original version.
entries.半: Compound ideogram: 八 (to divide) + 牛 (cow) – to cut a cow into two halves.
entries.华:
Phono-semantic compound: 化 (phonetic) + 十 (stalk and leaves, semantic). The top component in 華 has been simplified to a phonetic element 化.

This character first appeared in the 1956 Chinese Character Simplification Scheme by the People's Republic of China and is not known to have existed prior to that.
entries.卑: Compound ideogram: 甲 (fan) + 𠂇 (hand) - a man holding a fan, indicating that he is a servant.
entries.卓:
Compound ideogram – of a child (子) with a type of flag (ㅏ) on their head. (Ji Xusheng, 2004).

According to Zhang Shichao (張世超), the character represents a man (ㅏ) standing in a higher position on an altar illuminated by the sun (昜).

An ancient variant of the character is 㔬. The child (or the altar) is now written in a way similar to 早 in the modern script.
entries.協: Phono-semantic compound: 十 (phonetic) + 劦 (to collaborate, phonetic) — a variant form of 劦 with a phonetic 十 added.
entries.南:
Phonetic loan: The oracle-bone form depicts a lidded 同. Some forms contain strokes inside the vessel, probably representing its contents. In Western Zhou bronze inscriptions, the 同 element changed into 用. One proposal identifies this graph as the original character of 醓 (“meat sauce; minced meat preserved in brine”).

南 may be related to 腩 and 納 (“to put in; to receive”).
entries.単: Simplified from 單. Compare 厳 (from 嚴).
entries.博: Phono-semantic compound: 十 (ten, semantic) + 尃 (phonetic).
entries.卜:
Perhaps a Pictogram – of a crack in an oracle bone, used for divination in ancient China.

Officially adopted as the simplified form of 蔔 in the Chinese Character Simplification Scheme (s:漢字簡化方案) in 1956.
entries.卡: Compound ideogram: 上 (up) + 下 (down) with fusion of the horizontal lines, representing being squeezed between above and below.
entries.卢: Simplified form of 盧 from the cursive script (East Asia).
entries.卦: Phono-semantic compound: 圭 (phonetic) + 卜 (semantic). However, the phonetic component has a reference to a ritual since it represents a pair of ritual axes perhaps made of jade.
entries.卩: Pictogram: a kneeling person from sideview. Similar but unrelated to 欠, in which the person kneeling has the mouth open, and 女, in which the kneeling figure is a woman. See also 即. Unrelated to 报.
entries.卫:
This character is not known to have existed prior to the simplification of Chinese characters by the People's Republic of China in 1956.

The simplification of 衛 to 卫 may have been influenced by the Japanese katakana ヱ, compare the Japanese ryakuji ⿰彳ヱ.

In Zhongwen Da Cidian 《中文大辭典》, a dictionary based on the Japanese Dai Kan-Wa Jiten and published in Taiwan from 1962 to 1968, 𠀄, a character which is visually similar to 卫 (乛 on top instead of 𠃌), is recorded as an unorthodox variant of 衛. 

Another theory is that 卫 is a variant of 𫝀, which is the top component of 韋 in the middle of 衛.
entries.卬: Compound ideogram: 匕 + 卩: a man standing and a man kneeling; compare 化, 比, 北 and 尼.
entries.卯:
Origin uncertain. In oracle bone scripts, it refers to a sacrificial method of halving a victim, read as 劉.

Alternatively, it depicts two matching plate-like shapes fitting together—acting as the original ideogram for 侔, which later extended to mean 貿.

Traditionally interpreted in Shuowen as an opened door (the reverse of 門), or in folk etymology as a mortise in woodworking. An older variant is 戼.
entries.印:
Compound ideogram: 爪 (hand) + 卩 (kneeling person) – a hand suppressing a kneeling person.

According to 羅振玉 in his book 《增訂殷墟書契考釋》(1915), the character is an ideogram of a hand suppressing a kneeling person. The character 抑 (to suppress) was used to preserve the original meaning.
entries.危:
Compound ideogram: 厃 (person on a cliff or mountain) + 卩 (kneeling person).

Written like 𡴲 during the Warring States period, an Compound ideogram: 人 (person) + 山 (mountain).
entries.即: Compound ideogram: 皀 (ancient round-mouthed food vessel) + 卩 (to kneel) – to come near to eat; to approach.
entries.却: Variant of 卻*. The modern mainland China usage is of reform nature.
entries.卷:
Simplified from 拳.

Phono-semantic compound: 𢍏 (phonetic) + 卩 (kneeling person, semantic) - to bend; reel of books. The phonetic component could also add part of the meaning since it indicates the act of rolling rice into balls, hence "bending" rice. Two rather conservative variants are 𨤖 and 𠨟, in which rice is visible on top.

Now written as Phono-semantic compound: 龹 (phonetic) + 卩 (kneeling person, semantic). Similar but unrelated to 春 and 秦.
entries.卸: Omission of 彳 in 御. 午 still gives the sound.
entries.卿: Compound ideogram: 𠨍 (two men facing each other, semantic) + 皀 (food vessel with a stand, phonetic) – people engaged in ritual feasting. The character was once indistinguishable from 鄉; see the Glyph origin section there for more.
entries.厄:
Possibly an of a person kneeling (卩), and a small stroke to accentuate the knee (now 厂). Not cognate with 戹 (“yoke”) but eventually they shared meanings. 

Shuowen Jiezi interprets it as Phono-semantic compound: 厂 (phonetic) + 卪 (joint; node, semantic) – Wood#Knots.
entries.历: Simplified from 歷. by keeping the character's basic structure but replacing the components under 厂 with phonetic 力.
entries.厓:
Phono-semantic compound: 厂 (cliff, semantic) + 圭 (phonetic) to represent a cliff and the waterside.

Originally, the phonetic component is not related to the concept of earth (土) since in its original form it represents a pair of ritual axes perhaps made of jade 士. Hence, the link to the concept of earth in this character and 街 either comes from folk etymology or its appearance in the Small Seal script.
entries.厖: Phono-semantic compound: 厂 (cliff, semantic) + 尨 (phonetic).
entries.厘: Variant of 釐 by omitting the top part of it.
entries.厚: Compound ideogram: 厂 (cliff; cave on a cliff) + 𣆪 (jug). According to Shuowen, 𣆪 is an inverted 亯.
entries.厛:
Found in a Movable type#Metal movable type in China printing of the 《通俗小說》 novel. First attested in 《宋元以來俗字譜》, a Variant Chinese character dictionary compiled in 1930 that records unorthodox forms (俗字) that have existed since the Song dynasty.

Also part of the 324 simplified characters introduced by the Republic of China (Kuomintang government) in 1935 but was later retracted in 1936.
entries.原: Compound ideogram: 泉 (spring) + 厂 (cliff) – a spring bursting from a cliff-side – origin. A conservative variant is 厡, in which water is well visible at the bottom.
entries.厡: Ideogram – a spring 泉 bursting from a cliff-side 厂.
entries.厤: Phono-semantic compound: 厂 (semantic) + 秝 (phonetic). Also recorded as an ancient form of 曆* in the Kangxi dictionary in 1716 AD.
entries.厴: Phono-semantic compound: 厭 (phonetic) + 甲 (shell, semantic).
entries.厷:
Simplified from 宏.

Pictogram: a hand, an arm and a rounded part that represents either a shoulder or an elbow — original form of 肱.

Today the arm is not visible anymore, the hand is stylized as a left hand, and a semi-open shape 厶 at the bottom represents either the shoulder or elbow.
entries.去:
Compound ideogram: 大 (man) + 口 (mouth, object). Top figure simplified to 土, unrelated to 士, while bottom simplified to 厶; a conservative variant is 厺.

There are various interpretations of the combination of “man” and “mouth, object”. One is that the ideograph represented a man with a hole marked in his crotch, with the idea of “anus” (i.e. getting rid of). Another is that it represented a man departing from a cave or city.

Alternatively, it may be the original character of 呿, the meaning given by the combination of 大 and 口. The meaning “to depart” would be an extension of the meaning “to open one's mouth”, as the lips depart from each other when one's mouth is open.

Shuowen Jiezi interprets the character as a Phono-semantic compound: 大 (man, semantic) + 𠙴 (phonetic).

In addition, 去 is also the original character of 盍. The 大 could be a cover on top of an object 口.

The man on top is simplified as 土 as in 赤 and 走 (< 𧺆).
entries.厾: Semantic 去 + an abstract swoosh of throwing; referring to the "to throw" sense. Also compare 丟 (Yin, 2021).
entries.叀: Pictogram – a spindle. The original form of 專 and 惠.
entries.参: Simplified from 參., which is in turn Simplified from 曑.
entries.參:
Simplified from 曑.

The bronze script form is an Compound ideogram: 晶 (stars) + 光 (light; brightness) + 彡 (light rays) – Three Stars (Chinese constellation) mansion. 彡 also acts as a phonetic component. Ignoring the lines connecting the three stars, 光 may be interpreted as 卩, representing someone looking at the shining stars above him.

Alternatively, it may be the original character of 簪, since the bronze script forms resemble a person wearing a hat with three stars.

Based on the seal script form, Shuowen interprets the character as a Phono-semantic compound: 晶 (stars, semantic) + 㐱 (phonetic). However, according to the original form, this character is unrelated to 㐱.
entries.又:
Pictogram – a right hand. Original form of 右. Unrelated to 𠬤 (> 译).

Often written as ⺕ in many modern characters such as 事, 聿, 雪, 急, 爭, 尹, and 建 (which is unrelated to 聿).
entries.及: Compound ideogram: 人 (person) + 又 (hand) – a hand grabbing a person.
entries.友:
Phono-semantic compound: 又 (phonetic) + 又 (phonetic)

Shuowen: two hands, therefore friendship.
entries.反: Phono-semantic compound: 又 (hand, semantic) + 厂 (phonetic). The character originally depicted the action of turning the palm of the hand, and by extension, it came to mean "to return" or "to reverse."
entries.发: Simplified from 發. in the 1956 Chinese Character Simplification Scheme by the People's Republic of China.
entries.叓: Compound ideogram: 𰀉 (a flag hoisted onto a frame) + 又 (hand). Represents the work or duty assigned to a (lower) servant, who would e.g. hoist flags as part of their service, whence also the meaning “petty official”.
entries.叔:
Compound ideogram: 尗 (wooden stake, phonetic) + 又 (hand, semantic) – using a wooden stake to dig the ground. Later phonetically borrowed to mean "paternal uncle".

The whole character is partly related to 建 since it represents a hand planting a wooden stake in the ground.
entries.受: Possibly a Compound ideogram: 爪 (hand) + 舟 (boat) + 又 (hand) – to hand over.
entries.叙: Unorthodox variant Simplified from 敘. found in the Tang dynasty orthographic dictionary Ganlu Zishu (干祿字書) and eventually adopted as an official form by the People's Republic of China.
entries.叚: Compound ideogram: 爪 (hand) + 又 (hand) + 石 (stone). The stone indicates the ancient pronunciation, while the hands indicate the original concept of "borrowing". A conservative variant is 𠭊. Most of the character is identical to 段.
entries.叟:
Originally 叜. Compound ideogram: 宀 (roof; house) + 火 (fire) + 又 (hand) – hand holding a torch in the house – original form of 搜.

Since the clerical script, the top components 宀 and 火 have merged into the unrelated 𦥔.
entries.叡: Compound ideogram: 㕡 (gully) + 目 (eye) – deep insight.
entries.口:
Pictogram – resembles an open mouth.

In the oracle bone script, radical 口 is used for characters having abstract meanings. Such a character can have a figurative meaning derived from the phonetic part, e.g. 右 = 又 + 口 and 𪪺 = 弓 + 口, or be an unrelated borrowing, e.g. 否 = 不 + 口.
entries.古:
Ideogram: A shield (甲, contraction of 盾 and similar but unrelated to 中) and the radical of the mouth (口) both as a distinguishing mark and as a component that partly indicates pronunciation. Together, they indicate the concept of "strong, firm" (as strong as a shield); original form of 固 (Qiu Xigui, Ding Shan 丁山). Compare oracle bone forms with 干, 盾. Unrelated to 中 and hence to 史 and 使.

 finds evidence for the 十 component originally being a depiction of a piece of food and the character originally being a depiction of someone spitting out a piece of food due to his bad taste. Thus, Fang argues this character is the original form of 苦, "bitter".
entries.句:
Phono-semantic compound: 丩 (to entangle, semantic) + 口 (phonetic), which may represent the tip of a big nail.

The 丩 component, originally two entangled ropes, now resembles the unrelated 勹.
entries.另: In 玉篇校釋 (胡吉宣, 1989), it is considered a simplified form of 別, used to refer a synonym word with different pronunciation.
entries.叨: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 刀 (phonetic).
entries.叩: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (phonetic) + 卩 (semantic). The semantic component 卩 depicts a kneeling human.
entries.只: Pictogram: airflow coming out of a mouth (口) – a modal particle. Compare 四 and 曰.
entries.叫: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 丩 (phonetic). According to Shuowen Jiezi, its original meaning was "to shout".
entries.可: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (semantic) + 丂 (phonetic) with a reference to exhaled air. Perhaps its original meaning was "to sing", then 訶 and 哥 (可 written twice).
entries.台:
Phono-semantic compound: 㠯 (phonetic) + 口 (mouth, semantic).

An alternate variant of 㠯 (modern form: 以) in Chinese bronze inscriptions.
entries.叱: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 七 (phonetic).
entries.史:
Pictogram – 又 holding a stylized flag almost identical to 中 perhaps to indicate a representative or ambassador (see its variant 吏 used in 使 to mean "ambassador"). As an alternative, it holds either a pen or a hunting weapon resembling similar to 中. Hence, the inner component 中 is partly unclear.

The whole character originally indicates the act of taking notes; today, it means "history". Compare 事.
entries.右: Phono-semantic compound: 又 (phonetic) + 口 (semantic). Originally written as 又 as a phonetic loan in the oracle bone script; in bronze inscriptions, a meaningless 口 component was added as a distinguishing mark.
entries.号: Compound ideogram: 口 (mouth) + 丂 (exhaled air; a tiger's cry). See 號 for more details.
entries.司:
Inconclusive.

Jì Xùshēng: Compound ideogram – a mouth 口 giving orders and a scepter 刁 of authority. 

Liú Xìnglóng interprets 刁 to be a hand instead. 

Táng Lán: Originally the same character as 后, which later diverged.

Shuowen: 后 flipped.
entries.叻: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth; colloquial, semantic) + 力 (phonetic).
entries.吁: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 于 (phonetic).
entries.吃:
Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 乞 (phonetic) – "to stutter".

The phonetic component could add part of the meaning since it has the phonetically borrowed meaning of "begging" (i.e., trying to talk but with difficulties).

According to folk etymologies, 乞 in this character indicates that, while stuttering, less air comes from the mouth (compare 气, which has more trails). However, this is incorrect. 乞 is simply a variant of 气, originally meaning "air" and later borrowed to indicate "begging". The sense of eat may originally have been written 喫.
entries.各: Compound ideogram: 夂 (sole of foot) + 口 – to come, to enter; original form of 𢓜 and 格. The mouth could be referred to the entrance of a cavern or building (see 高, 去 and 谷; however, this is not the case in 向). Compare 出.
entries.吅: Compound ideogram: 口 + 口. Unrelated to 雚.
entries.合: Compound ideogram: 亼 + 口 (mouth): Two mouths speaking together. See also 會.
entries.吉: Compound ideogram – originally 圭 and 口 in the oracle bone script. The top component mutated into 士 in Western Zhou bronze inscriptions.
entries.同: Pictogram: a pipe — original form of 筒.
entries.名:
Compound ideogram: 夕 (crescent moon) + 口 (mouth) — to say one's own name to identify oneself in the dark.

An alternative theory has been proposed based on Shang era texts. 口 was originally used to write both 口 and 名. 夕 standing for what later came to be written 明, was added as a phonetic indicator to disambiguate the two meanings.
entries.吏:
Alternative descendant of 叓, which is the ancient form of 事. Furthermore, both characters are related to 史, which was born as a variant without the horizontal stroke on top.

The character should represent a hand holding a flag to mean "representative, ambassador"; see 使.
entries.吐: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 土 (phonetic).
entries.向: Compound ideogram: 宀 (house) + 口 (mouth), echos in a place. The original form of 響. It was borrowed to represent 𠨍 (嚮) later. The mouth does not represent an opening as in 高 and 谷. Compare 冋.
entries.吒: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 乇 (phonetic).
entries.吖: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 丫 (phonetic).
entries.君: Phono-semantic compound: 尹 (phonetic) + 口 (semantic). In the oracle bones and early Zhou bronze inscriptions, 君 was often interchanged with 尹. Shuowen suggests that 口 represents commands, but it may simply be decorative.
entries.吠: Compound ideogram: 口 (mouth) + 犬 (dog) – to bark.
entries.否: Phono-semantic compound: 不 (not, phonetic) + 口 (mouth, semantic). Similar to 咅.
entries.吧: Phono-semantic compound (形聲): semantic 口 + phonetic 巴 (OC *praː).
entries.吪: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 化 (phonetic).
entries.含: Phono-semantic compound: 今 (phonetic) + 口 (mouth, semantic).
entries.吭: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 亢 (phonetic)
entries.吱: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 支 (phonetic).
entries.吳: Compound ideogram: 口 (mouth) + 夨 (man with tilted head) – to speak loudly.
entries.吸: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 及 (phonetic) – to inhale through the mouth. Note that 及 originally derives from “grab”, hence connotations of “grab through the mouth, inhale”.
entries.吹: Compound ideogram: 口 (mouth) + 欠 (blow) according to oracle bones and bronzes. An archaic variant of this character is 龡.
entries.吼: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 孔 (phonetic).
entries.吾: Phono-semantic compound: 五 (phonetic) + 口 (mouth, semantic).
entries.呃: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 厄 (phonetic).
entries.呈: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (semantic) + 𡈼 (phonetic). The bottom component is not to be confused with 壬 or 王.
entries.呉:
Variant of 吳.

The modern Japanese usage is of reform (shinjitai) nature.
entries.呔: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth; speech, semantic) + 太 (phonetic).
entries.呢: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 尼 (phonetic)
entries.呧: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 氐 (phonetic)
entries.周:
Oracle bone script: Pictogram: a jade artifact with carved patterns. Original form of 彫. The character was later borrowed as a country name and 口 was added as a distinguishing mark. A semi-conservative version in which the carvings are visible is 𠕛. The top part of the character gradually became similar to 用 in the late Western Zhou period. See also 黃, which could have a reference to a jade artifact.

Folk etymology interprets the seal script form as 口 + 用, indicating the idea of using words skillfully to express oneself, thereby implying the meaning of being meticulous or detailed.
entries.呪: A derivative (分化): variant form of 祝 — to pray.
entries.呭: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 世 (phonetic).
entries.呲: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth; speech, semantic) + 此 (phonetic).
entries.味: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 未 (phonetic).
entries.呷: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 甲 (phonetic).
entries.呼: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 乎 (phonetic) – to exhale, call, or shout from the mouth.
entries.命: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 令 (phonetic). Doublet of 呤.
entries.呾: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 旦 (phonetic).
entries.咀: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (speech, semantic) + 且 (phonetic).
entries.咁: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 甘 (phonetic).
entries.咅: Phono-semantic compound: 丶 (semantic) + 否 (phonetic). The upper part of the character was corrupted into 立 and is unrelated to the contraction of 辛.
