entries.和: Phono-semantic compound: 禾 (phonetic) + 口 (mouth, semantic) – harmony. The original version was 龢, with the radical of the flute 𠎤 (> 龠) in its either archaic or contracted version perhaps to indicate the abstract concept of harmony through harmony in music.
entries.咍: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth; speech, semantic) + 台 (phonetic)
entries.咎: Originally Compound ideogram: 夊 (foot) + 人 (person). Later 口 was added, making the modern form an Compound ideogram: 各 + 人.
entries.咐: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 付 (phonetic).
entries.咒: Originally written 呪, see there for more.
entries.咕:
Considered a 後起字. Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 古 (phonetic).;“to stand someone up”

Derived from 放鴿子, from pigeon's sound.
entries.咖: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 加 (phonetic).
entries.咗: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 左 (phonetic)
entries.咢:
The same character as 噩, both ultimately derived from or identical to 喪, see there for more.

Later Compound ideogram: 吅 (to speak loudly, semantic) + 屰 (opposite, against, phonetic).
entries.咧: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth; speech, semantic) + 列 (phonetic).
entries.咨: Phono-semantic compound: 次 (phonetic) + 口 (mouth, semantic).
entries.咪: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth; speech, semantic) + 米 (phonetic).
entries.咫: Phono-semantic compound: 尺 (ruler; measuring stick, semantic) + 只 (phonetic).
entries.咯: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 各 (phonetic).
entries.咲: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 关 (to laugh, phonetic). It was the original form of 笑, meaning "to laugh." In Japan, it is used to represent the idea of flowers blooming.
entries.咸:
Compound ideogram: 戌 (ax) + 口 — to terminate. The 口 is a distinguishing mark. Later borrowed to mean "all".

Other explanations include shouting together with a spear in front of the battlefield, implying everyone; alternatively, to cut off one's head with an ax, depriving them of all they have; alternatively, to break a pot with an ax.

For etymology 2, Simplified from 鹹.
entries.咹: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 安 (phonetic)
entries.咽: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 因 (phonetic) – connected to the mouth, the throat.
entries.咿: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 伊 (phonetic).
entries.哀: Phono-semantic compound: 衣 (phonetic) + 口 (mouth, semantic).
entries.品: Compound ideogram: 口, representing various objects. Also occurs in 區.
entries.哄: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 共 (phonetic).
entries.哇:
Phono-semantic compound: 口 (semantic) + 圭 (phonetic).

Originally, the phonetic component is not related to the concept of earth (土) since in its original form it represents a pair of ritual axes perhaps made of jade 士. Hence, the link to the concept of earth in this character either comes from folk etymology or its appearance in the Small Seal script.
entries.哈: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 合 (phonetic). However the phonetic component, perhaps by chance, represents two open mouths.
entries.哎: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 艾 (phonetic).
entries.哥: Stacked form of 可, perhaps an open mouth with breath going out while talking or singing. In fact, the original meaning of 哥 and perhaps 可 was "to sing; song".
entries.哦: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth; speech, semantic) + 我 (phonetic).
entries.哧: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 赤 (phonetic).
entries.哩: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 里 (phonetic)
entries.哯: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 見 (phonetic).
entries.哲: In bronze script, written as 悊 and other variants, with no evidence of the existence of 哲 until small seal script. In 說文解字, described as a Phono-semantic compound: 折 (phonetic) + 口 (mouth, semantic).
entries.哺: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 甫 (phonetic).
entries.唁: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 言 (phonetic).
entries.唄: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 貝 (phonetic).
entries.唆: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 夋 (phonetic).
entries.唇: Phono-semantic compound: 辰 (phonetic) + 口 (mouth, semantic).
entries.唉: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 矣 (phonetic).
entries.唏: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 希 (phonetic)
entries.唐: Phono-semantic compound: 庚 (phonetic) + 口 (mouth, semantic). 口 functions as a differentiating mark (cf. 古/固), not as semantic "mouth." The graph abstracts some property — likely "hollowness" or "spatial openness" — from 庚, a pictograph of a hollow percussion/ritual instrument. Used in oracle bones for Shang king Cheng Tang.
entries.唦: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 沙 (phonetic)
entries.唧: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 即 (phonetic).
entries.唸: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 念 (to read, phonetic).
entries.啃: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 肯 (phonetic).
entries.啄: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 豖 (phonetic)
entries.啉: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 林 (phonetic).
entries.啊: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 阿 (phonetic).
entries.啚: Compound ideogram: 囗 (city boundary) + 㐭 (granary) – a granary outside city borders, hence “borderland, countryside”. Original form of 鄙.
entries.啜: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 叕 (phonetic).
entries.啞: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 亞 (phonetic).
entries.啟: Shu-ta Yang: Compound ideogram: 戶 (door) + 又 (hand) — to open a door with the hand. Later, 口 was added and 又 evolved to 攴.
entries.啡: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 非 (phonetic).
entries.啤: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth (phonetic), semantic) + 卑 (phonetic).
entries.啦: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 拉 (phonetic).
entries.啼: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 帝 (phonetic).
entries.喀: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 客 (phonetic).
entries.喃: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 南 (phonetic).
entries.善:
Originally written 譱 in bronze inscriptions, consisting of two 言 and one 羊. The 言 might have served as the phonetic component, while 羊 represented the sense "good; beautiful" (see 祥, 義). The small seal script of 善 was simplified from the bronze inscription form, consisting of one 言 below one 羊.

According to Shuowen, the form

譱 is an Compound ideogram: 誩 (to wrangle) + 羊 (sheep) – good; virtuous. This interpretation may be difficult to comprehend.
entries.喉: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 侯 (phonetic).
entries.喊: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 咸 (phonetic).
entries.喎: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 咼 (phonetic).
entries.喔: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 屋 (phonetic).
entries.喘: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 耑 (phonetic).
entries.喙: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 彖 (phonetic).
entries.喜:
Compound ideogram: 壴 (drum) + 口 (mouth).

Duplicated character: 囍.
entries.喝: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 曷 (phonetic).
entries.喦: Compound ideogram: three mouths (品) connected by lines.
entries.喩: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 兪 (phonetic).
entries.喪:
Originally Phono-semantic compound: 桑 (mulberry tree, phonetic) + 㗊 (many mouths, semantic). The number of mouths frequently varied. Sometimes 走 was included as a semantic component, and later 亡 was added as a phonetic (and also possibly semantic) component.

In the seal script became Phono-semantic compound: 哭 (cry, semantic) + 亡 (die, phonetic), from which the modern form derives.

Compare 咢 and 噩, which may be derived from or originally the same character as 喪.
entries.喫: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 契 (phonetic).
entries.單:
Pictogram – of a war or hunting weapon, a Y-shaped wooden stick with two stones attached on top. The component in the middle in some oracle bones was a huge point which represented a rope around the stick; perhaps, this weapon was used as a spear and then retrieved through this rope. Otherwise, the huge point in the middle was another stone attached to the stick. The huge point was then stylized as an horizontal trait, as 口 (the stick resembled 中) and eventually as 田. The horizontal stroke at the bottom of the character was added later.

An alternative theory suggests that it represents a net to catch animals with two weights on top, but the huge point in the middle of the character in some oracle bones may not be a web or net.

Alternatively, a cicada. The original form of 蟬
entries.喹: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 圭 (phonetic).
entries.喻: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 俞 (phonetic).
entries.喿: Compound ideogram: 品 (three mouths) + 木 (tree) – chirping of birds in a tree. Original form of 噪. Similar but unrelated to 果.
entries.嗅: Simplified from 齅.; in current form: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (semantic) + 臭 (phonetic).
entries.嗆: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 倉 (phonetic).
entries.嗎: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 馬 (phonetic).
entries.嗗: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 骨 (phonetic).
entries.嗚: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 烏 (phonetic).
entries.嗝: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 鬲 (phonetic).
entries.嗟: In Small Seal Script, a Phono-semantic compound: 言 (speech, semantic) + 差 (phonetic) (𧪘). In Regular Script, 言 became 口.
entries.嗡: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 翁 (phonetic).
entries.嗣: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 冊 (document, semantic) + 司 (phonetic). It originally referred to appointing the successor to the ruler through speech and documents, and by extension, expresses the idea of “succeeding.”
entries.嗨: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth; speech, semantic) + 海 (phonetic)
entries.嗯:
Simplified from 恩.

Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 恩 (phonetic).
entries.嗶: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 畢 (phonetic).
entries.嗺: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 崔 (phonetic).
entries.嗽: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 欶 (phonetic).
entries.嘀: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 啇 (phonetic).
entries.嘆: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 歎 (phonetic). It expresses the idea of feeling down and letting out a sigh.
entries.嘈: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 曹 (phonetic)
entries.嘎: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 戛 (phonetic).
entries.嘏: Phono-semantic compound: 古 (the past, semantic) + 叚 (phonetic).
entries.嘐: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 翏 (phonetic).
entries.嘔: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 區 (phonetic).
entries.嘕: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 焉 (phonetic).
entries.嘖: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 責 (phonetic)
entries.嘗: Phono-semantic compound: 尚 (phonetic) + 旨 (tasty, semantic).
entries.嘘:
Unorthodox variant Simplified from 噓. Found in the Jiyun 《集韻》 dictionary published during the Song dynasty (1039 AD).

Eventually adopted as an official form by the People's Republic of China in 1965 based on the Table of General Used Chinese Characters for Publishing 《印刷通用漢字字形表》 where Xin Zixing (新字形#新舊字形對照表) is promulgated for the first time.
entries.嘚: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 得 (phonetic).
entries.嘢:
Simplified from 野.

Phono-semantic compound: 口 (semantic) + 野 (phonetic).
entries.嘩: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 華 (phonetic).
entries.嘪: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 買 (phonetic)
entries.嘯: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 肅 (phonetic).
entries.嘵: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 堯 (phonetic).
entries.嘶: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 斯 (phonetic).
entries.嘻: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 喜 (phonetic).
entries.噂: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 尊 (phonetic).
entries.噇: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 童 (phonetic).
entries.噌: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 曾 (phonetic) – to scold or shout at.
entries.噓:
Simplified from 虛.

Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 虛 (phonetic) – to exhale, blow out from the mouth. Note that 虛 means empty, void, hence connotations of “empty via the mouth”.
entries.噗: Considered a 後起字. Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 菐 (phonetic).
entries.噥: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 農 (phonetic)
entries.器:
Uncertain.

The classical interpretation is an Compound ideogram: a 犬 guarding four 口. 

It might also be a phonetically borrowed character, originally meaning “to bark” (Compare 狺).

Another theory states the character is derived from 喪. (Compare 噩, 哭, 咢). Borrowed not for sound but as an Ideogram – referring to a funerary urn.
entries.噩: The same character as 咢, both ultimately derived from or identical to 喪, see there for more.
entries.噪:
Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 喿 (to chirp, phonetic).

Originally written 喿, see there for more.
entries.噬: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 筮 (phonetic).
entries.噮: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 睘 (phonetic)
entries.噴: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 賁 (phonetic)
entries.嚃: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 遝 (phonetic).
entries.嚆:
Simplified from 蒿.

Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 蒿 (phonetic).
entries.嚎:
Simplified from 豪.

Phono-semantic compound: 口 (semantic) + 豪 (phonetic).
entries.嚕: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 魯 (phonetic).
entries.嚗: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 暴 (phonetic). However, the phonetic component means "violence; sudden", hence it could add part of the meaning.
entries.嚛: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 樂 (phonetic).
entries.嚟: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 黎 (phonetic)
entries.嚡: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth; colloquial speech, semantic) + 鞋 (phonetic).
entries.嚥: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 燕 (phonetic).
entries.嚨: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 龍 (phonetic).
entries.嚳: Phono-semantic compound: 學 (phonetic) + 告 (to tell, semantic). 告 may also be a phonetic component.
entries.嚴:
Phono-semantic compound: 喦 (talkative, semantic) + 敢 (daring, phonetic) – the original script of 譀.

The meanings of “solemn” and “stern” may be a result of phonetic borrowing.
entries.嚶: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 嬰 (phonetic).
entries.嚷: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 襄 (phonetic)
entries.嚼: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 爵 (phonetic).
entries.嚿: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth; vernacular, semantic) + 舊 (phonetic).
entries.囀: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 轉 (phonetic).
entries.囂: Compound ideogram: 㗊 (four mouths; to clamor) + 頁 (head) – a clamoring crowd.
entries.囉: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 羅 (phonetic).
entries.囊: Compound ideogram – a tied bag (𣒚), with various items in it (𤕦). 𤕦 also serves as a phonetic element. There are many alternative forms. In the modern, standard form, the bottom turned into an abbreviated form of 襄, with the result that the character is a Phono-semantic compound: 㯻 (bag, semantic) + 襄 (phonetic).
entries.囍: Compound ideogram: 喜 + 喜 (happiness). 喜, the two characters representing the bride and groom.
entries.囗: Pictogram of a square-shaped enclosure. Unrelated to 口 (open mouth) and most likely unrelated to the original version of 丁 (head of a nail). Also unrelated to 因, in which it represents a carpet or mat.
entries.囙: Found in the historical Guangyun 《廣韻》 rime dictionary compiled during the Song dynasty (1007 AD).
entries.囚: Compound ideogram: 囗 (box, enclosure) + 人 (person) – an enclosed person: confinement, prisoner. Similar but unrelated to 因. Unrelated to 𥁕.
entries.囝: Compound ideogram: 囗 + 子 (child; son). Compare 囡.
entries.囟: Pictogram – fontanelle. See also 𡿺 and its simplification 㐫. Unrelated to 离.
entries.因:
Compound ideogram: 囗 (sheet) + 大 (person) – man on a mattress. Original form of 裀 or 茵.

Alternatively, possibly an Compound ideogram – of a man wearing clothing.
entries.团: Unorthodox character found in the historical Longkan Shoujian dictionary.
entries.囥: Phono-semantic compound: 囗 (enclosure, semantic) + 亢 (phonetic).
entries.囪: Pictogram – a window closed with a shutter, or something similar.
entries.囮: Phono-semantic compound: 囗 (to surround; to encircle, semantic) + 化 (phonetic)
entries.囯: Compound ideogram: 囗 (to surround) + 王 (king). Earliest attested form in regular script found in 《宋敬業造象記》 (507 AD).
entries.困: Compound ideogram: 囗 (surround) + 木 (wood). Probably the original form of 梱 and 閫.
entries.囲: Variant form. Phono-semantic compound: 囗 (surround, semantic) + 井 (phonetic).
entries.囹: Phono-semantic compound: 囗 (enclosure, semantic) + 令 (phonetic).
entries.囻: Coined during the Republican period upon 囯, replacing 王 with 民.
entries.国: Simplified from 國. Also compare 囯, an unorthodox variant of 國 that contains 王* instead of 玉*.
entries.圀: One of the Chinese characters created by Empress Wu to demonstrate her power. She was said to have disliked how the traditional form contained 或, which she interpreted as meaning "mislead" (see 惑). In this form, this character consists of 八方 (literally, ‘eight directions'; figuratively, 'all directions') within 囗 ('enclosure', representing the borders enclosing the territory of the country).
entries.圂: Pictogram – - A pig (豕) surrounded by an enclosure (囗).
entries.圄: Phono-semantic compound: 囗 (enclosure, semantic) + 吾 (phonetic).
entries.國: Phono-semantic compound: 囗 (closure, semantic) + 或 (phonetic).
entries.圍: Originally written as 韋. Now Phono-semantic compound: 囗 (enclosure, semantic) + 韋 (phonetic).
entries.圏: Unorthodox variant of 圈 with bottom component of 卷 written 己 instead of 㔾.
entries.園: Phono-semantic compound: 囗 (fence, semantic) + 袁 (phonetic).
entries.圓: Phono-semantic compound: 囗 (semantic) + 員 (phonetic). The interior 口 is 〇, which is the original ideogram for the word "circle"; 鼎 and 囗 were added later.
entries.圔: Phono-semantic compound: 囗 (closure, semantic) + 盍 (phonetic).
entries.圖:
Compound ideogram: 囗 (walled city) + 啚.

啚 is the early form of 鄙, thus meaning “territory”.
entries.圜: Phono-semantic compound: 囗 (circle, semantic) + 睘 (phonetic).
entries.圞:
Simplified from 圝.

Phono-semantic compound: 囗 (semantic) + 欒 (phonetic).
entries.土:
Pictogram 象形: a mound of earth. In oracle-bone inscriptions, it could also refer to the soil deity, serving as the original graph of 社. The mound later became narrowed or pointed at both ends, with the broad middle part developing into the horizontal stroke.

Unrelated to the top component of 夌, 走, and 周; also unrelated to the central component of 金 and the overall character 圭.
entries.圠: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 乙 (phonetic).
entries.圢: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 丁 (phonetic).
entries.圣: Unorthodox variant of 聖 found in the Ming dynasty orthographic dictionaries 《俗書刊誤》 and 《字學三正》; this character originally meant "to dig", a concept represented by a hand over a lump of earth or clay.
entries.在:
Phono-semantic compound: 才 (phonetic) + 士 (phonetic).

In the oracle bone script and some of the bronze inscriptions, 才 is phonetically borrowed to represent this word; a phonetic 士 was added later. 士 eventually corrupted into 土.
entries.圩: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 于 (phonetic). Compare 圬.
entries.圪: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth; soil, semantic) + 乞 (phonetic)
entries.圫: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 乇 (phonetic).
entries.圬: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 于 (phonetic). Compare 圩.
entries.圭: Pictogram: 士 + 士 – two ritual axes, perhaps made of jade, one on top of the other. 士. Stylized into but unrelated to 土; according to folk etymologies, it's a reduplication of the character 土.
entries.圮: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 配 (phonetic).
entries.地: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 也 (phonetic). One of the first versions of this character is 𡓬 (> 墬), in which a hill, a pig and a mound of earth are visible; visually, the upper part of the variant is 䧘.
entries.圴: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 勺 (phonetic).
entries.圵: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 上 (phonetic).
entries.圶: Phono-semantic compound: 大 (phonetic) + 土 (earth, semantic).
entries.圻: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (soil, semantic) + 斤 (phonetic).
entries.圿: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 介 (phonetic).
entries.址: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 止 (phonetic).
entries.坁: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 氏 (phonetic).
entries.坄:
Simplified from 殳.

Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 殳 (phonetic).
entries.均: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 匀 (phonetic).
entries.坈: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 冗 (phonetic).
entries.坉: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 屯 (phonetic).
entries.坊: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 方 (phonetic).
entries.坋: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 分 (phonetic).
entries.坌: Phono-semantic compound: 分 (phonetic) + 土 (earth, semantic).
entries.坍: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 丹 (phonetic).
entries.坎: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth; soil, semantic) + 欠 (phonetic).
entries.坐: Compound ideogram: 留 (to stay) + 土 (ground).
entries.坑: In its current form, a Phono-semantic compound: 亢 (phonetic) + 土 (soil, semantic). Early forms appear to be 阬.
entries.坒: Phono-semantic compound: 比 (phonetic) + 土 (earth, semantic).
entries.坓: Phono-semantic compound: 井 (phonetic) + 土 (earth, semantic).
entries.坚: Simplified from 堅.; compare 览.
entries.坡: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (dirt, semantic) + 皮 (phonetic).
entries.坢: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 半 (phonetic).
entries.坤: Written as 川 in the Han Stone Classics, Haihunhou bamboo slips, and Mawangdui silk texts (possibly the Kun trigram rotated 90° clockwise), and as 𡘩 in the Wangjiatai and Tsinghua bamboo slips.
entries.坦: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 旦 (phonetic)
entries.坩: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth; dirt, semantic) + 甘 (phonetic).
entries.坪: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 平 (phonetic).
entries.坰: Character composed by the radical of the earth (土) and 冋 as a phonetical component; the latter component also points to the concept of "territory, area".
entries.坳: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 幼 (phonetic).
entries.坴: Phono-semantic compound: 圥 (phonetic) + 土 (earth; soil, semantic).
entries.坼: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 斥 (phonetic). The original form is 𡍩.
entries.垂: Originally 𡍮. Pictogram: 𠂹 + 土, flowers hanging from a plant.
entries.垈: Phono-semantic compound: 代 (phonetic) + 土 (earth; dust, semantic).
entries.型: Phono-semantic compound: 刑 (phonetic) + 土 (earth, semantic) – an earthen mold, hence form, pattern.
entries.垌: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, ground, semantic) + 同 (phonetic).
entries.垍: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth; soil, semantic) + 自 (phonetic).
entries.垔: Phono-semantic compound: 西 (phonetic) + 土 (dirt, semantic)
entries.垖: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 堆 (phonetic).
entries.垠: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (soil, semantic) + 艮 (phonetic)
entries.垣: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 亘 (phonetic).
entries.垸: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 完 (phonetic).
entries.垺: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 孚 (phonetic).
entries.垻: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 貝 (phonetic).
entries.垼: Phono-semantic compound: 役 (phonetic) + 土 (earth, semantic).
entries.埃: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth; soil, semantic) + 矣 (phonetic).
entries.埇: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 甬 (phonetic).
entries.埋:
Originally written 薶, a Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (plant, semantic) + 貍 (phonetic). 

Later changed to 埋, a Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 里 (phonetic).
entries.城: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (soil, semantic) + 成 (phonetic), since city walls were originally made of stamped earth.
entries.埔: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 甫 (phonetic).
entries.埗: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 步 (phonetic).
entries.埞: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (land, semantic) + 定 (phonetic).
entries.埠: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 阜 (phonetic).
entries.埡:
Simplified from 啞.

Phono-semantic compound: 土 (dirt, semantic) + 亞 (phonetic).
entries.埤: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (dirt, semantic) + 卑 (phonetic)
entries.埪: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 空 (phonetic).
entries.埫: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 尚 (phonetic).
entries.埳: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (soil, semantic) + 臽 (phonetic).
entries.埶:
Compound ideogram: 木 (sapling) + 丮 (kneeling person; to hold) – a kneeling person planting a sapling, hence “to plant”. The original character of 蓺 and 藝.

Sometimes 土 was added underneath the sapling; the two then merged into unrelated 坴, with the top component 圥 resulting from corruption of 木. The 丮 component on the right side of the character evolved into 丸. 

This character 埶 was also often phonetically borrowed to represent 勢.
entries.執: Compound ideogram: 㚔 (criminal / handcuffs) + 丮 (hand): to arrest. In the present form, 㚔 and 丮 have been replaced by 幸 and 丸, respectively.
entries.培: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 咅 (phonetic).
entries.基: Phono-semantic compound: 其 (phonetic) + 土 (earth, semantic) – a foundation of earth.
entries.埼: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 奇 (phonetic).
entries.堀: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 屈 (phonetic). It conveys the meaning of digging a hole in the ground.
entries.堄: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 兒 (phonetic).
entries.堆: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 隹 (phonetic). The original form is 𠂤.
entries.堇: Compound ideogram – a person (大) being burned in a sacrificial ceremony to invoke the rain. At the bottom of the character, a fire (火) is visible. At the top of the character, an open mouth screaming (廿) is visible. Compare 黃.
entries.堈: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 岡 (phonetic)
entries.堐: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 厓 (phonetic).
entries.堑: Phono-semantic compound: 斩 (earth, phonetic) + 土 (semantic).
entries.堛: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 畐 (phonetic).
entries.堠: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (soil; earth, semantic) + 侯 (phonetic).
entries.堤: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (soil, semantic) + 是 (phonetic).
entries.堪: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 甚 (extreme, profound, phonetic) — originally meaning “heavy mountain/earthen protrusion”, it later came to signify the act of “enduring” that earth's weight.
entries.堯:
Compound ideogram: 垚 (tall (of earth), phonetic) + 兀 (towering and bald, semantic).

The oracle bone script consists of two 土 at the top and a kneeling man stylized as 兀 at the bottom.
entries.堰: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, ground, semantic) + 匽 (phonetic).
entries.報: Compound ideogram: 㚔 (handcuffs) + 𠬝 (to subdue) – to convict; to punish; to declare guilty.
entries.場: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 昜 (phonetic).
entries.塊: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth; dust, semantic) + 鬼 (phonetic) – clod of dirt.
entries.塑: Phono-semantic compound: 朔 (phonetic) + 土 (earth, semantic).
entries.塕: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 翁 (phonetic).
entries.塗: Phono-semantic compound: 涂 (phonetic) + 土 (earth; dirt, semantic).
entries.塘: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (dirt, semantic) + 唐 (phonetic).
entries.塚: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 冢 (phonetic) – an earthen mound, a tomb of earth.
entries.塝: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 旁 (phonetic).
entries.塞:
Oracle bone script: Compound ideogram: 宀 (house) + 工 (two items) + 廾 (two hands) – stuffing the house with items. Hence, the original version is 𡨄, a character similar but unrelated to 共 but partly related to 展.

Shuowen: Compound ideogram: 𡨄 + 土 (soil); the bottom component was added later.
entries.塢: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (soil, semantic) + 烏 (phonetic)
entries.塩: Japanese shinjitai Simplified from 鹽. In the 1946 Tōyō kanji list.
entries.塸: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 區 (phonetic).
entries.塹: Phono-semantic compound: 斬 (phonetic) + 土 (earth, semantic).
entries.塼: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (soil, semantic) + 專 (phonetic).
entries.塽: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 爽 (phonetic).
entries.塾: Phono-semantic compound: 孰 (phonetic) + 土 (soil, semantic).
entries.境: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 竟 (phonetic).
entries.墊: Phono-semantic compound: 執 (phonetic) + 土 (earth, semantic).
entries.墐: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth; soil, semantic) + 堇 (phonetic)
entries.増:
Japanese shinjitai Simplified from 增.

The current form is a Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 曽 (phonetic).
entries.墘: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (soil; earth, semantic) + 乾 (phonetic).
entries.增: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 曾 (phonetic) – things grow in the earth, to build from earth.
entries.墟: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (dirt, semantic) + 虛 (phonetic).
entries.墣: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 菐 (phonetic)
entries.墨: Phono-semantic compound: 黑 (phonetic) + 土 (soil, semantic).
entries.墩: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (soil, semantic) + 敦 (phonetic).
entries.墫: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (clay, semantic) + 尊 (phonetic).
entries.墬: Phono-semantic compound: 阜 (semantic) + 彖 (phonetic) + 土 (semantic).
entries.墭: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth; clay, semantic) + 盛 (phonetic).
entries.墶: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (soil, semantic) + 達 (phonetic).
entries.墺: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 奧 (phonetic).
entries.壁: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 辟 (phonetic) – an earthen wall.
entries.壅: Phono-semantic compound: 雍 (phonetic) + 土 (soil; ground, semantic).
entries.壋: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 當 (phonetic).
entries.壓: Phono-semantic compound: 厭 (phonetic) + 土 (dust, semantic).
entries.壕: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth; dirt, semantic) + 豪 (phonetic).
entries.壘: Phono-semantic compound: 畾 (phonetic) + 土 (dirt, semantic)
entries.壙: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth; dirt, semantic) + 廣 (phonetic)
entries.壞: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 褱 (phonetic). The radical of the earth is used since something that rots eventually becomes earth.
entries.壟: Phono-semantic compound: 龍 (phonetic) + 土 (earth, semantic).
entries.壠: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 龍 (phonetic).
entries.壤: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, dirt, semantic) + 襄 (phonetic).
entries.壩: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 霸 (phonetic).
entries.壪: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (dirt, semantic) + 彎 (phonetic).
entries.士: Pictogram – a war axe. Later, it took the meaning of "soldier" and eventually "officer, intellectual". Partly related to 王 since in at least two characters it should represent a ritual axe, perhaps made of jade: in fact, it is related to 圭 and 金 despite their appearance.
entries.壱: Found in Zhongwen Da Cidian 《中文大辭典》, a dictionary published in Taiwan from 1962 to 1968 that is based on the Japanese Dai Kan-Wa Jiten.
entries.壽:
In bronze inscriptions, one of the forms is a Phono-semantic compound – composed of 耂 (old, semantic) + 𢏚 (phonetic). It can additionally bear a decorative symbol (口) or two (口 and 又).

The common traditional form 壽 is evolved from the composition with the two decorative symbols, with 又 becoming 寸.
entries.夅: Pictogram – feet pointing down, descending (feet at top, legs pointing down – upside-down). Compare footprints in 舛, and foot in 夂, 夊.
entries.夆:
Simplified from 丰.

Phono-semantic compound: 夂 (footprint pointing down, walk, semantic) + 丰 (bush, brush, phonetic) – to meet.

According to Ji Xushen (季旭昇), a foot walking through brush, which resists being moved through.
entries.备: Simplified from 俻., a variant of 備. Officially adopted as the simplified form of 備 in the Chinese Character Simplification Scheme (s:漢字簡化方案) in 1956.
entries.変: Variant of 變. Simplified from 變.
entries.夊: Pictogram – footprint (pointing down), variant of 夂. Compare 止, which has similar form in oracle script, but has leg pointing up, and 𡕒 (as in right side of 舛, roughly ヰ), which also has leg pointing down, but toe pointing left, hence different evolutions.
entries.夋: Pictogram: originally a person squatting or sitting with bent legs, as preserved in early forms of 畯; probably the original character for 踆／蹲 (“to squat”). Later remodeled after 允 with added 夊.
entries.夌: Compound ideogram: 木 (tree, semantic) + 人 (a person, semantic). On bronze inscription, a foot 夂 was added at the bottom of the character. Later, the two components on top were highly compressed and stylized into 圥 (with a variant 𡴆). Its original meaning was perhaps "to climb; to surpass".
entries.夏:
Some scholars identify an oracle bone character Compound ideogram: 日 (sun) + 頁 (head; man) as this character – a man under the scorching sun; summer. However, it only appears as a diviner's name, making the identification uncertain.

In Spring and Autumn period bronze inscriptions, various variants appeared. 止 was often added below the man, and in some forms 日 was removed while 𦥑 was added. The seal script inherits from the latter form, with 止 replaced by the related 夊.

Warring States period forms also varied. The bamboo and silk script above shows a common form: 日 + 止 + 頁. The "ancient script" (古文) in Shuowen (labelled as large seal script) has deviated significantly, with 止 becoming 足 and the top part possibly a corruption of 頁.

The current form derives from the seal script, with 𦥑 and the legs of 頁 removed. Unrelated to 复.
entries.夐:
Perhaps a cave or yurt (穴) with an eye in the middle (目) and, at the bottom of the character, a hand holding a stick similar to 支. The original form is attested in the Shuowen Jiezi. The bottom components (a stick in hand indicating authority and an eye) should convey the concept of "authority".

Perhaps linked to 奐, in which it could appear as a contraction at the top of the character.
entries.夕: Pictogram – moon crescent. Compare to its ancient variant 月.
entries.夗:
Pictogram – An animal lying down about to die (Ji Xusheng, 2004).

Some older forms of the character may be interpreted as being composed of 肉 and 乃 or 人.
entries.夙:
The oracle bone script consisted of 月 and 丮, and resembled a man holding the moon, probably representing the worship of the moon. Alternatively, it might represent a person working under the moon in the early morning when the moon has not set.

In some forms of its bronze inscription, 月 corrupted into 夕.

丮 later got reduced into 凡.
entries.夜:
Phono-semantic compound: 亦 (phonetic) + 夕 (moon, semantic). 夕 may also serve as another phonetic component.

In the modern form, the phonetic 亦 is distorted into 亠 + 亻 + ㇏, with the right-falling stroke ㇏ merging into the semantic 夕.
entries.夢:
In the Oracle bone script, a Pictogram – or Compound ideogram – a person (人) lying on a bed (爿), sometimes with restless hands (compare the oracle-bone character for 丮) and sometimes with the eye (目) emphasized.

In the Bronze inscriptions, the eye (目) has eyebrows above it (compare 眉), and the person's body is attached underneath, now written as two dots on either side. The bed is no longer present, and instead 夕 has been added.

In the modern form 夢, the eyebrows are written 卝, the eyes are written 罒, and the person's body has become 冖, while 夕 remains on the bottom.

According to Shuowen, it is a Phono-semantic compound: 瞢 (phonetic) + 夕 (semantic).
entries.大:
Pictogram: a standing person facing forward. Compare 人, which represents the profile of a person.

Often explained as an ideogram of a person with outstretched arms; however, the ancient scripts do not show stretching.

Compare with 尢, which is a man with bent legs. Compare also 立, similar to 大, and 交, in which the legs are crossed. Compare also 文, which is a man with arms outstretched and a crest or tattoo on his chest, and to 夭, which is a man with arms outstretched and leaning to side (running or marching vigorously).

See the top component of 泰 in the original version (𡙌), the top component of 赤 and the bottom component of 奐 (well visible in some fonts). Related to 太.

Unrelated to 买, in which the bottom component is the stylization of a cowrie.
entries.夨: Pictogram – - a man tilting his head.
entries.太:
Phono-semantic compound: a differentiated form of 大 with a 丶 added to represent 太.

Compare 泰, which is also a differentiated form with 廾 and 水 added instead.
entries.夫:
Pictogram: a variant form of 大 preserving its original meaning of 夫. 大 and 夫 were originally used interchangeably before settling to their current meanings.

The character was later also phonetically borrowed as an instance of Phonetic loan – for 夫.

Shuowen mistakes the added horizontal stroke for a hairpin. In ancient times, when men reached the age of 20, they bound their hair with a hairpin during the Guan Li ceremony. The hairpin would thus be interpreted as the sign of “a grownup man”.
entries.夬: Pictogram – a hand wearing an archer's thumb ring.
entries.夭: Ideogram – a figure leaning forward, presumably running, hence energetic, young. See also the top component of the Kangxi radical 走.
entries.夰: Unclear. Xu Shen: Compound ideogram: 大 (man) + 八 (divide) – “to release”.
entries.失:
Pictogram – depicting a footprint of someone that has fallen surrounded by drops of blood.

Alternatively, according to Shuowen, Compound ideogram: 手 + 乙 — something falling from a hand (手). However, the original form doesn't show any hand.
entries.头: Simplified from 頭. from its cursive form, with 豆 into ⺀ and 頁 into 大.
entries.夷:
Originally Compound ideogram: 矢 (arrow) + 弓 (rope); the original meaning was "to shoot" (arrows) according to Chen Bingxin (陳秉新).

Later forms Compound ideogram: 大 (person; big) + 弓 (bow).
entries.夸: Phono-semantic compound: 大 (man, semantic) + 于 (phonetic)
entries.夺: Simplified from 奪. Used since the Ming dynasty.
entries.夾: Compound ideogram – one person (大) holding two other people (人) under his arm, or two people (人) sandwiching a person (大).
entries.奄:
Chen (2021): Phono-semantic compound: 盍 (semantic) + 甲 (phonetic) — original form of 掩.

Shuowen: Compound ideogram: 大 (big) + 申 (extend) – to cover.
entries.奇: Phono-semantic compound: 大 (big; great, semantic) + 可 (phonetic).
entries.奉: Originally Phono-semantic compound: 丰 (phonetic) + 廾 (two hands, semantic)， hence the original version is 𠬻. 手 was later added at the bottom, and the original character was corrupted into 𡗗. Related to 舉.
entries.奋: Simplified from 奮. Compare 夺. This was traced back to a blockprint of 《嶺南逸史》 from 1862-92.
entries.奌:
Variant of 點.

Current form is 占 + 大.
entries.奎:
Phono-semantic compound: 大 (semantic) + 圭 (phonetic).

Originally, the phonetic component is not related to the concept of earth (土) since in its original form it represents a pair of ritual axes perhaps made of jade 士. Hence, the link to the concept of earth in this character either comes from folk etymology or its appearance in the Small Seal script.
entries.奏:
Compound ideogram: two hands (廾) holding an object, perhaps a musical instrument used during a sacrifical ritual (the lower part of the object originally was similar to 夲).

Otherwise, the whole character depicts two hands collecting resin (桼) dripping from a cut tree (drawn like 屮). The resin is visible at the bottom of the character.
entries.奐:
Phono-semantic compound: 夐 (phonetic) + 廾 (semantic). The upper part indicates both ancient pronunciation and the concept of "eminent" (it contains an eye and a stick in hand representing authority), while the two hands at the bottom of the character (then stylized as 大) convey the meaning of "numerous, copious, abundant" attested on oracle bones. It was also used to represent 換.

Alternatively Compound ideogram: 穴 (yurt) + 廾 (hands) a pair of hands opening a yurt door to let in sunlight, hence there could be a potential shift of meaning from "brilliant".

A third interpretation by Xun Zaiguo (徐在國) explains that the character indicates "to steal" or "to take objects from other people's houses", i.e., a yurt from which two hands steal/take something. This interpretation could be linked to "numerous", but it is difficult to link to "brilliant".
entries.契:
Phono-semantic compound: 㓞 (to engrave, phonetic) + 大 (person, semantic), hence a person making an agreement and/or carving something with a knife.

Possibly a variant of 栔 or vice versa, given that the two characters were used interchangeably in ancient text.
entries.奓: Phono-semantic compound: 大 (person; big, semantic) + 多 (many, phonetic).
entries.奕: Phono-semantic compound: 亦 (phonetic) + 大 (big; great, semantic).
entries.套:
Compound ideogram: 大 (large) + 長 (long) – long, with some reference to hair. Originally written as 𡘷.

It was later borrowed for the “cover; cover with, put on (clothes); link” sense and has now lost its original meaning. It is also used as a classifier for a suit of clothes or a group of things, hence something that can be put on or a group of linked/interconnected things.
entries.奚: Compound ideogram: a hand (爪) grabbing a person (大) by their braids (幺) – “servant; slave”. In Warring States texts the bottom of the character was often simplified, making the character interchangeable with 系.
entries.奠:
Oracle bone script: Pictogram – an alcohol vessel (酉) placed on a mat (一).

In the bronze inscriptions, two strokes (八) were sometimes added above the alcohol vessel, representing overflowing alcohol; this is inherited in the small seal script as 酋. In some bronze inscriptions, two horizontal strokes were sometimes also added below the line representing a mat; the strokes sometimes were changed to something like 八. These two strokes then fused with the mat to give 丌 (a table with two legs) in the small seal script. 丌 later evolved into 大 by process of libian (隸變).
entries.奡:
Compound ideogram: 首 (head) + 大 (person). Original meaning unclear, possibly an arrogant person with their head held high, in which case the original form of 傲.

Bottom component is now written 夰.
entries.奧: The character has two lineages. The Shuowen Jiezi small seal form (宀 + 釆 + 𠬞), first attested on the mid-Western Zhou lid of the 康伯簋 vessel reading 簋, depicts an indoor rice-offering ritual whose seated shi impersonator is the "corner god" of the southwest corner; it denotes 尊位 through this ritual site. The clerical and regular form instead derives from the 勹/匚 form common in Han slips; its upper part is the Western Zhou bronze 匊, a belly storing grain (whence the 胃 component), the ancient character for 宛藏.
entries.奨:

Originally a variant of 姐. Later repurposed as a feminine third-person pronoun influenced by European languages, with the glyph being the result of replacing the 人 radical in 他 with 女. Linguist Liu Bannong is credited with coining this use around the 1910s, in turn replacing a precursor form of 他女 in print.

Uncertain.

entries.子:
Pictogram – an image of a baby, with a large head and spread arms. The legs are wrapped in a blanket. Compare with 了, where the arms are wrapped, and 㜽, in which a lock of hair is visible on top. Compare also 棄 and 毓, in which the image of the baby is reversed upside-down.

The big seal script form is much more elaborate, showing a baby with hair on a head (囟) and arms on the two sides of the body, sitting on a stool (几).

See also the right component of 保.

entries.學:
The earliest oracle bone form consists of 𦥑 + 六; subsequent groups write 爻 + 六 or 𦥑 + 爻, and later forms combine all three into 𦥯 (𦥑 + 爻 + 六), with some abbreviated to 爻. Bronze inscriptions add semantic 子.

In oracle bone inscriptions, the character is attested in four kinds of contexts: (1) a ritual building (學 / 大學) that could be built (作學), entered (入學), and used for the 尋 rite, where a new 庸 (鏞) bell was housed; (2) to learn or rehearse ritual music and dances (學商, 學羌); (3) to instruct or drill a collective (王學眾人); and (4) the name of a deceased former minister, 學戊 (Xue-wu), 戊 being a day-name.

In the modern form, 六 has corrupted to 冖, and the hands 𦥑 around the 爻 have become connected with the 冖. Shuowen regards 𦥑 as the phonetic component in the character, which may be true according to some Old Chinese reconstructions such as that of Pan Wuyun's, though probably not others.

See also the top component of 覺, which is a contraction of 學.

entries.宀:
Pictogram – a house; similar to 广. According to Wang Yun (王筠), the latter character depicts a building with three walls, while the former depicts a house with four walls.

Today, the pictogram appears smaller, but a conservative character is 𰃦, which appears in 向. See also the top component of 冡 and the original version of 叟.
entries.它:
Pictogram: a snake. This is now written as the derivative 蛇. 

Phonetic loan: the character was later borrowed for the then-homophonous third-person pronoun (“he/she/it”). Today 他 is used for male or gender-unspecified “he” and 她 for “she”.

It's possible that 寸 (original form of 肘) is also a phonetic component. A more conservative version is 㝊, in which 又 is not a phonetic component.
