entries.宓: Phono-semantic compound: 宀 (roof, semantic) + 必 (phonetic) – hidden at home.
entries.宗: Compound ideogram: 宀 (house) + 示 (spirit tablet) – temple; ancestral shrine.
entries.官: Compositionally related to 宮, but approximately analysable as Compound ideogram: 宀 + 𠂤 – multiple rooms under a roof, an official building.
entries.宙: Phono-semantic compound: 宀 (roof, semantic) + 由 (phonetic). It originally represented the farthest place accessible by boat or vehicle and, by extension, came to express the idea of spatial expansion or vastness.
entries.宛:
Phono-semantic compound: 宀 (semantic) + 夗 (phonetic).

Its original meaning was perhaps linked to "house"; in ancient times, it was read as "館".
entries.宜: Originally a Pictogram – or Compound ideogram: 且 (sacrifical altar) + 多 (two pieces of meat) – two pieces of sacrificial meat placed in a sacrifical altar.
entries.宝: Simplified from 寶. Officially adopted as the simplified form of 寶 in the Chinese Character Simplification Scheme (s:漢字簡化方案) in 1956.
entries.实: From cursive script (East Asia) of 實. Compare Japanese shinjitai 実.
entries.客: Phono-semantic compound: 宀 (roof, semantic) + 各 (phonetic) – a guest.
entries.宣: Phono-semantic compound: 宀 (roof, semantic) + 亘 (phonetic). The character originally represented the main hall where the emperor resided. By extension, it came to be used to mean "clear" or "evident."
entries.室:
Phono-semantic compound: 宀 (roof, semantic) + 至 (phonetic). Its original meaning is "house, residence".

The arrows also indicates that a residence is a place or spot which somebody stops by, marked by an arrow on the ground, hence the phonetic component also adds part of the meaning. Therefore, the character can also be understood as an ideogrammic compound – "a ⼧ roof over ⾄ this exact spot". According to Shuowen Jiezi, it is indeed so, as the meaning is "至所止 arrive at a specific place, symbolized by the roof.
entries.宦: Compound ideogram: 宀 (house) + 臣 (servant) – slave; servant.
entries.宬: Phono-semantic compound: 宀 (roof, semantic) + 成 (phonetic).
entries.宯: Phono-semantic compound: 宀 (roof, semantic) + 孝 (phonetic).
entries.宰:
Compound ideogram: 宀 (house) + 乂 (to govern) — house of government.

乂 originally appeared as similar to 䇂 in the oracle bone script; in the modern form of this character, it has corrupted into 辛.
entries.宴: Phono-semantic compound: 宀 (semantic) + 妟 (phonetic) – a woman in peaceful background (a roof and the sun). However, the appearance of the character, its meaning and his ancient pronunciation could link this character to 安.
entries.宵: Phono-semantic compound: 宀 (roof, semantic) + 肖 (phonetic).
entries.家:
Oracle bone script: Phono-semantic compound: 宀 (roof, semantic) + 𢑓 (male pig, phonetic). An archaic variant closer to the original drawing is 𡩀. See 𢑓 for more. Similar to 冡*.

Later the phonetic component was corrupted to 豕, so Shuowen Jiezi erroneously analyzed it as Phono-semantic compound: 宀 (roof, semantic) + 豭 (pig, phonetic).

All etymologies based on the modern version of the phonetic component (豕) are folk etymologies since they miss the original component (𢑓).
entries.容:
Phono-semantic compound: 宀 (semantic) + 公 (phonetic) – to hold; to contain.

容 has also largely supplanted 頌 for the sense of “appearance”.
entries.宽: Simplified from 寬. - Note that the 丶* stroke above the 儿* component in 萈* has been eliminated.
entries.宿:
In the oracle bone script, an Compound ideogram: 人 (person) + ⿴囗⿱人仌 (bamboo mat) – a person resting on a mat. Sometimes a house (宀) was added.

Later the pictogram of the bamboo mat became 㐁 or 𠀬, and eventually came to be written 百.

Contrast 寒.
entries.寂: Phono-semantic compound: 宀 (house, semantic) + 叔 (phonetic)
entries.寄: Phono-semantic compound: 宀 (house, semantic) + 奇 (phonetic) ― living away from home.
entries.寅:
Originally an Ideogram: an arrow 矢 with a distinguishing mark (now 日). 

 considers it the original character of 演.

In the modern form the arrowhead has corrupted into 宀.
entries.密: Phono-semantic compound: 宓 (phonetic) + 山 (mountain, semantic) – hidden in the mountains, secret, intimate. Note that the phonetic 宓 alone has also been used to express the same morpheme as 密.
entries.寇: Compound ideogram – - a person who holds a stick (卜) with his hand (又), about to beat the head (元) of another person, under the other persons own roof (宀). In Oracle bone script, two hands are holding the stick. In modern form, 卜 and 又 have merged into one character (攴), and is partially surrounded by 元.
entries.寉: 宀 + 隹, a corruption of 隺.
entries.寊: Phono-semantic compound: 宀 (roof, semantic) + 貞 (phonetic).
entries.寐:
Phono-semantic compound: 㝱 (dream, semantic) + 未 (phonetic).

Original form may have been an Compound ideogram: 宀 (house) + 爿 (bed) + 人 (person) – a person sleeping on a bed in a room. Compare ancient forms of 夢.
entries.寒:
Compound ideogram: 宀 (house) + 人 (person) + 茻 (grass) – a person in a house, sleeping in the grass to protect from the cold. In some bronze inscriptions, 二 is added at the bottom of the character; this may simply be decorative or may represent a mat. In the seal script, 二 is changed to 仌 to emphasize its meaning of coldness.

Contrast 宿.
entries.寙: Phono-semantic compound: 宀 (roof, semantic) + 㼌 (phonetic).
entries.寛:
Unorthodox form Simplified from 寬. Elimination of 丶 stroke and alteration of 𦫳 (ram's horn component) → 艹 (grass radical).

Originally found in the historical Longkan Shoujian (龍龕手鑑) dictionary (997 AD).
entries.察: Phono-semantic compound: 宀 (roof, semantic) + 祭 (phonetic).
entries.寠: Phono-semantic compound: 宀 (roof, semantic) + 婁 (phonetic).
entries.寡:
In the bronze script from the Western Zhou period, it was originally an Compound ideogram: 宀 (house) + 頁 (head) — only one person in the house; alone.

In the bronze script from the Warring States period, two decorative strokes were added around 頁. The seal script found in Shuowen adds two additional strokes, making the component under 宀 appear as 分 and 頁, leading Shuowen to erroneously interpret the character as an Compound ideogram: 宀 (house) + 頒 (to distribute).
entries.寢: Phono-semantic compound: 宀 (roof, semantic) + 爿 (bed, semantic) + 𠬶 (broom and hand, phonetic).
entries.寤: Phono-semantic compound: 㝱 (dream, semantic) + 吾 (phonetic).
entries.實:
Compound ideogram: 宀 (roof) + 周 (carved jade) + 貝 (shellfish; cowrie).

The two lower components of 周 and 貝 had combined to form 貫, hence the incorrect analysis in Shuowen Jiezi of this character as 宀 + 貫.
entries.寧:
Oracle bone script: Compound ideogram: 宀 (house) + 皿 (food or wine vessel) + 丂 (table (?)) – contentment. The 心 component was added in bronze inscriptions to yield 寧, and the 丂 component was sometimes omitted to yield 寍.

Shuowen: Phono-semantic compound: 寍 (phonetic) + 丂 (speech (?), semantic).

Note that the simplified form 宁 is also a traditional character on its own.
entries.寨:
Simplified from 砦.

Phono-semantic compound: 𡨄 (to block; to block up; to jam; to plug, phonetic) + 木 (wood, semantic).
entries.審: Compound ideogram: 宀 (roof) + 釆 (to distinguish) + 田. There are two theories about the component 田. One is that it was originally 口, then corrupted into 曰, then further into 田. The other one is that its a remnant from a variant form ⿱宷思 with 心 omitted. The Shuowen Jiezi describes 審 as the seal script variant of 宷.
entries.寬:
Phono-semantic compound: 宀 (house, semantic) + 萈 (goat, phonetic)—a spacious house.

See also 家.
entries.寭: Phono-semantic compound: 宀 (roof, semantic) + 惠 (phonetic).
entries.寯: Phono-semantic compound: 宀 (roof, semantic) + 雋 (phonetic).
entries.寰: Phono-semantic compound: 宀 (roof, semantic) + 睘 (phonetic) – emperor's domain of 1000 li surrounding the capital.
entries.寳: A variant of 寶//, apparently contaminated by 珎//珍.
entries.寴: Phono-semantic compound: 宀 (roof, semantic) + 親 (phonetic).
entries.寶:
Oracle bone script: Compound ideogram: 宀 (house) + 琡 (jade) + 貝 (cowry) – treasures in a house.

The phonetic component 缶 was added to the character in bronze inscriptions.
entries.寷: Phono-semantic compound: 宀 (roof, semantic) + 豐 (phonetic).
entries.寺:
Phono-semantic compound: 之 (to go, phonetic) + 又 (hand, semantic) – to grasp, to hold. Phonetic 𡳿 (之), which represents a footprint pointing up, became 土 or 士 in the clerical script from the late Western Han to the Eastern Han, and semantic 又 became 寸 in Small Seal Script. The derivative 持 refers to the original word.

The character was often used in the place of a more specialized form. For example, in the Chu Silk Manuscript (see table above) it clearly stood for 時.
entries.寻:
Simplified from 尋.

Current form 又 (hand) + 寸 (hand).
entries.封:
Phono-semantic compound: 丰 (phonetic) + 土 (earth, semantic) + 寸 (hand, semantic). Compare 邦.

Originally 丰, depicting a tree seedling. Variants that added any combination of 土, 又, 田, 丮 appeared from bronze inscriptions onwards.
entries.専:
Variant of 專; Simplified from 專. Compare 恵.

The modern Japanese usage is of reform (shinjitai) nature.
entries.尃: Phono-semantic compound: 甫 (garden, phonetic) + 寸 (hand, semantic) – to distribute crops. However, the phonetic component has a reference to a sprout growing in a field 田 according to its original version.
entries.射:
In the oracle bone script, an Compound ideogram: 弓 (bow) + 矢 (arrow) – to shoot a bow. In the bronze inscriptions, a hand (又) drawing the bowstring was added. Hence, a conservative variant is 𢎤.

Later the bow and arrow on the left became 身 before or during the clerical script period, and the hand came to be written 寸.
entries.將:
Phono-semantic compound: 爿 (bed; small table, phonetic) + 肉 (meat, semantic) + 寸 (hand, semantic) – to offer meat as tribute. Besides pronunciation, 爿 may partly indicate a small cutting board and/or sacrificial table on which the meat is placed. The sacrificial meat and the hand together form the shape 𪧷, which is similar but unrelated to 有.

The ⺼ component is on its side, hence resembles 夕 with an added dot; compare 祭, 然.

Shuowen erroneously considers the phonetic component of 將 to be 醬 (abbreviated).
entries.專:
Compound ideogram: 叀 (spindle, phonetic) + 又 (hand, semantic) – a hand turning a spindle or spinning wheel. It has come to mean to bundle several things together into one. Originally also written 叀.

The 又 was later replaced by related 寸.
entries.尉: Possibly Compound ideogram: 𡰥 + 寸 (hand) + 火 (fire).
entries.尊:
Shuowen: Compound ideogram: 酋 (wine) + 寸 (hand) – a hand 寸 offering a vessel of wine 酋 to show respect and veneration.

However, based on the small seal script, it may instead be a variant of 𢍜, which is Compound ideogram: 酋 (wine) + 廾 (two hands).
entries.尋:
Compound ideogram: two hands (now 彐 and 寸) stretched out measuring a mat (now 工) – "a unit of measurement; arm span". The component 口 (“mouth, talk”) was likely added to emphasize the act of reading the measurement out loud. Forms with it have appeared as early as oracle bone script, but forms without it have also appeared as late as the Spring and Autumn period. 

Appears as 𢒫 in the Shuowen Jiezi, which interprets the character as Phono-semantic compound – with 彡 as the sound component.
entries.尌:
Compound ideogram: 木 (tree) + 寸 (hand) — to plant a tree. The form in the oracle bone script appears as 权. A phonetic 豆 was added later.

In the modern form, 木 and 豆 have fused into 壴, and the character is sometimes mistaken for a compound of 壴 + 寸.

This character has largely been superseded by 樹.
entries.對:
In the oracle bone and bronze scripts, it was an Compound ideogram: 丵 (tool for digging) + 土 (earth) + 又 (hand). The original meaning of the character is unclear, but it may be “to develop (land)”. It was later borrowed for “to reply”. Compare 封, 邦.

In the seal script, 又 has become the related 寸. Shuowen has two seal script forms for this character: 𡭊 (main form) and 對 (alternative form). The main form, which has a 口, was probably created to specialize the character to signify “to reply”, but this form was not inherited in later scripts. Shuowen interprets the latter form (shown above) as a form that Emperor Wen of Han created by replacing 口 with 士 because many of the replies were untruthful (just lip service), but it is more likely that 士 is a corruption of 土.
entries.導: Phono-semantic compound: 道 (path, phonetic) + 寸 (hand, semantic) – to lead someone.
entries.少:
Pictogram – four dots, perhaps three grains of sand (see 沙), to indicate "a few, a little". Phonetically borrowed from 小, which is depicted by three dots.

Unrelated to 步 (and hence 歲), in which the lower component is the stylization of a foot.
entries.尓: Unorthodox variant (俗字) of 爾 found in some Japanese dictionaries.
entries.尔:
Variant of 尒, which is in turn an abridgement of 爾.

Officially adopted as the simplified form of 爾 in the Chinese Character Simplification Scheme (s:漢字簡化方案) in 1956.
entries.尕: Compound ideogram: 乃 (breast; milk) + 小 (small) – a suckling infant (small).
entries.尖: 小 (small) + 大 (large) – the width of an object gradually changing from small to large.
entries.尗: Pictogram – a wooden stake digging the dirt. See also 弋 and 才.
entries.尘:
Simplified from 塵., making an Compound ideogram: 小 (small, semantic) + 土 (earth, semantic).

According to the Kangxi dictionary, 尘 is an ancient form of 塵. This character is also used in simplified Chinese.
entries.尚: Phono-semantic compound: 八 (semantic) + 向 (phonetic). Similar to 冋.
entries.尤: Pictogram – hand with a wart. Original form of 疣 and 肬.
entries.尭: Simplified from 堯. in Japanese shinjitai.
entries.尮: Phono-semantic compound: 尢 (lame, semantic) + 朶 (phonetic).
entries.尯: Phono-semantic compound: 尢 (lame, semantic) + 危 (phonetic).
entries.就: Originally 𫢁, Compound ideogram: 享 + 京, a temple and a tower – meaning "to sacrifice at a high place". During the Warring States period, 享 was omitted. In seal script, 尤 is added to the right, signifying "high; to go to a higher place".
entries.尸:
Pictogram – - A man with his legs bending, and a side to the front. Its ancient form is 𡰣. The letter ㄕ(shī) was based exactly on this form. The picture is variously interpreted as either sitting or lying.

When used as a radical, 尸 is usually derived from a variation of 人 or 亻, as in 尾.
entries.尹:
Compound ideogram: 丿 (stick) + 又 (hand).

A hand holding a rod or brush, indicating control, similar to 事* and 支*.
entries.尻:
Pictogram – in the oracle bone script – a person with the buttocks highlighted.

In the seal script, it developed into a Phono-semantic compound: 尸 (body, semantic) + 九 (phonetic).
entries.尾: Compound ideogram: 尸 (person) + 毛 (hair; feather).
entries.尿: Pictogram – in the oracle bone script - a urinating man. In the seal script, it became an Compound ideogram: 尾 (tail) + 水 (water). 尾 later simplified into 尸.
entries.局:
Phono-semantic compound: 尸 (semantic) + 句 (phonetic).

Folk etymology found in some dictionaries mistakes it for a representation of a deceased person's limbs being bent and buried.
entries.屁: Phono-semantic compound: 尸 (body, semantic) + 比 (phonetic).
entries.屄: Compound ideogram: 尸 (body) + 穴 (hole) — a hole under a body.
entries.屆: Phono-semantic compound: 尸 (body, semantic) + 凷 (phonetic)
entries.屈: Originally 𡲶. Phono-semantic compound: 出 (phonetic) + 尾 (tail, semantic). 尾 became 尸 in clerical script.
entries.屋:
Phono-semantic compound: 𡉉 (phonetic) + 室 (room, semantic). The upper part has corrupted into the unrelated 尸.

Shuowen mistakes it for an ideogrammic compound.
entries.屌: Phono-semantic compound: 尸 (body, semantic) + 吊 (hanging, phonetic): “something that hangs from the body”.
entries.屐: Shuowen: Phono-semantic compound: 履 (shoe, semantic) + 支 (phonetic).
entries.展:
Phono-semantic compound: 尸 (semantic) + 𧝑 (phonetic), which has a variant 𧝣; the original version is 㞡. The phonetic component is a reference to fine red silk clothes, one of the six garments worn by the queen in the Rites of Zhou, and it contains as well a reference to the concept of "opening, extending; watch carefully" in the component 㠭.

Similar but unrelated to 昔 and 共.
entries.屙:
Simplified from 阿.

Phono-semantic compound: 尸 (semantic) + 阿 (phonetic).
entries.屚: Compound ideogram: 屋 (roof) + 雨 (rain) – to leak.
entries.屠: Phono-semantic compound: 尸 (body, semantic) + 者 (phonetic).
entries.屩: Phono-semantic compound: 履 (footwear, semantic) + 喬 (phonetic)
entries.屬: Phono-semantic compound: 尾 (tail, semantic) + 蜀 (phonetic).
entries.屯: Pictogram – a swollen sprout or bud beginning to emerge; the original form of 芚.
entries.屰: Pictogram – an upside down human figure (大 inverted) – opposite, backwards, opposing. In the small script version, a horizontal stroke was added perhaps to emphasize the fact that the man is upside down. Original form of 逆.
entries.山:
Pictogram – three mountain peaks. In the Oracle Bone Script, they were represented by triangles rather than vertical strokes. Compare 丘, particularly earlier forms.

Unrelated to 出 and the top component of 岁 and 豐. Also unrelated to 屮 and 巾.
entries.屵: Compound ideogram: 山 (mountain) + 厂 (cliff). Proto-form of 岸 and perhaps 崖.
entries.屶: Kokuji (created in Japan). 山 + 刀
entries.屺: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain; hill, semantic) + 己 (phonetic).
entries.岀: 山 on top of one another, originally found in the historical Qing dynasty Zhengzitong dictionary (正字通).
entries.岃: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 刃 (phonetic). Compare 屻.
entries.岆: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 夭 (phonetic).
entries.岇: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 卬 (phonetic).
entries.岈: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 牙 (phonetic).
entries.岋: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 及 (phonetic).
entries.岌: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 及 (phonetic).
entries.岐: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 支 (phonetic)
entries.岓: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 斤 (phonetic).
entries.岔: Compound ideogram: 分 (split; division) + 山 (mountain)
entries.岛: Simplified from 島. (bottom component 山 remains unchanged) based on radical simplification of 鳥 to 鸟.
entries.岠: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 巨 (phonetic).
entries.岢: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 可 (phonetic)
entries.岦: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 立 (phonetic).
entries.岩:
Compound ideogram: 山 (hill) + 石 (rock).

Originally written as 巖 – Phono-semantic compound: 山 (hill, semantic) + 嚴 (phonetic). The variant form 岩 first appeared in the clerical script in the Han dynasty era.
entries.岫: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 由 (phonetic).
entries.岬: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 甲 (phonetic).
entries.岱: Phono-semantic compound: 代 (phonetic) + 山 (mountain, semantic)
entries.岳: 羋 (sheep bleat) + 山 (mountain): rebus of 羋 for 岳, with 山 added as semantic component.
entries.岸: Phono-semantic compound: 屵 (cliff, semantic) + 干 (phonetic) – the edge of the land. Its proto-form was 屵.
entries.峙: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 寺 (phonetic).
entries.峨: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 我 (phonetic).
entries.峪: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 谷 (valley, phonetic)
entries.峭: Originally Phono-semantic compound: 阜 (soil mountain, semantic) + 肖 (phonetic), later Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 肖 (phonetic).
entries.峯: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 夆 (phonetic).
entries.峰: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 夆 (phonetic).
entries.峴: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 見 (phonetic).
entries.島: Phono-semantic compound: 鳥 (phonetic) + 山 (mountain, semantic).
entries.峻: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 夋 (phonetic).
entries.峽: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 夾 (phonetic).
entries.崇: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 宗 (phonetic).
entries.崎: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 奇 (phonetic).
entries.崑: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 昆 (phonetic).
entries.崔: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 隹 (phonetic).
entries.崖:
Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 厓 (cliff, phonetic).

Alternatively analyzed as Phono-semantic compound: 屵 (cliff, semantic) + 圭 (phonetic). In this case, its proto-form could be 屵.

Originally, the phonetic component is not related to the concept of earth (土) since in its original form it represents a pair of ritual axes perhaps made of jade 士. Hence, the link to the concept of earth in this character, 厓 and 街 either comes from folk etymology or its appearance in the Small Seal script.
entries.崗: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 岡 (phonetic).
entries.崙: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 侖 (phonetic).
entries.崟: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 金 (phonetic).
entries.崧: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 松 (phonetic).
entries.崩: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 朋 (phonetic) – to collapse (of a mountain).
entries.崽: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 思 (phonetic).
entries.嵊: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 乘 (phonetic).
entries.嵌: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 歁 (phonetic).
entries.嵍: Phono-semantic compound: 敄 (phonetic) + 山 (mountain, semantic).
entries.嵐: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 葻 (phonetic)
entries.嵡: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 翁 (phonetic).
entries.嵯: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 差 (phonetic).
entries.嵷: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 從 (phonetic).
entries.嶁: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 婁 (phonetic).
entries.嶅: Phono-semantic compound: 敖 (phonetic) + 山 (mountain, semantic).
entries.嶇: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 區 (phonetic).
entries.嶓: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 番 (phonetic).
entries.嶙: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 粦 (phonetic).
entries.嶝: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 登 (phonetic).
entries.嶢: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 堯 (phonetic).
entries.嶧: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 睪 (phonetic).
entries.嶶: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 微 (phonetic).
entries.嶺: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 領 (phonetic).
entries.巖: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 嚴 (phonetic).
entries.巗: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 嚴 (phonetic).
entries.巘: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 獻 (phonetic).
entries.巛: Pictogram – of water flowing; see 水, 川, and 𡿧. Unrelated to 兪 (> 俞).
entries.川: Pictogram – of flowing water – compare 水, 巛, and 𡿧.
entries.巠:
According to, this character is an ancient form of 經. Its bronze inscription form is a Pictogram – of vertical threads passing through the top of a loom and has the meaning "to abide by, to comply with". Unrelated to 工.

The etymology of this character is a matter of debate, and how it relates to

經 is still unclear. 

Several ancient dictionaries have the meaning as being connected (or related) to water, including the Shuowen, which has the meaning as "water flowing underground."

This is based, in part, on its having identified the "three lines" as representing 巛 (or 川), meaning "river" or "flowing water."
entries.巡: Phono-semantic compound: 辵 (walk, semantic) + 川 (phonetic).
entries.巢: Pictogram: a baby bird (巛) in a nest (田), which is on top of a tree (木).
entries.巣: Unorthodox variant of 巢 found in a Movable type#Metal movable type in China copy of Biographies of Exemplary Women 《列女傳》. First attested in 《宋元以來俗字譜》, a Variant Chinese character dictionary compiled in 1930 that records unorthodox forms (俗字) that have existed since the Song dynasty.
entries.工:
Pictogram – a bladed tool to plow the ground and to mark a border. As an alternative, a carpenter's square; according to the second interpretation, the character is related to the original meaning of 巨.

Unrelated to 巠 > 𢀖 and 壬.
entries.左:
Originally written 𠂇 and 䶹 in the oracle bone script: Pictogram – a left hand. Compare 又.

Late bronze inscription forms show an added 工 component, making the current form a Phono-semantic compound: 𠂇 (left hand, phonetic) + 工 (work, semantic), representing the original form of 佐.
entries.巨:
Phonetic loan – of 矩, borrowed for 巨. By the small seal script, the character was simplified and the man holding the carpenter's square was removed; however, the hand holding it appears to remain as the コ shape inside the 工.

Shuowen interprets it as a pictogram, however Chen (2021) points out that 矩 is the original shape.
entries.巫: Uncertain. One theory identifies this graph with the original character for 荒 in 四荒.
entries.差:
Compound ideogram: 來 (wheat) + 𠂇 (left hand) – to hull wheat by rubbing grains inside hands. Original form of 搓.

工 or 口 was later added under 𠂇 to form 左, which is also this character's phonetic component.
entries.己: Pictogram – silk rope for binding objects. Original form of 紀. The character must not be confused with 已 and 巳. See also 丩.
entries.已: May have originally been the same character as 巳, a Pictogram – of either a snake or a fetus. This character cannot be found in the Shuowen Jiezi.
entries.巷: Phono-semantic compound: 共 (phonetic) + 己 (oneself, semantic)
entries.巸: Phono-semantic compound: 𦣞 (chin, semantic) + 巳 (phonetic). 𦣞 may also act as a phonetic component.
entries.帀: Uncertain. Shuowen interprets the glyph as an inverted 之 (originally written as 㞢). Zhang Shichao (張世超) also interprets it as "roots" (柢). However, 之 in oracle bones represents a footprint.
entries.市: Oracle bone script and bronze inscriptions: Phono-semantic compound: 兮 (bustling, semantic) + 之 (phonetic).
entries.布: Phono-semantic compound: 父 (phonetic) + 巾 (kerchief, semantic).
entries.帅: Simplified from 帥. Compare 师 from 師.
entries.帆: Phono-semantic compound: 巾 (cloth, semantic) + 凡 (phonetic).
entries.师: Simplified from 師. Compare 帅 from 帥.
entries.希: Originally 𢁫, Compound ideogram: 爻 + 巾 (cloth).
entries.帔: Phono-semantic compound: 巾 (cloth, semantic) + 皮 (phonetic)
entries.帖: Phono-semantic compound: 巾 (a square item of cloth, semantic) + 占 (phonetic).
entries.帙: Phono-semantic compound: 巾 (cloth, semantic) + 失 (phonetic).
entries.帚:
Pictogram – a broom with bristles on top and tied handle on the bottom.

In modern form, top now resembles 聿, 肀, 彐, and overall graphically decomposes roughly as 肀 + 冖 + 巾.
entries.帛: Phono-semantic compound: 白 (phonetic) + 巾 (cloth, semantic).
entries.帝:
Pictogram: Original form of 蒂. In the Shi-xiao (師小) group, the earliest group containing 帝, two graphs, Heji 5662 and Heji 21080, depict the whole plant in full detail — an inverted-triangle corolla, stamens, and a stalk — with a 丁-shaped (rectangular) or 工-shaped mark at the joint below the corolla and above the stalk. In the early groups, the choice follows usage: the 丁-type is usual for 禘, the 工-type for 帝; the two may even alternate within a single divination. The 丁-type falls out of use after the third period of the oracle-bone script.

In the oracle-bone corpus the graph writes three words: the supreme deity 帝, who commands rain, thunder, and wind, grants harvests and aid in war, and sends down calamity and illness; the sacrifice 禘, offered to the four quarters, rivers, and mountains with offerings of cattle, sheep, dogs, and Qiang captives, performed by the king or his envoys; and, from the second period onward, a posthumous royal title 帝, as in 帝甲, 帝丁, and 文武帝, related to 嫡.
entries.帥: Compound ideogram: 寻 (two hands) + 巾 (scarf) - to wear a scarf. Shuowen Jiezi interprets it as Phono-semantic compound: 𠂤 (phonetic) + 巾 (semantic).
entries.師:
Compound ideogram: 𠂤 + 帀.

師 may be related to words denoting multitude, abundance, or movement to and fro, such as 詵, 駪, 甡, 莘, 侁, 瑟, 蝨 and 蟋.
entries.席:
Pictogram: a woven mat with ornament. Later, a phonetic 石 was added and the image of the mat corrupted into 巾. 

In the small seal script, 石 had corrupted into 𲟁, leading Shuowen to interpret it as 庶 (phonetic) + 巾 (semantic). In the variant 𠩛, the mat is better preserved and 石 has corrupted into 厂 instead.

Compare 度 and 庶.
entries.帮: Simplified from 幚., a variant of 幫 (with the phonetic 封 replaced with 邦). Officially adopted as the simplified form of 幫 in the Chinese Character Simplification Scheme (s:漢字簡化方案) in 1956.
entries.帰: Unorthodox variant Simplified from 歸. (⿱𠂤止 → ⿰丨丿) originally found in the Yuan dynasty orthographic dictionary 《字鑑》.
entries.常:
Phono-semantic compound: 尚 (phonetic) + 巾 (cloth, semantic).

The character originally referred to a "lower garment" similar to a skirt, before being phonetically borrowed to mean "long-lasting; frequently". The original sense is now represented by the character 裳.
entries.帽: Phono-semantic compound: 巾 (cloth, semantic) + 冒 (phonetic). Originally written as 冃; later, 目 and 巾 were added.
entries.幅: Phono-semantic compound: 巾 (clothing, semantic) + 畐 (phonetic).
entries.幕: Phono-semantic compound: 莫 (phonetic) + 巾 (cloth, semantic).
entries.幛: Considered a 後起字. Phono-semantic compound: 巾 (cloth, semantic) + 章 (phonetic).
entries.幟: Phono-semantic compound: 巾 (cloth, semantic) + 戠 (phonetic).
entries.幠: Phono-semantic compound: 巾 (towel, semantic) + 無 (phonetic).
entries.幡: Phono-semantic compound: 巾 (cloth, semantic) + 番 (phonetic).
entries.幣: Phono-semantic compound: 敝 (phonetic) + 巾 (cloth, semantic) – silk given as a gift or sacrificed.
entries.幫: Phono-semantic compound: 封 (phonetic) + 帛 (silk, semantic) – originally, the upper part of a shoe (鞋幫).
entries.干:
Pictogram – of a shield with feather ornaments on top; in some versions in oracle bones, the central and flat part of the shield can be seen as 回.

As an alternative, it is possible 干 and 單 are variant forms of the same character in oracle bone script due to their similar shapes and its appearance in the original forms of 敢. Hence, 干 would depict a bifurcated hunting weapon, not a shield. But 單 has two dots on top that depict two stones, while these two dots are absent in 干.

Also borrowed phonetically as a simplification of 乾 (dry) and 幹. See also 盾 (the pictogram of another shield) and its possible differentiation 古.

The interpretation that links this pictogram to a pestle is folk etymology. Unrelated to 午, which however represents a pestle.
entries.年:
Phono-semantic compound: 禾 (wheat; grain, semantic) + 人 (phonetic). Originally meaning "harvest", it later came to mean "year". In the oracle bone script and early bronze inscriptions, it was originally written like 秂.

In bronze inscriptions after the Western Zhou period, a stroke was often added to 人 to give 千, which still acted as a phonetic component, thus getting (秊). The current form is inherited from the clerical script, where libian (隸變) has occurred.
entries.幵: Compound ideogram: 干 + 干 – comparing two 干 side by side, even.
entries.幸:
Two kinds of glyph are found in Warring States era:;The glyph in Sanjin (三晉)

A compound of 犬 at left + 羊 at right.

Dog and sheep are seen to bring luck (Zhao, 1999).

羊 is phonetic (Liu, 2022).; The glyph in Chu (楚)

A compound of upside-down 矢 at left + 犬 at right, with unknown intention (Chen, 2005).

Qin-Han dynasty era inherited the Sanjin glyph with 犬 at top and 羊 at bottom (Liu, 2022). This is the source of the contemporary 幸 (Chen, 2015).
entries.幹: Originally 榦, a Phono-semantic compound: 倝 (phonetic) + 木 (tree, semantic). The semantic 木 was replaced with a phonetic 干, making both components phonetic.
entries.幼: Compound ideogram: 幺 (tiny) + 力 (strength). 幺 may also act as a phonetic component.
entries.幽: Phono-semantic compound: 𢆶 (phonetic) + 山 (semantic) (originally 火 in oracle bone).
entries.幾:
Compound ideogram: 𢆶 (silk threads; little things) + 戍 (to guard against) – watching over the fine details.

Note that the simplified form 几 is also a traditional character on its own.
entries.广:
Pictogram: A house with a roof, similar to 宀. According to Wang Yun (王筠), the former character depicts a building with three walls, while the latter depicts a house with four walls.

Unrelated to 床 and 疒, in which it represents a bed. Unrelated to ⼚, which represents a cliff.
entries.広: Simplified from 廣.; shinjitai. First attested in 1891 in Japan, influenced by 鑛 → 鉱.　Perhaps also influenced by 弘, 宏, 紘, all of which have the on reading こう and kun readings ひろ(い), ひろ(し) in Japanese.
entries.庆: Simplified from 慶. (elimination of bottom right component to 大) in the 1956 Chinese Character Simplification Scheme by the People's Republic of China. This character is not known to have existed prior to that.
entries.庇: Phono-semantic compound: 广 (house that is built to depend on a cliff, semantic) + 比 (phonetic).
entries.庈: Phono-semantic compound: 广 (cliffside house, semantic) + 今 (phonetic).
entries.床: Originally an unorthodox variant of 牀. Now made up of 广 (house) + 木 (tree), an Compound ideogram – representing a wooden furniture item (a bed) in a house.
entries.应: Unorthodox variant of 應. From cursive script (East Asia).
entries.底: Phono-semantic compound: 广 (building, semantic) + 氐 (phonetic) – the bottom or base, foundation of a building. Note that 氐, according to one interpretation, is a figure bowing or the root of a tree, hence a connotation of "down"; if the interpretation is correct, the phonetic component also adds part of the meaning.
entries.庖: Phono-semantic compound: 广 (house, semantic) + 包 (phonetic).
entries.店: Phono-semantic compound: 广 (house built to depend on a cliff, semantic) + 占 (phonetic)
entries.庚: Pictogram – a flail and a threshing device. See also 康, 唐 and 庸.
entries.府: Phono-semantic compound: 广 (building, semantic) + 付 (phonetic) – a type of building.
entries.度:
Phono-semantic compound: 石 (rock, phonetic) + 又 (hand, semantic). Duan Yucai argues that the presence of the hand component in this character is because the hand was used as a reference for measurement. 石 is then corrupted into 𲟁.

Shuowen considers it to be a Phono-semantic compound: 庶 (phonetic) + 又 (semantic).

Compare 庶 and 席.
entries.座: Phono-semantic compound: 广 (house on cliff, semantic) + 坐 (phonetic).
entries.庫:
Phono-semantic compound: 广 (building, semantic) + 車 (phonetic).

Shuowen incorrectly interprets it as an ideogrammic compound.
entries.庵: Phono-semantic compound: 广 (house, semantic) + 奄 (phonetic).
entries.庶:
Phono-semantic compound: 石 (stone, phonetic) + 火 (fire, semantic). In the small seal script, 石 has corrupted into 𲟁. Shuowen Jiezi interprets it as 广 (roof) + 炗 (light).

Compare 度 and 席.
entries.康:
Compound ideogram: 庚 (threshing tools) + 米 (rice) – chaff. The clearest version is 𢊪, in which the two components can be identified well; in the semi-conservative variant 𥹺, the rice at the bottom is still well visible. The derivative 糠 refers to the original word.

Unrelated to 隶, in which the bottom part is a reference to a tail (毛); also unrelated to 水.
entries.庸:
Phono-semantic compound: 庚 (semantic) + 同 (phonetic).

Probably the original graph of 鏞 (“large bell”), formed from 庚 plus 同 / 用.
entries.廄: Phono-semantic compound: 广 (house, semantic) + 㲃 (phonetic).
entries.廈: Phono-semantic compound: 广 (semantic) + 夏 (phonetic). However, the phonetic component means "great", hence it adds part of the meaning.
entries.廊:
Phono-semantic compound: 广 (semantic) + 郎 (phonetic).

良 may be the original form of this character, see there for more.
entries.廌: Pictogram – a deer-like mythical beast. Compare with 鹿.
entries.廓: Phono-semantic compound: 广 (broad; wide; extensive, semantic) + 郭 (phonetic).
entries.廢:
Phono-semantic compound: 广 (house, semantic) + 發 (phonetic).

During the Zhou Dynasty–Qin Dynasty period, 灋 and 法 were used to represent 廢.
entries.廩: Originally written 㐭. Later developed into an Compound ideogram: 广 (house, semantic) + 㐭 (granary, phonetic) + 禾 (grain, semantic).
entries.廬: Phono-semantic compound: 广 (roofed house, semantic) + 盧 (phonetic).
entries.廰: Nonstandard simplification of 廳, with 聽 substituted with its shinjitai form of 聴.
entries.廳: Phono-semantic compound: 广 (house, semantic) + 聽 (phonetic).
entries.廴: Pictogram (象形) – a man (人) with one leg behind him, implying a stride/step. Unrelated to 乃.
entries.建:
Compound ideogram: 廴 + 聿. Originally, a Pictogram – a hand (又) planting a pole (𰀁) into a base. The left component was originally written as ∟. The right component is stylized as 聿; while the hand is still recognizable, the bottom part is unrelated to a writing brush.

The whole character is mostly similar to 叔.
entries.廿:
Two 十 ("ten") written side by side, with a horizontal stroke at the bottom that fuses them. See also 卅.

In characters such as 漢 and 黄, it represents an open mouth 口, while in 度 and 席 it actually represents a stylized rock 石.
entries.开:
Compound ideogram: 干 + 干 (trunk). Two trunks are of the same height.

Also Simplified from 開.

As a component in composite characters, the part is not directly related to 開 and instead originally derives from 井 (such as in 刑, 型, etc.) or from 幵 (such as in 研, 形, etc.).
entries.弁: Compound ideogram: 厶 + 廾: hands (廾) placing a hat (厶) on someone’s head.
entries.弄: Compound ideogram: 玉 (jade) + 廾 (hands) – to touch jade with one's hands.
entries.弊: Phono-semantic compound: 敝 (destroy, tatters, phonetic) + 廾 (both hands, semantic): emphatic form of 敝 — destroying something with both hands.
entries.弋: Pictogram: a sharp peg — original form of 杙. Same as 才 and 尗.
entries.式: Phono-semantic compound: 弋 (phonetic) + 工 (work, semantic).
entries.弒: Phono-semantic compound: 殺 (to kill, semantic) + 式 (phonetic).
entries.弓: Pictogram – a bow. See also the original version of 射. Unrelated to 弗. See also 夷.
entries.弔: In the oracle bone script, a person with a corded arrow wound around the body; an ideogram of 約.
entries.引:
Compound ideogram: 弓 (bow) + 丿 (indicatory stroke)

Oracle-bone and bronze forms depict a (often slack) bow with a short slant stroke added as an indicatory mark; it most likely marks the place/line of drawing the bow (i.e. pulling the string), hence the basic meaning “to pull; to draw (a bow)”. A newer view takes the stroke as pointing to the bow’s curved section (弓淵) and derives “to draw” secondarily, but this remains less certain.
entries.弗:
Pictogram – rope wrapped around two pieces of wood to keep them straight.

Later borrowed phonetically to mean “no”. The derivative 拂 stands for the original word.
entries.弘:
Compound ideogram: 弓 (bow, phonetic) + 口 (mouth, semantic) – the sound of a bow > a loud sound.

The 口 later corrupts into 厶 (the ancient form of 肱), which Shuowen interprets to be the phonetic component of the character.
entries.弟: Pictogram – of a spear handle wrapped in a leather strap. The wrapping signified order or sequence, which extended to "younger brother".
entries.弥:
Phono-semantic compound: 弓 (bow, semantic) + 尔 (phonetic)

Usage recorded as early the 6th century, found in the Yupians:玉篇 (四庫全書本)/卷29, which was used interchangeably with 彌.
entries.弦: Phono-semantic compound: 弓 (bow, semantic) + 玄 (phonetic).
entries.弧: Phono-semantic compound: 弓 (bow, semantic) + 瓜 (phonetic). It refers to a bow made of wood, and by extension, expresses the idea of bending like a bow.
entries.弩: Phono-semantic compound: 奴 (phonetic) + 弓 (bow, semantic).
entries.弭: Phono-semantic compound: 弓 (bow, semantic) + 耳 (phonetic).
entries.弱:
Compound ideogram: 弓 (bow) + 彡 (hair, meaning "decoration" in this case)—a decorative bow that is functionally inferior. Or it might be indicating that the bow is shaking, which implies a worn-out bow. 

An alternate etymology is 𢎥 + 𢎥, 𢎥 being a variant of 卷.
entries.張: Phono-semantic compound: 弓 (bow, semantic) + 長 (phonetic).
entries.強: A Phono-semantic compound: semantic 虫 and phonetic 𪪺.
entries.强: Variant form of 強*. Already appeared in the Han Dynasty in Zhong Yao's "Jian Ji Zhi Biao".
entries.彄: Phono-semantic compound: 弓 (bow, semantic) + 區 (phonetic)
entries.彆: Phono-semantic compound: 敝 (phonetic) + 弓 (bow, semantic).
entries.彊:
Phono-semantic compound: 弓 (bow, semantic) + 畺 (phonetic).

Bow is powerful.
entries.彋: Phono-semantic compound: 弓 (bow, semantic) + 睘 (phonetic)
entries.彎: Phono-semantic compound: 弓 (bow, semantic) + 䜌 (phonetic).
entries.彐:
A variant of 彑 ("pig snout"). But in many characters, such as 事, 尹, 雪, and 爭 it depicts a hand holding something. The hand is stylized since it only has three fingers instead of five (see 又, with three fingers, and 止, a footprint with three toes). Unrelated to 录, in which it represents a cloth filter for water, and 庚 (as well as to its derivative 康. See also 丑, which represents an animal paw.

The only characters in which a similar shape represents a wild boar (not a domestic pig) are the ancient variants of 敢.
entries.归:
Unorthodox variant Simplified from 歸. found in various Movable type#Metal movable type in China copies of Classic Chinese Novels. First attested in 《宋元以來俗字譜》, a Variant Chinese character dictionary compiled in 1930 that records unorthodox forms (俗字) that have existed since the Song dynasty. 

Originally part of the 324 simplified characters introduced by the Republic of China (Kuomintang government) in 1935 but was later retracted in 1936. 

Eventually adopted as an official simplified character by the People's Republic of China in the 1956 Chinese Character Simplification Scheme.
entries.当: Unorthodox variant of 當. From cursive script (East Asia).
entries.彔: Pictogram: a pictogram of a well windlass drawing water; the original pictographic form of 轆 in 轆轤.
entries.彗: Compound ideogram: 甡 (broom) + 又 (hand) – to hold a broom which is made of bamboo.
entries.彘: Compound ideogram: 豕 (pig; boar, semantic) + 矢 (arrow, phonetic) – a wild boar being shot by an arrow (as opposed to a domesticated pig)
entries.彝: Compound ideogram: 彑 (head, phonetic) + 米 (rice, semantic) + 糸 (silk, semantic) + 廾 (two hands, semantic) – a bird or slave with its wings or hands tied, offered for sacrifice with two hands. The bird or slave's head is represented by 彑, the body now by 米 (no connection to “rice”), the string that ties the wings or hands by 糸, and the two hands by 廾. The 彑 component is stated to be a phonetic in Shuowen.
entries.彠: Phono-semantic compound: 尋 (unit of length, semantic) + 蒦 (phonetic).
entries.彡:
Pictogram: three strands of hair. See also ⾽, 而, 冄, and 㐱.

However, in two characters, it indicates three light rays: in 昜 they represent sunrays while in 參 they represent the light rays of three stars.

The character today means "ornament", hence it is partly related to 丯 (incisions), 彭 (sound vibrations coming from a drum), and 影 (shadow). The three traits in 鬱 are simply decorative.
entries.形:
Phono-semantic compound: 井 (phonetic) + 彡 (semantic).

Originally written as 刑 in ancient texts. Based on the corrupted form of 井, Shuowen mistakes 幵 to be the phonetic component. The variant form 𢒈, which preserves the original phonetic component, is found in tombstones from the Han dynasty and Wei (state) times.
entries.彣: Phono-semantic compound: 文 (phonetic) + 彡 (decorative lines, ornament, semantic). The character can be split in two to coin 彥.
entries.彥: Phono-semantic compound: 厂 (phonetic) + 彣 (variegated; literary talent, semantic)
entries.彫: Phono-semantic compound: 彡 (representing patterns or ornamentation, semantic) + 周 (phonetic). It represents the act of carving patterns, and by extension, conveys the meaning "to engrave" or "to carve."
entries.彬:
Phono-semantic compound: 焚 (phonetic) + 彡 (semantic).

Alternatively may be Phono-semantic compound: 棼 (phonetic) + 彡 (semantic).
entries.彭:
Compound ideogram: 壴 (drum) + 彡 (visualization of the sound of drumming) – sound of drumming.

Shuowen considers it to be a Phono-semantic compound – where 彡 acts as the phonetic component.
entries.彰: Phono-semantic compound: 章 (emblem, phonetic) + 彡 (colorful patterns, semantic) – conspicuous.
entries.影: Phono-semantic compound: 景 (phonetic) + 彡 (semantic). The original meaning is "shadow". The phonetic component also indicates the concept of image.
entries.彳: Simplified from 行. – the left side of the character, which represents a street intersection as seen from above. See also the top component of 辵.
entries.役: Compound ideogram: 彳 (movement; action, semantic) + 殳 (a weapon, like a spear, semantic). The character originally depicted guarding a border with a weapon in hand, and by extension, it came to represent the idea of performing a duty or task.
entries.往:
Originally 㞷/𫭠, a Phono-semantic compound: 止 (foot, semantic) + 王 (phonetic); see also the top component of 出. Later 彳 was added to form 𢓸, a Phono-semantic compound: 彳 (to step, semantic) + 止 (foot, semantic) + 王 (phonetic). Eventually, the right component was stylized into the unrelated 主. The footprint 屮 pointing upwards on top became a point as in the character 之.

See also 迋.
entries.径: Simplified from 徑. based on the table of 54 simplified radical components listed in the 1956 Chinese Character Simplification Scheme by the People's Republic of China.
entries.後:
In oracle bone script, Compound ideogram: 幺 (thread) + 夊 (foot) – a foot bound by a rope, thus lagging behind. The component 彳 was added afterwards to emphasize this action.

Note that the simplified form 后 is also a traditional character on its own, with a different meaning.
entries.徐: Phono-semantic compound: 彳 (walk slowly, semantic) + 余 (phonetic)
entries.徒: Small seal script: Phono-semantic compound: 辵 (walk, semantic) + 土 (phonetic). Later corrupted into 彳 + 走.
entries.従: Unorthodox variant Simplified from 從. found in the Tang dynasty orthographic dictionary Ganlu Zishu (干祿字書).
entries.徛: Phono-semantic compound: 彳 (to walk with small steps, semantic) + 奇 (phonetic).
entries.從: Originally written as 从. Now Phono-semantic compound: 辵 (walk, semantic) + 从 (follow, phonetic).
entries.御: Oracle bone script: Phono-semantic compound: 午 (phonetic) + 卩 (kneeling person, semantic) – govern. Bronze inscriptions added 彳 and 止 to emphasize action.
entries.復:
Phono-semantic compound: 彳 (walk, semantic) + 复 (repeat, phonetic).

Walk back and forth.
entries.循: Phono-semantic compound: 彳 (movement, semantic) + 盾 (phonetic) – to follow (movement).
entries.微:
In oracle bone script, it may be written as 𡵂 or 𢼸. 

The former is a variant of 美, borrowed for sound, Pictogram – of a person with long hair. 

The latter an Compound ideogram: 美 (phonetic) + 攴 (hand with tool, semantic) – splitting or combing hairs; minute. Possibly the original form of 媺. 

彳 was added to emphasize action to create the modern form.
entries.徳: 徳 evolved naturally from earlier forms of the Chinese script; 德 was reintroduced via knowledge that 徳/德 etymologically contains 直 as a component.
entries.徵:
Compound ideogram: 彳 + 𭖒 + 攵 – originally meaning punishment.

Originally written as 𭖒 in oracle bone script; Pictogram – of a knife with tooth-shaped protrusions on the back. Variants which added 止 were common. In bronze inscriptions, 彳 was often added to the character as well. In bamboo slips, 止 was replaced with 攵, arriving at the modern form.
entries.德:
Phono-semantic compound: 彳 (semantic) + 直 (phonetic) + 心 (semantic).

The sense “virtue” is first attested in early Western Zhou Chinese bronze inscriptions, where the word may also be written 徝, without 心. It typically refers to the virtue of King Wen and the former kings, to be emulated, received or revered: 文王徝赫赫 (“King Wen's virtue is resplendent”, 天亡簋); 今我唯即型稟于玟王正德 (“now I approach the upright virtue of King Wen to emulate and receive it”, Da Yu ding); 助王龏德，欲天臨我不敏 (“help the king revere virtue, that Heaven may look down on me, the unworthy”, He zun).

In oracle bone script, 徝 (also with 行 in place of 彳; written 直 by some diviner groups) usually means “(of the king) to proceed to; to march on”, with a place (中商) or a polity (土方, 羌) as its goal. With an ancestor as its goal it denotes a ritual approach, or a dead king joining a senior one: 王求直大甲 (“the king seeks to go to Da Jia”, Heji 32301); 父乙徝祖乙 (“Father Yi proceeds to Zu Yi”, Heji 1660), cf. 父乙賓于祖乙 (“Father Yi is received as a guest by Zu Yi”, Heji 1657) and 下乙賓于帝 (“Xia Yi (= Zu Yi) is received by Di”, Heji 1402). Such approaches awaited the approval (若) of ancestors and spirits: 祖丁唯徝若于王 (“will Zu Ding approve the king's going?”, Heji 1854). In the Da Yu ding passage, 即 “to approach”, also used of ancestors in oracle bones (即于上甲, Tunnan 2322), takes King Wen's virtue rather than King Wen himself as its goal; the He zun likewise ties virtue to Heaven's favour, as 徝 was tied to the spirits'
entries.徹:
Oracle bone inscriptions: Compound ideogram: 鬲 (pot) + 又 (hand) – a hand removing utensils after eating. Bronze inscriptions replaced 又 with 攵 to emphasize action.

In seal script 彳 was added to further emphasize action, and what was originally a pot had corrupted into the unrelated 育.
entries.徽: Phono-semantic compound: 微 (phonetic) + 糸 (cloth, semantic).
entries.心: Pictogram – a heart, now highly stylized.
entries.忄: Variant of 心, when used as left radical (compare 㣺).
entries.忆: Simplified from 憶. Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 乙 (phonetic).
entries.忉: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 刀 (phonetic).
entries.忌: Phono-semantic compound: 己 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.忍: Phono-semantic compound: 刃 (blade, phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.忏: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 千 (phonetic).
entries.忐: Compound ideogram: 上 (up) + 心 (heart). Compare 忑.
entries.志:
Phono-semantic compound: 之 (phonetic) + 心 (semantic).

Note that the top has been simplified and is now graphically 士.
entries.応: Japanese shinjitai character. Simplified from 應.
entries.忝: Phono-semantic compound: 天 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic)
entries.忠: Phono-semantic compound: 中 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.忤: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 午 (phonetic)
entries.忮: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 支 (phonetic).
entries.忰: Unorthodox variant of 悴. The phonetic component 卆 is a variant of 卒.
entries.念:
Zhang (2021): Compound ideogram: 今 (upside-down mouth) + 心 (heart): to listen to one's heart. Original character for 念.

Shuowen interprets 今 to be a phonetic component, but the Old Chinese phonetics do not match.
entries.忻: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 斤 (phonetic).
entries.忼: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 亢 (phonetic).
entries.忽: Phono-semantic compound: 勿 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic). Folk etymology interprets it as an ideogrammic compound.
entries.态: Simplified from 態. Phono-semantic compound: 太 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.怎: Phono-semantic compound: 乍 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.怒: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 奴 (slave, phonetic) – angry.
entries.怔: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 正 (phonetic)
entries.怕: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 白 (phonetic).
entries.怖: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 布 (phonetic). It conveys the meaning of "to fear" or "to be afraid."
entries.思:
Original form was 恖, considered by Shuowen to be a Phono-semantic compound: 囟 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic). It may also be a Compound ideogram: 囟 (fontanel) + 心 (heart).

囟 started to corrupt into the unrelated 田 as early as the silk script.
entries.怠: Phono-semantic compound: 台 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.怡: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 台 (phonetic).
entries.急: Phono-semantic compound: 及 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.怦: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 平 (phonetic).
entries.性: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 生 (phonetic) – nature, personal quality, hence of the heart.
entries.怨: Phono-semantic compound: 夗 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.怵: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 朮 (phonetic).
entries.怹: Compound ideogram: 他 (he; she) + 心 (heart). Compare 您.
entries.怺: Kokuji (created in Japan). Compound ideogram: 心 (heart) + 永 (eternal).
entries.总: As simplified Chinese, from 縂 with 糸 omitted; in turn, it derives from a simplification of 總. First attested in 《宋元以來俗字譜》, a Variant Chinese character dictionary compiled in 1930 that records unorthodox forms (俗字) that have existed since the Song dynasty.
entries.恁: Phono-semantic compound: 任 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.恃: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 寺 (phonetic)
entries.恆:
Compound ideogram: 心 (heart, semantic) + 亙 (partial moon, phonetic).

May have originally been written 亙.

In Small Seal Script, the 月 in 亙 was written 舟.
entries.恇: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 匡 (phonetic).
entries.恍: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 光 (phonetic). This character replaced 怳's usage in the late Middle Chinese.
entries.恐: In the Shuowen Jiezi appears as Phono-semantic compound: 𢀜 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic). The modern form can be interpreted as Phono-semantic compound: 巩 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic)
entries.恕: Phono-semantic compound: 如 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.恢: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 灰 (phonetic).
entries.恤: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 血 (phonetic).
entries.恥: Phono-semantic compound: 耳 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic)
entries.恧: Phono-semantic compound: 而 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.恨: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart; thought; emotion, semantic) + 艮 (phonetic).
entries.恩: Phono-semantic compound: 因 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.恪: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 各 (phonetic).
entries.恬: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 甜 (phonetic).
entries.恭: Shuowen: Phono-semantic compound: 共 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic)
entries.息: Compound ideogram: 自 (nose) + 心 (heart) – to breathe (life) through one’s nose. Note that 自 originally meant “nose” and was later borrowed for “self”.
entries.恵: Simplified from 惠.; compare 専.
entries.恿: Phono-semantic compound: 甬 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.悀: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 甬 (phonetic)
entries.悄: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 肖 (phonetic).
entries.悅:
Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 兌 (phonetic).

Often written as 說 in pre-Qin texts.
entries.悉: Compound ideogram: 釆 (to distinguish) + 心 (heart) – detailed.
entries.悌: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 弟 (phonetic). Often written as 弟 in Pre-Qin classics.
entries.悕: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 希 (phonetic)
entries.悠: Phono-semantic compound: 攸 (phonetic) + 心 (heart; mind, semantic)
entries.患:
Phono-semantic compound: 串 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).

Since Shuowen does not have the character 串, it interprets the character as 吅 (phonetic) + 丨 (semantic) + 心 (heart, semantic) – to pierce through something from the heart. Duan Yucai claims in his commentary that older copies of Shuowen actually have 毌 (to pierce through, phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic) instead.
entries.悤:
The original form shows a heart (心) with a big dot on top. Qiu Xigui (裘錫圭) and Shen Pei (沈培) see the dot indicating a hole and hence its original meaning was "intelligent" (聰) – it's a traditional Chinese idea to describe intelligence as holes on the heart.

The thick dot evolved into a patterned shape 囪 in Han dynasty. For a similar phenomenon, compare 山 in Han dynasty, which also variantly has a solid filling or a patterned filling.

The character then changed meaning perhaps due to a proximity of meaning (learn fastly > hastily), but the original meaning is preserved into 聰.
entries.悦: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 兌 (phonetic). It expresses the meaning of being delighted.
entries.悰: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 宗 (phonetic)
entries.悲: Phono-semantic compound: 非 (phonetic) + 心 (heart; thought; emotion, semantic).
entries.悸: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 季 (phonetic).
entries.惀: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 侖 (phonetic).
entries.情: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 青 (phonetic).
entries.惊: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 京 (phonetic).
entries.惌: Phono-semantic compound: 宛 (phonetic) + 心 (heart; mind, semantic).
entries.惏: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 林 (phonetic).
entries.惑: Phono-semantic compound: 或 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.惘: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 罔 (phonetic).
entries.惜:
Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 昔 (phonetic) – a feeling (of the heart).

Note that 昔 has meaning of “past, ending”, hence connotations of “feelings for the past, feeling about an ending – regret, rue”.
entries.惠: Compound ideogram: 叀 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic). Originally also written 叀.
entries.惡:
Phono-semantic compound: 亞 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).

惡 may also be compared with 於 and 嗚 (“exclamation”), 歍 (“to vomit; to feel nauseous”), and 汙 and 淤 (“filthy; stagnant”).
entries.惦: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 店 (phonetic).
entries.惧: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 具 (phonetic). Originally, it was a popular variant of 懼.
entries.惰: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart; mind, semantic) + 隋 (phonetic).
entries.惲: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 軍 (phonetic).
entries.想: Phono-semantic compound: 相 (to look at, phonetic) + 心 (heart, mind, semantic) – to think, to consider.
entries.愁: Phono-semantic compound: 秋 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic)
entries.愆: Phono-semantic compound: 衍 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.愊: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 畐 (phonetic).
entries.意: Modern form is a compound of 音 and 心. However, the top component is etymologically unrelated to 音. According to, 𠶷 (a compound of 言* and 中*) found in bronze inscriptions is the same character as 意.
entries.愐: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 面 (phonetic).
entries.愚: Phono-semantic compound: 禺 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic) – stupid.
entries.愛:
Originally written as 㤅. Phono-semantic compound: 旡 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).

As early as the Qin dynasty, a redundant component 夊 was added to the bottom of the character, as with some other characters depicting people. Compare 憂 (from 㥑). Hence, the character changed into 𢙴.

Further corruption of the top component of 𢙴 turned the original phonetic 旡 into ⿱爫冖.
entries.愜: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 匧 (phonetic).
entries.感: Phono-semantic compound: 咸 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.愠:
An unorthodox variant Simplified from 慍. which can be found in the historical Longkan Shoujian (龍龕手鑑) dictionary compiled in 997 AD.

Eventually adopted as an official form by the People's Republic of China in 1965 based on the Xin Zixing (新字形) standardized form of characters.
entries.愣: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 楞 (phonetic).
entries.愧:
Originally written 媿. In the modern form, a Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 鬼 (phonetic).

Shuowen interprets the character as an Compound ideogram: 恥 (shame) + 鬼 (spirit).
entries.愩: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 貢 (phonetic).
entries.愬: Phono-semantic compound: 朔 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.愴: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 倉 (phonetic).
entries.愷: Compound ideogram: 心 (heart, semantic) + 豈 (drum, phonetic). Likely related to 凱//豈.
entries.愽: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 尃 (phonetic).
entries.愿: Phono-semantic compound: 原 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.慃: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 翁 (phonetic).
entries.慄: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 栗 (phonetic). It expresses the meaning of fearing.
entries.慇: Phono-semantic compound: 殷 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.慈: Phono-semantic compound: 茲 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.態: Phono-semantic compound: 能 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic) – one’s heart-felt attitude.
entries.慌: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 荒 (phonetic).
entries.慕: Phono-semantic compound: 莫 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.慘: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 參 (phonetic)
entries.慙: Phono-semantic compound: 斬 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.慚: Phono-semantic compound: 斬 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.慢: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 曼 (phonetic).
entries.慣: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 貫 (phonetic) – habit is what one does by heart.
entries.慥: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 造 (phonetic)
entries.慧: Phono-semantic compound: 彗 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.慨: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 既 (phonetic).
entries.慫: Phono-semantic compound: 從 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.慬: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 堇 (phonetic).
entries.慮: Phono-semantic compound: 思 (to think, semantic) + 虍 (phonetic).
entries.慶:
In oracle bone inscriptions Compound ideogram: 廌 (antelope) + 心. The component 心 signified goodness, blessings and auspiciousness. 

In bronze inscriptions 心 is often also written as 文. During the Warring states period, the tail of 廌 corrupted into 个, then further into 夂 during the Qin dynasty. Based on the overlap between the many ancient variants of the character suggests that 麕, 廌, 麐, 鹿 all refer to kinds of deer – beautiful and therefore worth celebrating when obtained. He also concludes that there is enough evidence that 慶 and 麐 were once the same character. Since 麐 was the most precious among deer, its character was used to express celebration.
entries.慷: Originally written as 忼. Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 康 (phonetic).
entries.慺: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 婁 (phonetic).
entries.慾: Phono-semantic compound: 欲 (phonetic) + 心 (semantic) – to lust with one’s heart.
entries.憋: Phono-semantic compound: 敝 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.憎: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 曾 (phonetic).
entries.憐: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 粦 (phonetic).
entries.憚: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 單 (phonetic).
entries.憤: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 賁 (phonetic).
entries.憧: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 童 (phonetic).
entries.憬: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 景 (phonetic).
entries.憭: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 尞 (phonetic).
entries.憲: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 𡩜 (a form of punishment involving tattooing the eyes, phonetic). The character conveys the meaning of "law" or "rule."
entries.憶: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 意 (thought, phonetic).
entries.憻: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 亶 (phonetic)
entries.懁: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 睘 (phonetic)
entries.懂: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 董 (phonetic).
entries.懃: Phono-semantic compound: 勤 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.懄: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 勤 (phonetic).
entries.懇: Phono-semantic compound: 貇 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.應: Phono-semantic compound: 䧹 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.懊: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 奧 (phonetic).
entries.懌: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 睪 (phonetic)
entries.懍: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, emotions, semantic) + 稟 (phonetic).
entries.懕: Phono-semantic compound: 厭 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.懟: Phono-semantic compound: 對 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.懦: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 需 (phonetic).
entries.懪: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, mind, semantic) + 暴 (phonetic). However, the phonetic component means "violence", so it could add part of the meaning. A conservative version is 𢥟; later, the whole character was stylized into 懪.
entries.懬: Phono-semantic compound: 廣 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.懵: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 瞢 (phonetic).
entries.懶: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 賴 (phonetic).
entries.懷: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 褱 (to miss; bosom, phonetic). The original meaning is "to miss, to long for". Originally written 褱, see there for more.
entries.懸: Phono-semantic compound: 縣 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic). 縣 originally referred to this word; 心 was added later for distinguishment.
entries.懺: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 韱 (phonetic).
entries.懾: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 聶 (phonetic).
entries.戀: Phono-semantic compound: 䜌 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.戉: Pictogram – a battle axe, the original form of 鉞. Almost identical to 戌.
entries.戌: Pictogram – of an axe or halberd, almost identical to 戊 and similar to 戈.
entries.戎: Compound ideogram: 甲 (shield) + 戈 (halberd; weapons) – weaponry, arms.
entries.成: Phono-semantic compound: 戊 (semantic) + 丁 (phonetic). The phonetic component is not 囗 or 口, as folk etymology states. According to Ji Xusheng 季旭昇, its original meaning was "city walls", with a reference to something protected conveyed by the weapon. Its original meaning is preserved in 城.
entries.戒: Compound ideogram: 戈 (halberd) + 廾 (hands) – to hold up a weapon as warning.
entries.戓: Compound ideogram: 戈 (dagger-axe (used to defend the territory)) + 囗 (city wall), “territory”.
entries.戕: Phono-semantic compound: 爿 (phonetic) + 戈 (dagger-axe, semantic)
entries.或: Phono-semantic compound: 戈 (semantic) + 員 (circle, phonetic)
entries.战:
Simplified from 戰.

Phono-semantic compound: 占 (phonetic) + 戈 (semantic).
entries.戚: Phono-semantic compound: 戊 (scythe, semantic) + 尗 (phonetic) – in early sense, a battle-axe, a kind of cutting weapon. Later borrowed to mean "relative".
entries.戟: Simplified from 𢧢., an Compound ideogram: 榦 (branch) + 戈 (dagger-axe), in which 榦* was reduced to 倝*.
entries.戠: Compound ideogram: 音 + 戈 (the second component was originally 弋, a wooden pole with a pointed end to be implanted in the ground and not a weapon). The original meaning is preserved in the character 樴, also written as 杙.
entries.戡: Phono-semantic compound: 甚 (phonetic) + 戈 (dagger-axe, semantic)
entries.戭: Phono-semantic compound: 寅 (phonetic) + 戈 (spear, semantic).
entries.戮: Phono-semantic compound: 翏 (phonetic) + 戈 (dagger axe, semantic).
entries.戰: Phono-semantic compound: 單 (phonetic) + 戈 (halberd, semantic) – battling with a halberd.
entries.戱: Phono-semantic compound: 虛 (phonetic) + 戈 (halberd, semantic).
entries.戲: Phono-semantic compound: 䖒 (phonetic) + 戈 (halberd, semantic), originally referring to the wing or flank of an army.
entries.戵: Phono-semantic compound: 瞿 (phonetic) + 戈 (spear, semantic).
entries.戶: Pictogram: one-half of 門. The character in its original form is similar to 𠁣.
entries.戻: Simplified from 戾. Compound ideogram: 戶 (door, semantic) + 犬 (dog, semantic). It depicts a dog twisting its body to slip under a door, which came to convey the meanings “to return” or “to reach/arrive.” The modern commonly used character is a simplified form.
entries.戾: Compound ideogram: a dog 犬 bending to enter through a door 戶 – to bend over. Extended to mean crooked, deviant, contrary.
entries.房:
Phono-semantic compound: 戶 (door, semantic) + 方 (phonetic).

The meaning of 方 'side' can also play a role, if the character originally referred to one of the two rooms beside the central room (side room).
entries.所: Phono-semantic compound: 戶 (phonetic) + 斤 (axe, semantic) – the sound of logging (the definition given in Shuowen).
entries.扁: Compound ideogram: 戶 (door) + 冊 (bamboo tablets) – to inscribe on the door, or two things that are flat and thin.
entries.扈: Phono-semantic compound: 戸 (phonetic) + 邑 (area, semantic).
entries.手:
Pictogram – hand and fingers. The top stroke is the bent over middle finger, while the horizontal strokes are each two fingers. Compare 爪, 寸, 九, 又, and 彐 as a stylized hand. Compare 丑 as an animal claw. See also the bottom part of 舉 and 奉.

Note that unlike the other hand/claw characters, 手 has consistently had five fingers: a mammalian/human hand, as opposed to the three digits often found in the others.

Compare also 止, derived from a footprint pointing upward, originally composed of 3 toes and a sole.
entries.扌: Derived from its seal script form,.
entries.才:
Pictogram – a sharp peg. Same as 弋 and 尗. The sense "talent" is via an early phonetic loan. See also the top component of 𢦏.

Xu Shen erroneously analyzed this character as a sprout growing from the ground.
entries.扑:
Phono-semantic compound: 手 (hand, semantic) + 卜 (phonetic).

entries.支:
Compound ideogram: 又 (hand) + 竹 ((half of 竹) branch of bamboo) – a branch.

entries.攰: Compound ideogram: 支 (limb) + 力 (strength) – reminiscent of the idiom 體力不支.
entries.攴:
Pictogram: a hand (又) holding a tool of some sort (possibly a weapon or whip), meaning “to hit”. The tool later corrupted into the phonetic component 卜. Today, the character is mostly stylized except in some archaic variants.

Similar but unrelated to 支, 伊, and 父. The stylized version is unrelated to 囱 (> 窗) and 文.
entries.收: Phono-semantic compound: 攴 (semantic) + 丩 (phonetic) – to arrest.
entries.改:
In the oracle bone script, a Phono-semantic compound: 巳 (phonetic) + 攴 (semantic).

The interpretation linked to a child beaten or threatened by a stick in hand to indicate "correct, amend" referred to educating a child is probably folk etymology.

Since the small seal script, the phonetic component has been changed to 己.
