entries.敏: Phono-semantic compound: 每 (phonetic) + 攴 (hand; action, semantic). The 攴 component was sometimes written as 又 in early writing.
entries.敔: Phono-semantic compound: 吾 (phonetic) + 攴 (to rap, hit, semantic).
entries.敕: Compound ideogram: 柬 + 攴 (a stick in hand that represents authority) – to warn. The left component, according to Zhang Shichao (張世超), is the contraction of 熏. In the Small Seal script, it was sometimes written as 束.
entries.敖:
Originally 𫠤, a Pictogram – depicting a person 人 with a headdress similar to 屮 and then 丰 and 出 (but unrelated to these character). Later, the person was stylized to a shape similar to 夭 (a man running); 攴 was added perhaps to convey the concept of authority, making it a and transforming it into 𢾍. The man under the headress then become stylized as 方 (or 万 in some modern scripts). See also 免, 冒, and 美.

As an alternative, according to 季旭昇 Ji Xusheng, it represents a man walking and travelling in the countryside, symbolized by a sprout 屮 on top. See also the original form of 每.

Shuowen Jiezi erroneously interprets it as an Compound ideogram: 出 (leave) + 放 (release) due to the later stylization.
entries.敗: Phono-semantic compound: 貝 (phonetic) + 攴 (strike, semantic).
entries.教:
Simplified from 敎.

Phono-semantic compound: 爻 (phonetic) + 子 (child, semantic) + 攴 (teaching cane; stick that represents authority, semantic) – teaching a child. See also 學 and 算.
entries.敝:
Compound ideogram: 巾 (cloth) + 攴 (hand holding a wooden stick) – a hand hitting a piece of cloth with a stick.

Sometimes dots were added around the cloth, producing 㡀 as seen in the modern form. The dots could represent dust or dirt, in which case the character means to beat a cloth with a stick to clean it from dust. Alternatively, the dots could represent broken pieces of cloth, suggesting the meaning of “worn out, tattered,” but evidence of this sense does not appear until the seal script.

Unrelated to 黹.
entries.敢:
Compound ideogram: a hand (又) using a capturing tool (𰅱) to hunt a wild boar (豕). Later, 𰅱 was omitted and a redundant component 口 or 甘 was added (Chen Jian, 2020; Xie Mingwen, 2020). 

The components eventually corrupted into the modern form.
entries.散:
The original version visible on oracle bone script is 㪔, hence Compound ideogram: 林 (trees, forest) + 攴 (to knock, to tap), also written with hemp stalks 𣏟 (> 𢽳) or bamboo 竹 instead of two trees. The original meanings are "to clear a place from vegetation; to kill". The character later started meaning "to dissipate, to disperse" since bamboo in particular breaks easily into pieces; eventually, the meaning shifted to "to walk around, to stroll".

Shuowen: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (semantic) + 𢽳 (phonetic), written as 𣀙, in which 林 is well visible on top.
entries.敦:
Originally written 𦎫 in oracle bone script and bronze script, an Compound ideogram: 亯 (ancestral shrine) + 羊 (sheep). According to Ma Rusen (馬如森), the character represents a cooked goat used as a sacrifice. According to Ma Xulun (馬敍倫) and Yang Shuda (楊樹達), the character's original meanings was "to cook" and is the original form of 燉.

Later used to mean “to force; to compel” and came to be written with 攴, making the modern form an Compound ideogram: 𦎫 (phonetic) + 攴 (hand, semantic). The character 燉 was graphically shaped after the modern version.
entries.敫: Shuowen: Compound ideogram: 白 (white) + 放 (to release) – “to shine”. Possibly the original form of 皦.
entries.敬: Possibly Compound ideogram: 茍 (kneeling person or sitting dog) + 攴 (hand holding a stick, authority).
entries.数: Unorthodox variant of 數*, attested since Ming dynasty. Simplified from 數.
entries.敲: Phono-semantic compound: 高 (phonetic) + 攴 (to hit lightly; to tap, semantic).
entries.敵: Phono-semantic compound: 啻 (phonetic) + 攴 (to tap; to hit, semantic).
entries.敷: Variant form of 𢾭. Phono-semantic compound: 尃 (distribute, phonetic) + 攴 (hand with whip; action, semantic). The bottom left 寸 has been replaced with 方.
entries.敺: Phono-semantic compound: 區 (phonetic) + 攴 (to rap, hit, semantic). Original form of 驅.
entries.斃: Phono-semantic compound: 敝 (phonetic) + 死 (death, semantic).
entries.文:
Ideogram: a man with a painted or tattooed chest – original form of 紋. The tattoo was usually a cross, a V shape or a stylized heart. In the current form, the tattoo has vanished, making it simply an outline of a man (head, outstretched arms, legs, chest) similar to 立. Compare 大, which has no chest.

Unrelated to the Kangxi radicals 齐 and 攵.
entries.斈: Variant (俗字) of 学. First specified in JIS X 0208.
entries.斉:
Variant of 齊.

Unrelated to 文, but currently classified under that radical.
entries.斑: Phono-semantic compound: 文 (pattern, semantic) + 班 (phonetic).
entries.斗: Pictogram – (Shuowen), indicating a ladle-shaped dipper or cup used to measure grain (see below) held by hand. See also 升.
entries.料: Compound ideogram: 米 (rice) + 斗 (dipper) – to measure; to gauge.
entries.斜: Phono-semantic compound: 斗 (ladle/dipper, semantic) + 余 (phonetic). The character expresses the idea of scooping or drawing out. By extension, it is also used to mean "slant" or "diagonal."
entries.斟: Phono-semantic compound: 甚 (phonetic) + 斗 (dipper; cup, semantic).
entries.斥:
Originally written 㡿, a Phono-semantic compound: 广 (building, semantic) + 屰 (phonetic).

The 屰 later came to be written 干, and the 广 was sometimes written as 厂, eventually leading to the modern form of the character.

Alternatively, may be derived from 宅.
entries.斧: Phono-semantic compound: 父 (phonetic) + 斤 (axe, semantic)
entries.斨: Phono-semantic compound: 爿 (phonetic) + 斤 (axe, semantic)
entries.斬: Compound ideogram: 斤 (axe, semantic) + 車 (cart; vehicle, semantic). It refers to an ancient punishment in which a body was torn apart using carts, and by extension, conveys the meaning “to cut.” Another theory expresses the idea of cutting wood to make a vehicle.
entries.斯: In the late Western Zhou bronze inscription on the 禹鼎, the character is composed of 斤 and possibly a phonetic element similar to “⿱凶二”, unrelated to 其 or 齒. It may be read as 廝 (the “凶” shape may be an ideograph for 策/筴 meaning “small basket”). In Spring and Autumn period Qi bronze inscriptions and Warring States Chu script, the component was graphically assimilated to “⿱𠚕丌” and “⿰⿱𠚕丌斤” (from the initial form of 齒).
entries.斳: Phono-semantic compound: 堇 (phonetic) + 斤 (axe, semantic).
entries.斷:
Compound ideogram: 𢇍 (to cut) + 斤 (axe).

Before the Qin dynasty, this character was written as 𠸿 or 𠜷. According to Shuowen, the left component is an old form of 叀.
entries.方:
Possibly the original character of 旁, with its form related to 巫. 巫 depicts four extremities with indicator symbols, being the original character of 荒 in 四荒. Compared to 巫, one end of this character lacks the indicator symbol and is elongated to denote "side" 旁. 方 in 四方 and 荒 in 四荒 may be cognates.

It is unrelated to 㫃, from which characters like 旗 and 旅 are derived.
entries.於: From an ancient variant form of 烏. Not related to 方 or 㫃.
entries.斿: Compound ideogram: 㫃 (flag) + 子 (child) – a child holding a flag (to travel).
entries.旁:
Phono-semantic compound: 同 (semantic) + 方 (phonetic).

The upper component, which perhaps indicates the semantic field, is unclear and has evolved significantly in time, including 冖 (Shang dynasty), 同 (Western Zhou), or forms resembling 辛 (Spring and Autumn period bronze of Wu (state)) or 用 (Warring States period bronze inscription of Wei (state) and proto-clerical script of Qin (state)). In the Chu Silk Manuscript the form was much simplified.

The modern form was a descendant from the clerical script. Hence, a knife or chisel to mark prisoners 辛 is written above the phonetic component 方, perhaps to indicate the concept of moving to remote. However, as already stated, the semantic component in this character is unclear and evolved during time, hence more explanations linked to the earlier versions can be formulated.
entries.旃: Phono-semantic compound: 㫃 (flags flying, semantic) + 丹 (phonetic).
entries.旅: Compound ideogram: 㫃 (flag) + 从 (two people) – brigade.
entries.旋: Compound ideogram: 㫃 (flag) + 止 (foot) + 〇 (circle). 〇 is the original form of 圓 and also serves as a phonetic component. It has since merged with the 止 into the unrelated 疋.
entries.旐: Phono-semantic compound: 㫃 (flag; banner, semantic) + 兆 (phonetic).
entries.旗: Phono-semantic compound: 㫃 (flag, semantic) + 其 (phonetic).
entries.旛: Phono-semantic compound: 㫃 (flag, semantic) + 番 (phonetic)
entries.旜: Phono-semantic compound: 㫃 (flags flying, semantic) + 亶 (phonetic).
entries.无:
One of the three characters (無//, 无//, 亡//) that have historically been used to represent the word "no, not any". First attested in the Warring States period; used interchangeably with 無// until the Tang dynasty. Readopted by the People's Republic of China in 1956.

The origin of this character is unknown. Probably an ancient variant form of either 元, 天 or 堯. This character must not be confused with 旡.
entries.旡: Pictogram – a kneeling figure turning around with mouth open. Compare: 欠, showing another open-mouthed but front-facing figure. The ancient version is 㒫.
entries.既:
Compound ideogram: 皀 (bowl of rice) + 旡 (kneeling figure) – person kneeling at bowl of rice – sitting down to eat (rice already finished cooking), turning away (already finished eating) or abstaining from eating or consuming. 

Note the stroke order in the right component 旡, which may not be clear in the compressed form of this character: the left vertical and second horizontal are one stroke with a corner, while the upper right vertical continues in a diagonal stroke to lower left.
entries.日: Pictogram – the sun. A dot or line was added in the centre to distinguish it from visually similar characters, e.g. 口. Compare earlier forms of the character with the astronomical and astrological symbol for the Sun (☉) and the Egyptian hieroglyph 𓇳.
entries.旦:
Phono-semantic compound: 日 (semantic) + 丁 (phonetic).

According to Shuowen Jiezi, the sun (日) appearing over the horizon (一). However, this version is not the original one and this interpretation belongs to folk etymology. This simplification is the same that appears in 正.

Unrelated to the top component of 得. Also unrelated to 查.
entries.旧:
Variant of 臼.

The reformative usage in simplified Chinese and Japanese that replaced 舊 can be analysed either as from an elimination of 雈 with glyphic alteration from 臼 to 旧 or as using a homophonic character.
entries.旨:
Compound ideogram: 匕 a spoon (匙) to eat or drink something delicious. The original version is 𠤔. See 嘗. Similar but unrelated to 皀.

According to the Shuowen: Phono-semantic compound: 匕 (phonetic) + 甘 (delicious, semantic).
entries.早:
Early bronze inscriptions: Pictogram – acorn. Original form of 皂 through an intermediate variant 皁 (once also written as 草). Borrowed phonetically for "morning" sense.

Late bronze inscriptions: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 棗 (phonetic), with 棗 sometimes simplified as 朿.

Small seal script: Compound ideogram: 日 (sun) + 甲 (first) – when the sun first rises. However, Xu Shen's interpretation is not based on oracle bones and bronzes inscriptions.

In some ancient texts, 蚤 was often used instead.

Unrelated to the ancient version of 是: in this character, it doesn't represent an acorn but a spoon.
entries.旪: Compound ideogram: 曰 (to speak) + 十 (ten) – many voices in harmony.
entries.旬:
Phono-semantic compound: 螾 (phonetic) + 日 (sun; day, semantic).

The pictographic protoform of 螾 was borrowed to represent "period of days" in oracle bone script. In bronze inscriptions, the semantic component 日 was added to this character. In the Warring States period, the phonetic component was mistaken as 勹, hence the incorrect analysis in Shuowen Jiezi of this character as 勹 + 日.
entries.旭: Phono-semantic compound: 九 (phonetic) + 日 (sun, semantic).
entries.旳: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 勺 (phonetic). Later written as 的. Its original meaning is "bright".
entries.时: Variant of 時. From cursive script (East Asia).
entries.旺:
Simplified form of the original 暀, a Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 往 (phonetic).

The current form is reanalyzed as a Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 王 (phonetic).
entries.昂: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 卬 (man standing and man kneeling, phonetic).
entries.昆: Pictogram – the body and legs of an insect.
entries.昇: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 升 (phonetic).
entries.昊:
Compound ideogram: 日 (sun) + 天 (sky) – “the vast sky”.

In seal script written 昦, a

Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 夰 (to release, phonetic).
entries.昌: Compound ideogram: 日 (sun, semantic) + 口 (mouth, semantic). The mouth is a reference to being awakened at dawn through shouts or songs. During the Warring States Period, 口 developed into 曰.
entries.昏: Compound ideogram: 氏 + 日 (sun), or 氐 + 日 (sun). Hence, the twilight or nightfall is the moment in which the sun (日) lowers and goes down (氏).
entries.易:
Oracle bone script and bronze inscriptions: a Pictogram – of a filled container, the original form of 賜. Possibly specialised from 益. Perhaps borrowed phonetically to mean "easy".

The character is not the pictogram of a chameleon, as folk etymology says. Unrelated to 陽 since it doesn't represent the sun.
entries.昔:
Phono-semantic compound: 龷 (phonetic) + 日 (sun; day, semantic). 

The semantic 日 indicates "past days". The phonetic top component originally depicted "rough/wrinkled" or "intertwined" textures; it was an independent character and the original ideogram for 腊 and 皵.

Shuowen: Compound ideogram: 仌 + 日 – two pieces of flesh (仌) dried in the sun (日). Original form of 腊 (dried meat).

Similar but unrelated to 展, 共, and 散.
entries.昜: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 丂 (staff; cane, phonetic).
entries.星: Phono-semantic compound: 晶 (twinkling stars, phonetic) + 生 (phonetic). 晶 originally referred to this word; a phonetic 生 was added later (Ji Xusheng, 2004). 晶 was later simplified into 日.
entries.映: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 央 (phonetic).
entries.春:
Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass, semantic) + 屯 (swollen sprout, phonetic) + 日 (sun, semantic). Some oracle-bone and bronze forms contain only two components, either 艸/屮/木 with 屯, or 日 with 屯. The character may relate to a semantic cluster of its phonetic series: 蠢, 純, 敦, and 芚.

The form 萅 preserves the older arrangement with 艸. In the regular script, the 艸 and 屯 have merged into 𡗗.
entries.昦: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 夰 (release, phonetic). Same as 昊.
entries.昧: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun; day, semantic) + 未 (phonetic).
entries.昨: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 乍 (phonetic). However, the phonetic component could add part of the meaning since it was borrowed phonetically to mean "at first".
entries.昭: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 召 (phonetic).
entries.是: Unclear. Possibly taken from an oracle-bone form of 智, composed of 子, 止 and 冊.
entries.晁: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (semantic) + 兆 (phonetic), appeared as a variant form of 鼂.
entries.時:
Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun; day, semantic) + 之 (to go, phonetic) — the passing of time.

In ancient scripts, it had the form 旹. The phonetic component later changed to 寺.
entries.晉: Compound ideogram: 臸 (to arrive) + 日 (sun)
entries.晙: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 夋 (phonetic).
entries.晝:
Compound ideogram: 聿 + 日 (sun). Used to mean “daytime” in ancient texts.

The significance and meaning of the 聿 component, as present in the oracle bone inscriptions, is not clear. Various theories exist, including that it serves as a phonetic component, in which case the character would be a Phono-semantic compound: 聿 (phonetic) + 日 (sun, semantic).
entries.晡: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 甫 (phonetic)
entries.晦: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 每 (phonetic).
entries.晧: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (white, semantic) + 告 (phonetic).
entries.晨: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 辰 (time, phonetic). Originally written as 辰 alone; 辰 now refers primarily to one of the twelve earthly branches.
entries.普: Compound ideogram: 並 (side by side) + 日 (sun).
entries.景: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 京 (phonetic). Originally, it meant "sunlight". Compare 昜.
entries.晴:
Written as 夝 in Shuowen and as 星 in the Classic of Poetry.

Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 青 (phonetic).
entries.智: Compound ideogram: 大 (adult) + 口 (mouth) + 子 (child) – to transmit knowledge. In western Zhou bronze inscriptions, 甘 started being added. As time went by, 子 corrupted into 于, 大 into 矢, and 甘 into 白, giving rise to the form seen in the Shuowen Jiezi (𥏼). The component 于 was dropped around the Han_dynasty#Western_Han, arriving at the modern form.
entries.暀: Originally written 𣈧, a Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 往 (phonetic).
entries.暄: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 宣 (phonetic).
entries.暇: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 叚 (phonetic)
entries.暈:
Originally a Pictogram – the sun (日) surrounded by lines on all sides – halo.

Now Phono-semantic compound: 日 (Sun, semantic) + 軍 (phonetic).
entries.暉: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (Sun, semantic) + 軍 (phonetic).
entries.暐: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (day; sun, semantic) + 韋 (phonetic)
entries.暖: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 爰 (phonetic). Later also used as a variant of 煖 which is used as another word with different pronunciation.
entries.暗: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 音 (phonetic).
entries.暘: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 昜 (phonetic).
entries.暠: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 高 (phonetic).
entries.暡: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 翁 (phonetic).
entries.暨: Phono-semantic compound: 既 (phonetic) + 旦 (sunrise, semantic).
entries.暮: Phono-semantic compound: 莫 (sunset, phonetic) + 日 (semantic). 莫 is the original pictogram for this word; an additional 日 was added to distinguish.
entries.暴:
Its original form is 𫻺 and can be seen on oracle bone script; Compound ideogram: 虎 (tiger) + 戈 (weapon) – violence. The character also means "to expose to the sun", but its most archaic form does not convey this particular meaning.

However, by the time of bamboo slip script, usage of 𫻺 had been replaced entirely by phonetically borrowing 㬥. This new character originates from the proto-form 𮲡, an Compound ideogram: 日 (sun) + 共 (hands lifting an object); in this precise case, the hands are lifting a plant graphically similar to 丰 or 出. 米 was later added to emphasize the meaning of drying things out in the sun since rice and similar plants can be dried out in the sun. Eventually, the bottom component was stylized as the unrelated 水 and the whole character was stylized into 暴: the plant is no more visible in the new version.

The meaning "to expose to the sun" is preserved in 𣌑 > 曝.
entries.暵: Compound - the radical of the sun 日 and 堇 as a phonetic component; however, the phonetic component is linked to fire and heat since it represents a man burned alive.
entries.暹: Compound ideogram: 日 (sun) + 進 (to advance).
entries.曆: Phono-semantic compound: 厤 (phonetic) + 日 (sun; day, semantic).
entries.曇: Compound ideogram: 日 + 雲, presumably “sun behind clouds”.
entries.曉: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 堯 (phonetic).
entries.曐: Phono-semantic compound: 晶 (twinkling stars, semantic) + 生 (phonetic).
entries.曖: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 愛 (phonetic).
entries.曙: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 暑 (phonetic).
entries.曜: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 翟 (phonetic).
entries.曝: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 暴 (expose, phonetic). Originally, 暴 referred to this word; later, 日 was added to distinguish. A conservative version is 𣌑, then the character was stylized into 曝.
entries.曠: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 廣 (phonetic).
entries.曦: Phono-semantic compound: 日 (sun, semantic) + 羲 (phonetic).
entries.曰: Ideogram: a mouth (口) with word or breath (一) coming out. Compare 言, in which a small stroke on top of a bifurcated tongue (舌) is also used to represent words; see also 四 and 只. Unrelated to 甘.
entries.曲:
Ideogram – a bent object. Also Simplified from 麴. via the variant character 麯.

Unrelated to 曹 and 典.
entries.曳:
Possibly Compound ideogram: 𦥑 (two hands) + 人 (person) – two hands dragging a person. Compare 臾.

Alternatively, Shuowen interprets the character as a Phono-semantic compound: 申 (semantic) + 𠂆 (phonetic).
entries.更: Originally an, showing two chariots (丙). Later 攴 was added and a 丙 omitted to create the form seen in the Shuowen Jiezi (㪅), a Phono-semantic compound: 𰀒 (two chariots, phonetic) + 攴 (hand holding a whip; action, semantic). The remaining 丙 eventually corrupted into a shape similar to 雨.
entries.曷: Shuowen Jiezi: Phono-semantic compound: 匃 (phonetic) + 曰 (semantic)
entries.書: Phono-semantic compound: 聿 (writing brush, semantic) + 者 (phonetic).
entries.曹:
Originally 㯥, an Compound ideogram: two bundles 東. The original meaning is "pair; peer, same kind". Later, 囗 was added as a distinguishing mark, which corrupted into 甘 in bronze inscriptions and 曰 in Seal Script, thus arriving at the intermediate character form 𣍘. The top two 東 have merged and now resemble 曲 with an extra stroke.

Unrelated to 曲 and 典.
entries.曼: Perhaps two hands opening an eye, or two hands over the eyebrows to indicate the eyes looking at a wide place. The second interpretation links this character to the character 看, which has one hand over an eye.
entries.曽: Original form of 曾, used in compound characters such as 増 (from 増).
entries.替: Compound ideogram: 竝 + 曰 – two figures (竝) changing places. Two top components have been simplified from 立 to 夫.
entries.最: Originally 㝡, Phono-semantic compound: 宀 (roof, semantic) + 取 (phonetic) – "to gather". Later 二 was added as distinguishing marks to disambiguate the character for the meaning "the most". The top components have corrupted into 冃 in the traditional form. These components were further corrupted into 曰 in the simplified version.
entries.朁: Phono-semantic compound: 兓 (phonetic) + 口 (semantic). The semantic component was originally 口 in oracle bone script, which later corrupted into 甘 in bronze script, then 曰 in seal script, and finally 日 in standard script.
entries.會: Phono-semantic compound: 合 (to meet, semantic) + 𡆧 (phonetic). 𡆧 is the original form of 𨭗.
entries.有:
Phono-semantic compound: 又 (phonetic) + 肉 (meat, semantic). The hand shape has been abstracted to 𠂇; compare 右, where 又 has also taken this shape. The 肉 in turn has taken the form of ⺼.

The character may have been the original form of 侑. Alternatively, it may be the original form of 醢, which also has the 又 element as phonetic.

Folk etymology traditionally explains it as a hand holding meat, hence “in possession of”. However, the oracle bone script shows no meat.

Shuowen Jiezi and other ancient sources have erroneously analyzed the character as a Phono-semantic compound: 又 (phonetic) + 月 (moon, semantic). Shuowen Jiezi defines 有 as "不宜有也" ("[to have something that] not should be had"), citing the Spring and Autumn Annals (春秋傳): "日月有食之" ("There are solar and lunar eclipses"). As eclipses were not auspicious to the Chinese, they were "something that should not be happening". The 月 component alludes to the inauspicious lunar eclipse.
entries.服:
Phono-semantic compound: 凡 (tray, semantic) + 𠬝 (to subdue, phonetic) – to serve. 𠬝 is the original pictogram for this character; 凡 was added later.

凡 here has been corrupted into 舟 and subsequently 月.
entries.朏: Compound ideogram: 月 (moon) + 出 (to come out; to appear).
entries.朓:
Phono-semantic compound: 月 (moon, semantic) + 兆 (phonetic).

Note that the left component is not 肉, distinguish 脁.
entries.朔: Phono-semantic compound: 屰 (phonetic) + 月 (moon, semantic)
entries.朕:
Simplified from 𦩎.

Oracle-bone forms depict a 舟 (“boat”) beside two hands holding a rod-like object. In 合集 20610, a variant shows one hand holding the object, which overlaps with the prow of the boat. The graph may be transcribed as ⿰舟尹, and has been identified with 朕. The graph may be interpreted as an ideograph for 乘 (“to mount; to ascend; to board”). 

In Western Zhou bronze inscriptions, 朕 is used as a first-person genitive pronoun of deference, commonly before terms for ancestors, parents, or rulers; it is also used as a loan for 媵 in the sense “to send; to escort; to accompany; to transfer”. 

The traditional sense “sign; trace; evidence”, also written 眹, may be related to 證, 徵 and 應.
entries.朗: Phono-semantic compound: 良 (phonetic) + 月 (moon, semantic)
entries.朙: Compound ideogram: 囧 (whorl) + 月 (moon). See 明 for this form's historical forms.
entries.望:
Originally written 𦣠, an Compound ideogram: 臣 (eye) + 𡈼 (person standing on the ground) – a person standing up and looking off into the distance. Later 月 was added to produce 朢.

The 臣 component is now written 亡, making the current form a Phono-semantic compound: 亡 (phonetic) + 月 (semantic) + 𡈼 (semantic).
entries.朞: Phono-semantic compound: 其 (phonetic) + 月 (moon, semantic).
entries.期:
Phono-semantic compound: 其 (phonetic) + 日 (semantic).

The original composition with the semantic 日 is preserved in the variant forms 㫷 and 𣇳. The sun then changed to 月 to produce 朞, from which the character then evolved to the current form.
entries.朦:
Phono-semantic compound: 月 (moon, semantic) + 蒙 (phonetic).

Unlike most other characters with a 月-like component on the left, this character's 月 is not a simplification of 肉; 朦朧 was originally used in reference to the moon.
entries.朧:
Phono-semantic compound: 月 (moon, semantic) + 龍 (phonetic).

Unlike most other characters with a 月-like component on the left, this character's 月 is not the cursive form of 肉; 朦朧 was originally used in reference to the moon.
entries.木:
Pictogram – a tree: branches on top, roots on the bottom (more visible in earlier forms). 

See also 本, 未, and 末.
entries.未: Pictogram: a tree (木) with superposed or lush branches. Likely the original form of 枚.
entries.末: Ideogram: a tree (木) with its top highlighted with an extra stroke, implying the meaning of “apex”; contrast 本, 朱.
entries.本: Ideogram: a tree (木) with its bottom highlighted with an extra stroke, accentuating the roots; contrast 末, 朱.
entries.札: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 乙 (phonetic). It represents a thinly shaved wooden tag and, by extension, a tag or document on which characters are written.
entries.朮: Pictogram – a hand holding or gathering grain. It is the original character of 秫.
entries.朱: Ideogram: a tree (木) with its center highlighted with an extra dot-like stroke, accentuating the tree's core; contrast 本, 末.
entries.朳: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree; wood, semantic) + 八 (phonetic).
entries.朴:
Phono-semantic compound: 木 (semantic) + 卜 (phonetic).

Officially adopted as the simplified form of 樸 (etymology 6) in the Chinese Character Simplification Scheme (s:漢字簡化方案) in 1956.
entries.朵: Originally a depicting a stalk of a plant 禾 with something drooping. The bottom part of 禾 corrupted into 木, while the extra stroke corrupted into 乃, later simplified into 几.
entries.机: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree; wood, semantic) + 几 (phonetic).
entries.朿:
Pictogram – a tree 木 with thorns.

Alternatively, according to, it is a Pictogram – depicting a three-pointed spear.
entries.杀: Phonetic and vulgar form of 殺. Simplified from 殺. Compare 壳 from 殼.
entries.杁: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 入 (phonetic).
entries.杂: Seemingly influenced by 雑 and 𰗣. Both are (shorthand) variants of 雜.
entries.权: Simplified from 權. Same simplification occurs in 观.
entries.杅: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 于 (phonetic). Compare 杇.
entries.杆: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 干 (phonetic).
entries.杇: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 于 (phonetic). Compare 杅.
entries.杉: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 彡 (phonetic).
entries.李:
Oracle bone script: Phono-semantic compound: 來 (wheat, phonetic) + 子 (semantic). The phonetic part 來 became gradually corrupted to yield 木.

Shuowen erroneously remarks that this is a Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 子 (phonetic).
entries.杏:
Compound ideogram: 木 (wood) + 口 (mouth) – perhaps referring to the tastiness of its fruit.

Shuowen considers it to be a Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 可 (phonetic), but this is unlikely.
entries.村:
Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 寸 (phonetic).

Origin unclear. Seems a late graph, not in Shuowen dictionary of ca.100AD. Ogawa treats it as variant of CO graph 杶* "lacquer tree" which was used phonetically in the sense of "village" in place of another graph for "village", 邨*, which may be taken provisionally as 阝* "settlement, village", and 屯* "accumulate, stay" as semantic and phonetic.
entries.束: Ideogram – bag tied at both ends (earlier forms were often vertically symmetric). See also 東 and 柬.
entries.杠: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 工 (phonetic).
entries.杤:
Kokuji (created in Japan).

A zokuji (俗字). Nonstandard form of 栃. 万 is simplified form of 萬.

Pronunciation was derived from combined kun'yomi of (十) (10) and (千) (1000).

For place name, it is a former character used before the decree of 栃 as official character in 1879.
entries.杭:
Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 亢 (phonetic).

Originally a variant of 抗.
entries.杯: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (semantic) + 不 (phonetic). According to a variant, the phonetic component is 否, which also had the ancient meaning of "to block", perhaps referred to liquids in a glass.
entries.東:
Pictogram: a pictogram of a full 橐 tied at both ends. It is the original form of 重: forms with a human figure gave rise to 重, while forms without it gave rise to 東.

Interpreted in the Shuowen Jiezi as an Compound ideogram – the sun (日) rising behind a tree (木). According to p. 47-50, the character represents the Fu Sang tree. However, the original form is rather different, hence any interpretation tied to a tree is most likely a folk etymology. 

See the top component of 曹 in the original version. See also 柬, 熏, 西 and 鹵/卤.
entries.杲: Compound ideogram: 日 (sun) + 木 (tree) – the sun shining above trees.
entries.杳: Compound ideogram: 木 (tree) + 日 (sun) - dark. Compare 杲.
entries.杵: Compound ideogram: 木 (wood, semantic) + 午 (pestle, phonetic) – a wooden pestle.
entries.杻: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 丑 (hand; claw, phonetic) – wooden manacles or handcuffs. The phonetic component also indicates a hand or claw, hence it may add part of the meaning.
entries.松: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 公 (phonetic).
entries.板:
Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 反 (phonetic).

Officially adopted as the simplified form of 闆 (etymology 2) in the Chinese Character Simplification Scheme (s:漢字簡化方案) in 1956.
entries.极: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, wood, semantic) + 及 (phonetic).
entries.构:
Phono-semantic compound: 木 (semantic) + 勾 (phonetic).

Variant of 構.
entries.枅: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 幵 (phonetic)
entries.枇: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 比 (phonetic).
entries.枊: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 卬 (phonetic).
entries.枋: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 方 (phonetic)
entries.析: Compound ideogram: 木 (wood) + 斤 (axe) - to split wood.
entries.林: 木 (tree) to give the idea of multiple trees (compare 森), thus a forest. See also the top component of 散 in its original version.
entries.枙: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 厄 (phonetic).
entries.枚:
Generally thought to be an Compound ideogram: 木 (tree; wood) + 攴 (hand holding a stick).

However, considers it to be a Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 文 (phonetic), where 文 was later corrupted to 攴.
entries.果: Pictogram – fruits on a tree. Related to the original form of 采. Compare 栗 and 某. Unrelated to 喿.
entries.枝: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 支 (branch, phonetic).
entries.枯: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 古 (phonetic).
entries.枱: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 台 (phonetic).
entries.架: Phono-semantic compound: 加 (phonetic) + 木 (tree, wood, semantic) – a wooden prop.
entries.枹: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 包 (phonetic).
entries.枼:
Pictogram: leaves growing from a tree. Original form of 葉. Later phonetically borrowed as an instance of Phonetic loan – to represent 枼.

Shuowen mistakes it for a compound.
entries.柄: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 丙 (phonetic) – a wooden handle.
entries.柏: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 白 (phonetic).
entries.某:
Compound ideogram: 木 (tree) + 甘 (sweet); original form of 梅. Later borrowed to represent 某.

Similar to 果 and 栗. Similar but unrelated to 柑.
entries.柑: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood; tree, semantic) + 甘 (phonetic). Similar but unrelated to 某.
entries.染:
Compound ideogram: 水 (water) + 九 (hook) + 木 (tree) – to hang (on a hook 九) from a tree (木) into water (氵), so as to dye.

Earlier forms more often graphically 水 + 杂; in the modern form, the water radical is moved upward to the upper-left corner.
entries.柔: An ideograph depicting soft branches on 木, the original form of 柔. In the Eastern Zhou period the upper part was assimilated to 矛, giving the modern form.
entries.柘: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 石 (phonetic).
entries.柚: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree; wood, semantic) + 由 (phonetic).
entries.柜: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 巨 (huge, phonetic).
entries.柝: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 斥 (phonetic). Originally written 𣔳.
entries.查:
Originally written as 査, hence it is a Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 且 (phonetic). Today, the bottom part is stylized as 旦.

It originally indicates Chinese hawthorn, also known as mountain hawthorn, today written as 山楂; it also indicates a wooden raft. The original meanings are both preserved in the syllable 楂.
entries.柬: Compound ideogram: 束 (tie) + 八 (division, individually). Its original meaning is "to pick, to select, to choose", later written as 揀. Perhaps, the two points/marks inside the pictogram of the tied bag (later stylized as 八) mark and emphasize the content of a bag and/or the extraction of its content. See also 東//, 熏//, and 鹵//.
entries.柯: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 可 (phonetic).
entries.柱: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 主 (phonetic).
entries.柳:
Phono-semantic compound: 木 (semantic) + 卯 (phonetic) in oracle bone script and bronze inscriptions.

Later 桺 (木 (semantic) + 丣 (phonetic)) in small seal script.

The glyph finally turned back to 木 + 卯 in the current form.
entries.柵:
Simplified from 珊.

Simplified from 冊.

Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree; wood, semantic) + 冊 (a form made by lining up pieces of wood and binding them together, phonetic).
entries.査: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 且 (phonetic). It represents the idea of a raft made from assembled wood. The original character is 楂. It is later borrowed to mean "to examine" or "to investigate."
entries.柿:
Originally written as 柹: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (semantic) + 𠂔 (phonetic).

The current form is Phono-semantic compound: 木 (semantic) + 市 (phonetic).
entries.标: Simplified from 標. Officially adopted as the simplified form of 標 in the Chinese Character Simplification Scheme (s:漢字簡化方案) in 1956.
entries.栓: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 全 (phonetic) – a wooden peg.
entries.栔:
Phono-semantic compound: 㓞 (phonetic) + 木 (semantic). However, the phonetic components represents some incisions made with a knife.

Possibly a variant of 契 or vice versa, given that the two characters were used interchangeably in ancient text.
entries.栖: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 西 (phonetic).
entries.栗: Pictogram – chestnuts growing on a tree. Similar to 果 and 某. Unrelated to 要 and 票.
entries.栝:
Simplified from 括.

Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree; wood, semantic) + 𠯑 (phonetic).
entries.校: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 交 (phonetic).
entries.栩: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 羽 (phonetic).
entries.株: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 朱 (phonetic).
entries.栮: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree; wood, semantic) + 耳 (phonetic).
entries.栴: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 旃 (phonetic).
entries.样: Simplified from 樣. in the 1956 Chinese Character Simplification Scheme by the People's Republic of China.
entries.核:
Simplified from 核.

Simplified from 搰.

Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 亥 (phonetic) – a kind of tree. Modern meanings are borrowed.
entries.格: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 各 (phonetic).
entries.桀: In Guodian Chu Slips Bamboo_and_wooden_slips, Phono-semantic compound: 匄 (phonetic) + 木 (semantic). In the modern script, 匄 has corrupted into 舛.
entries.桃: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 兆 (phonetic).
entries.桅: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 危 (phonetic).
entries.桉: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 安 (phonetic).
entries.桌: Compound ideogram: 卓 (high, phonetic) + 木 (tree; wood, semantic) – table. The bottom 十 of 卓 has merged with or been replaced by 木. An obsolete variant that distinguishes the two components is 棹.
entries.桐: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 同 (phonetic).
entries.桑: Pictogram – of a mulberry tree. What were the shape of the tree's foliage is now 叒.
entries.桓: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 亘 (phonetic)
entries.桔: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 吉 (phonetic).
entries.桖: Compound ideogram: 木 (wood, semantic) + 血 (blood, phonetic).
entries.桙: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 牟 (phonetic).
entries.桥: Simplified from 橋. Unrelated to the Kangxi radicals 齊 > 齐 and 儿.
entries.桶: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 甬 (phonetic).
entries.桸: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 希 (phonetic).
entries.桼: Compound ideogram: 木 (tree) + 水 (water) – the resin (liquid) from a tree, used to make varnish.
entries.桿: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 旱 (phonetic).
entries.梁: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 刅 (phonetic) + 木 (wood, semantic) — a bridge.
entries.梂: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 求 (phonetic)
entries.梅: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 每 (phonetic).
entries.梓: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood; tree, semantic) + 宰 (phonetic)
entries.梗: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (semantic) + 更 (phonetic) – a type of plant.
entries.條: Phono-semantic compound: 攸 (phonetic) + 木 (semantic). Originally it indicates a small branch, perhaps with some reference to a wooden stick (in the top component, there is a man warned by a hand holding a vertical stick). The bottom part of the character is unrelated to 茶.
entries.梢: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 肖 (phonetic).
entries.梣: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 岑 (phonetic).
entries.梯: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, tree, semantic) + 弟 (phonetic) – a wooden ladder.
entries.械: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 戒 (phonetic). The character originally represented the meaning of "handcuffs" or "shackles," and by extension, it came to be used to mean "device" or "mechanism."
entries.梵: Phono-semantic compound: 林 (forest, semantic) + 凡 (phonetic) – lush. Originally a variant form of 芃.
entries.棄:
Compound ideogram: 子 (child) + 𠀠 (basket) + 廾 (two hands) - throwing out a child in a basket. 子 was often inverted as 𠫓.

In the oracle bone script form, 子 may appear with dots on either side of its head and body, perhaps representing amniotic fluid or dust.
entries.棆: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 侖 (phonetic).
entries.棉: Variant of 綿 by replacing 糸 with 木 (裘錫圭：《文字學概要（修訂本）》, p222).
entries.棋: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wooden, semantic) + 其 (phonetic).
entries.棍: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 昆 (phonetic).
entries.棑: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 非 (phonetic).
entries.棒: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, wood, semantic) + 奉 (phonetic) – a wooden club.
entries.棓: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, wood, semantic) + 咅 (phonetic).
entries.棕: Originally written as 椶, a Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 㚇 (phonetic). The phonetic component was later replaced by 宗.
entries.棚: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 朋 (phonetic)
entries.棟: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 東 (phonetic).
entries.棠: Phono-semantic compound: 尚 (phonetic) + 木 (tree, wood, semantic).
entries.棡: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 岡 (phonetic).
entries.棢: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 罔 (phonetic).
entries.棣: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood; tree, semantic) + 隶 (phonetic)
entries.棧: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 戔 (phonetic).
entries.森: Compound ideogram: 木 (tree), to suggest a large number (compare 三) of trees such as one would find in a forest. Compare 林.
entries.棰: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 垂 (phonetic).
entries.棲: Before the Warring States Period, written as 西. Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 妻 (phonetic).
entries.椉: Pictogram: 大 (person) + 舛 (feet) + 木 (tree) – a person climbing a tree.
entries.植: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 直 (phonetic).
entries.椎: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 隹 (phonetic). It expresses the idea of a piece of wood used to smash things, signifying a “hammer” or “mallet.”
entries.椏: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 亞 (phonetic).
entries.椑: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree; wood, semantic) + 卑 (phonetic).
entries.椙:
Kokuji (created in Japan). 

Compound ideogram: 木 (tree, semantic) + 昌 (prosperous, semantic).
entries.椰: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 耶 (phonetic).
entries.椹: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood; tree, semantic) + 甚 (phonetic).
entries.楊: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, wood, semantic) + 昜 (phonetic) – a kind of tree.
entries.楓: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 風 (phonetic)
entries.楗: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 建 (phonetic).
entries.楘: Phono-semantic compound: 敄 (phonetic) + 木 (wood, semantic).
entries.楚:
Originally, a compound formed by 林 (forest), 囗 (an enclosure), and 止 (a footprint pointing up) – according to Shuowen Jiezi, "a group of trees". Perhaps the whole character points to a location on space with a group of trees or a small forest. As seen on some versions on bronzes, the two bottom component were fused and stylized as 足, thus getting the old variant 䠂. 

Eventually, the whole character was further stylized as Phono-semantic compound: 林 (forest; grove; woods, semantic) + 疋 (phonetic). However, the phonetic component preserves part of the original drawing.
entries.楝: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 柬 (phonetic).
entries.楞: Compound ideogram: 四 (four) + 方 (square) + 木 (wood), or 四方 (square) + 木 (wood) – “four corners, edge”. A relatively late-appearing character, first recorded in the clerical script.
entries.楠: Vulgarized from 枏. Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood; tree, semantic) + 南 (phonetic).
entries.楫: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 咠 (phonetic).
entries.極: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, wood, semantic) + 亟 (phonetic) – originally meaning a crossbeam rafter.
entries.楷: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 皆 (phonetic).
entries.楽: Unorthodox variant Simplified from 樂. (𢆶 → ⿱丷八) found in the Ming dynasty orthographic dictionary 《字學三正》. Also found in 《宋元以來俗字譜》, a Variant Chinese character dictionary compiled in 1930 that records unorthodox forms (俗字) that have existed since the Song dynasty.
entries.概: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 既 (phonetic) – strickle.
entries.榅:
Unorthodox variant Simplified from 榲. that can be found in various historical dictionaries. 

Eventually adopted as an official form by the People's Republic of China in 1965 based on the Xin Zixing (新字形) standardized form of characters.
entries.榆: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 俞 (phonetic).
entries.榑: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 尃 (phonetic).
entries.榛: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 秦 (phonetic).
entries.榞: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 原 (phonetic).
entries.榦: Phono-semantic compound: 倝 (phonetic) + 木 (tree, semantic).
entries.榧: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood; tree, semantic) + 匪 (phonetic).
entries.榨: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 窄 (tight, phonetic).
entries.榪: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 馬 (phonetic).
entries.榭: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood; wooden structure, semantic) + 射 (phonetic); also Compound ideogram: 木 + 射 (archery), as it originally referred to an early type of architecture for both the practice and the ceremony of archery: an open-space hall built on raised ground, without internal division into rooms (;). In bronze script, the alternative form 𫷺 (i.e. ⿸广射) can be seen.
entries.槁: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 高 (phonetic).
entries.槃: Phono-semantic compound: 般 (phonetic) + 木 (wood, semantic).
entries.構: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 冓 (phonetic).
entries.槓: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 貢 (phonetic).
entries.様:
Japanese shinjitai Simplified from 樣.; compare bottom of 暴.

Right component is approximately 𦍌 + 氺.
entries.槤: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 連 (phonetic).
entries.槭: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 戚 (phonetic).
entries.槯: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 崔 (phonetic).
entries.槷: Phono-semantic compound: 埶 (phonetic) + 木 (wood, semantic)
entries.槽: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 曹 (phonetic) – a wooden trough or vat.
entries.樂:
Compound ideogram: 絲 (string) + 木 (wood) – strings on a piece of wood, i.e. a wooden musical instrument.

The oracle bone form shows two strings connected to the wood. In the bronze inscriptions, a 白 component was added in between the two strings, which may either represent the thumb (fiddling) or a phonetic part.
entries.樅: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 從 (phonetic)
entries.樊: Compound ideogram: 棥 (fence, phonetic) + 𠬜 (two hands, semantic). 棥 may have depicted a fence (resembling 网 or later 爻) between two trees (林).
entries.樑: Specialized form of 梁, with the addition of the semantic component 木.
entries.樓: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 婁 (phonetic).
entries.樗: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 雩 (phonetic).
entries.樟: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 章 (phonetic).
entries.模: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 莫 (phonetic).
entries.樣: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 羕 (phonetic).
entries.権: Variant of 權. Simplified from 權.
entries.樫: Kokuji (created in Japan). Compound ideogram: 木 (tree) + 堅 (hard, tough).
entries.樴: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 戠 (phonetic).
entries.樷: Phono-semantic compound: 林 (forest, semantic) + 取 (phonetic).
entries.樸: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 菐 (phonetic).
entries.樹: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 尌 (to plant a tree, phonetic). Originally written as 尌; an extra 木 was added to differentiate.
entries.樽: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 尊 (phonetic).
entries.樾: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 越 (phonetic)
entries.橄: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 敢 (phonetic).
entries.橈: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 堯 (phonetic).
entries.橋: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 喬 (phonetic).
entries.橐:
In oracle bone script, Pictogram – of a bag with a bottom. Compare with 𣒚, 束, 東, 囊.

Now Phono-semantic compound: 石 (phonetic) + 𣒚 (bag with a bottom, semantic).
entries.橙: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree; wood, semantic) + 登 (phonetic).
entries.橤: Phono-semantic compound: 惢 (phonetic) + 木 (tree, semantic).
entries.橫: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 黃 (phonetic).
entries.橮:
Simplified from 貿.

Phono-semantic compound: 木 (semantic) + 貿 (phonetic).
entries.橳:
Compound of 木 and 勝. 勝 replaces the reading かち (kachi), from the wood name かちのき (kachinoki).

It is also called ぬるで (nurude), after contracted ぬで (nude).
entries.檄: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 敫 (phonetic).
entries.檈: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 睘 (phonetic)
entries.檉: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 聖 (phonetic).
entries.檊: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 幹 (phonetic).
entries.檔: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 當 (phonetic).
entries.檗: Phono-semantic compound: 辟 (phonetic) + 木 (tree, semantic).
entries.檢: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (semantic) + 僉 (phonetic). Perhaps, it originally indicates the blade on the top of a wooden spear. Partly related to 鐱 > 劍, which indicates a sword (hence a blade).
entries.檣: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 嗇 (phonetic).
entries.檨: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 羨 (phonetic).
entries.檬: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 蒙 (phonetic).
entries.檿: Phono-semantic compound: 厭 (phonetic) + 木 (tree, semantic).
entries.櫃: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wooden, semantic) + 匱 (box, phonetic).
entries.櫈: Compound ideogram: 木 (wood, semantic) + 凳 (bench, phonetic).
entries.櫓: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 魯 (phonetic).
entries.櫖: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 慮 (phonetic).
entries.櫛: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 節 (phonetic).
entries.櫟: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 樂 (phonetic).
entries.櫡: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 箸 (phonetic).
entries.櫪: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 歷 (phonetic).
entries.櫫: Phono-semantic compound: 豬 (phonetic) + 木 (tree; wood, semantic).
entries.櫱: Phono-semantic compound: 辥 (phonetic) + 木 (wood; tree, semantic).
entries.欂: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 薄 (phonetic)
entries.欄: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 闌 (phonetic).
entries.權: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 雚 (phonetic) – a type of tree named 黃華 (Shuowen); phonetically borrowed for "standard weight".
entries.欒: Phono-semantic compound: 䜌 (phonetic) + 木 (tree, semantic).
entries.欖: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 覽 (phonetic).
entries.欚: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree; wood, semantic) + 蠡 (phonetic)
entries.欠:
Pictogram – a kneeling person with mouth open for various reasons (e.g., begging 欠, speaking and/or spitting while speaking 次, blowing 吹, singing 歌, desiring 欲, being tired 軟, vomiting 歐...).

The reversed version of this character is 㒫 > 旡 (e.g. 既), which must not be confused with 无.

Similar but unrelated to 卩, in which the person kneeling has the mouth shut.
entries.欸: Phono-semantic compound: 矣 (phonetic) + 欠 (breath, semantic).
entries.欺: Phono-semantic compound: 其 (phonetic) + 欠 (breath, semantic)
entries.欽: Compound ideogram – and Phono-semantic compound: 金 (gold; precious, phonetic) + 欠 (beg for, semantic). The character depicts a kneeling person.
entries.款:
Originally 歀, Phono-semantic compound: 柰 (phonetic) + 欠 (lacking, desire, semantic), meaning “desire”. The 木 component was simplified into 士 via libian, similar to 隸//→隷//.

Shuowen Jiezi interprets it as Phono-semantic compound: 窾 (phonetic) + 欠 (lacking, desire, semantic).
entries.歃: Phono-semantic compound: 臿 (phonetic) + 欠 (to yawn, semantic).
entries.歉: Phono-semantic compound: 兼 (phonetic) + 欠 (person with mouth open, semantic) to convey the original meaning of feeling hunger after eating. The phonetic component 兼 could be a reference to food since it represents a hand holding two crop plants.
entries.歋: Phono-semantic compound: 虒 (phonetic) + 欠 (to yawn, semantic).
entries.歌: Phono-semantic compound: 哥 (phonetic) + 欠 (blow, semantic). Specialized form of 哥.
entries.歐: Phono-semantic compound: 區 (phonetic) + 欠 (to yawn; to exhale, semantic) – to vomit (original form of 嘔).
entries.歕: Phono-semantic compound: 賁 (phonetic) + 欠 (breath, semantic)
entries.歠: Phono-semantic compound: 叕 (phonetic) + 㱃 (to drink, semantic).
entries.止:
Pictogram – a footprint pointing up, originally meaning "foot"; stylized as 龰. The derivative 趾 refers to the original meaning. Compare 手. Note that in oracle script, composed of 3 toes and a sole.

Compare to 夊, 夂, which have similar shape in oracle script, but pointing down (toe pointing right), and 𡕒 (as in right side of 舛, roughly ヰ, toe pointing left), hence different evolution.

Compare to 丑, which is the pictogram of an animal claw.

Eventually, note that the foot is represented with three toes, like the human hand in the characters 爪, 寸, 九, 又, and 彐.
entries.正:
Phono-semantic compound: 丁 (phonetic) + 止 (semantic)

Oracle bone and Shang–Zhou bronze forms show 丁 with 止. Some late Western Zhou and early Spring and Autumn bronze forms reduce 丁 to a horizontal stroke joined to 止. Later bronze and Chu bamboo forms often show 上 over 止; one-stroke forms also occur in Chu bamboo slips.

In oracle bone script, the graph is used for the word later written 征.
entries.此:
Compound ideogram: 止 (feet) + 人 (person) – where a person stops; here.

Alternatively, this may be the original form of 跐.
entries.步: Compound ideogram: 止 (foot) + 止 (foot) reversed – one foot in front of the other. Compare: 夅, 舛, other characters deriving from "two feet". See also the inner component of 歲. Unrelated to 少.
entries.歩: Assimilation of the bottom component 𣥂 to the more common 少. While continuously proscribed, it has appeared since the Han era.
entries.歪: Originally written as 竵. In its current form, an Compound ideogram: 不 (not) + 正 (straight; proper).
entries.歭: Phono-semantic compound: 止 (foot, semantic) + 寺 (phonetic)
entries.歯:
Unorthodox variant Simplified from 齒. (⿳从一从 → 米) found in various Movable type#Metal movable type in China copies of classical novels.

First attested in 《宋元以來俗字譜》, a Variant Chinese character dictionary compiled in 1930.
entries.歲:
Phono-semantic compound: 步 (semantic) + 戉 (phonetic) to indicate the passing of time as "movement". Hence, the original version was close to 𢧁. In addition to 戉, various components such as 月 used to be present, sometimes as simple as two dots.

The current form derives from the Qin (state)-style handwriting of the late Warring States (with a full-width 止 on the top and a bottom-left 撇 stroke extending outward as in 戊 or 戌 instead of bending inward as in 戉), which was also inherited by the clerical script.
entries.歴:
Variant of 歷, Simplified from 歷.

The modern Japanese usage is of reform (shinjitai) nature.
entries.歸:
Compound ideogram: 𠂤 (ancient form of 師) + 帚 (broom; sweep) – to eradicate the enemy and return.

Some analyse the 帚 component in the oracle bone script as a ligature of 止 and 方, i.e. “(of tribes in the periphery) to cease enmity and submit”.

A 止 or 辵 component was further added in the bronze inscriptions.

Shuowen deems 𠂤 to be the phonetic component of this character.
entries.歹: Pictogram – - human remains. The top component of 餐 still preserves the intermediate variant 歺.
entries.歿: Phono-semantic compound: 歹 (death, semantic) + 沒 (phonetic)
entries.殄: Its original form, 𠂈, likely represents a knife or dagger and means "exterminate": see the top component of 眞.
entries.残: Simplified from 殘. for Japanese shinjitai and Simplified from 殘. for simplified Chinese.
entries.殍: Phono-semantic compound: 歹 (remains, semantic) + 孚 (phonetic).
entries.殘:
Phono-semantic compound: 歹 (vicious, bones, semantic) + 戔 (phonetic) – to viciously harm, injure.

Semantic was originally 歺, but was simplified to 歹.
entries.殳:
Pictogram – or Compound ideogram: 𠘧 + 又 – a hand holding a tool similar to a hammer, hence activity (with a reference to the act of "beating"). See also 段 and the original version on oracle bones of 鼓.

The whole character was then borrowed phonetically to indicate an ancient halberd made of bamboo.
entries.段: In the bronze script it is a Phono-semantic compound: 厂 (phonetic) + 殳 (semantic), showing a hammer in hand breaking a stone with fragments coming off; 殳 was the pictogram of a hammer and later was borrowed to indicate a bamboo halberd. Most of the character is identical to 叚.
entries.殸: Compound ideogram: 声 (stone chime) + 殳 (hand holding a hammer or a mallet) — a stone chime being struck by a mallet. Compare 鼓, in which a drum is being beaten. See also the right component of 段. See also 㱿.
entries.殺:
In the oracle bone script, it was an Compound ideogram – of a boar that had been impaled in the head.

In the seal script, the original compound was corrupted into 𣏂 (sometimes written as 杀). It was also in the seal script that the Pictogram: 人 (person) + 又 (right hand), which was later corrupted into 殳 or 攴, was added under the head of the boar to specify the killing was done by a person.

The modern-day character inherits this and can be thought of as a Phono-semantic compound: 𣏂 (phonetic) + 殳 (spear, semantic).
entries.殿:
Shuowen: Phono-semantic compound: 臀 (phonetic) + 殳 (hand holding a weapon, semantic) – the sound of hitting (not attested in ancient documents).

 considers the character to be developed from 𠂤; 尸 and 丌 are added to form 𡱂, and 殳 is added to emphasize the meaning of “hitting the buttocks”.
entries.毂: Simplified from 轂. and horizontal stroke above 车 removed.
entries.毄:
Simplified from 罊.

Compound ideogram: 軎 (axle tip) + 殳 (weapon) - things which hit each other.
entries.毅: Phono-semantic compound: 豙 (phonetic) + 殳 (an ancient Chinese weapon, semantic)
entries.毆: Phono-semantic compound: 區 (phonetic) + 殳 (action, semantic).
entries.毋: In the oracle bone script, 母 was borrowed to represent this character. It was later specialized to distinguish it from “mother”, replacing the two dots with one stroke.
entries.母: Differentiated form of 女* with the addition of distinguishing dots. In the early oracle bone texts both words 女 and 母 were written as 女*. Part of this character appears in 乳.
entries.毎: Simplified from 每., replacing the two dots with one stroke.
entries.每:
Possibly an Compound ideogram: 屮 (semantic) + 母 (woman, phonetic). The top component resembling 屮 may represent a bamboo hairpin (笄) to indicate that the woman was at least 15 years old.

Alternatively, partly in accordance to the interpretation of Xu Shen, the sprout may indicate that the woman was considered adult and ready to be married and generate sons.

See the original form of 敖, in which the top component is the same. See also 毒.

The top component of the character is unrelated to 旅, 傷, 复, 乞 as well as 人.
entries.毐: Compound ideogram: 士 (virtuous man) + 毋 (to not have) – person with no morals.
entries.毒:
Chen, Jian (2020): Pictogram – of a woman wearing a feathered ornament on her head – original form of 纛. Later borrowed for 毒. If this is the correct interpretation, see also 每.

Alternatively, Li Xueqin (2012) proposes it is a Phono-semantic compound: 屮 (vegetation, semantic) + 毐 (phonetic), meaning "a type of poisonous plant."
entries.毓:
Simplified from 育.

Pictogram: 母 (woman) + 子 (child) — a woman giving birth to a child. Original form of 育. Later decorated and stylized as 每 + 㐬.
entries.比:
Chu Wan-li (1948): Phono-semantic compound: 匕 (phonetic) + 匕 (phonetic).

Shuowen interprets it as an ideogrammic compound meaning to juxtapose. Graphically similar but unrelated to 从, 尼, 化 and 北.
entries.毬: Phono-semantic compound: 毛 (hair, semantic) + 求 (phonetic)
entries.毽: Phono-semantic compound: 毛 (feather, semantic) + 建 (phonetic).
entries.氅: Phono-semantic compound: 敞 (phonetic) + 毛 (feather, semantic).
entries.氈:
Phono-semantic compound: 亶 (phonetic) + 毛 (hair, fur, semantic).

In some fonts, the lower left is 且 (instead of 旦).
entries.氊: Phono-semantic compound: 毛 (hair, fur, semantic) + 亶 (phonetic).
entries.氌: Phono-semantic compound: 毛 (hair, semantic) + 魯 (phonetic).
entries.氐: Pictogram: 氏 (clan; bowing figure) + 一, hence 氏 with an empty circle (then a line, today either a line or a point) underneath: perhaps a bowing figure depicted while sowing a field or the root of a tree (see 柢) with a mark at the bottom.
entries.氓: Phono-semantic compound: 亡 (phonetic) + 民 (people, semantic).
entries.气:
Pictogram: clouds flowing through the sky.

In the oracle bone script, it was represented by three horizontal strokes, expressing the "feeling" of the sky. However, in order to avoid confusion with the number 三, 气 was changed to draw a small stroke from top to bottom.

Its variant is 乞 and was later used to distinguish a phonetically borrowed meaning, "to beg".

Semantically unrelated to 氣 and its variant 餼 due to a different meaning ("give food as a gift").
entries.氖: Phono-semantic compound: 气 (gas, semantic) + 乃 (phonetic).
entries.気: Simplified from 氣. in the 1946 Tōyō kanji list.
entries.氙: Phono-semantic compound: 气 (gas, semantic) + 山 (mountain, phonetic). The phonetic component is abbreviated from 仙.
entries.氜: Compound ideogram: 气 (gas; air) + 日 (sun).
entries.氟: Phono-semantic compound: 气 (gas, semantic) + 弗 (phonetic).
entries.氠: Phono-semantic compound: 气 (gas, semantic) + 申 (phonetic).
entries.氡: Phono-semantic compound: 气 (gas, semantic) + 冬 (phonetic).
entries.氣:
Phono-semantic compound: 气 (phonetic) + 米 (rice, semantic).

Later borrowed meanings of “air, flow” from 气. The derivative 餼 refers to the original word. Compare 乞.
entries.氥: Phono-semantic compound: 气 (gas, semantic) + 西 (phonetic).
entries.氦: Phono-semantic compound: 气 (gas, semantic) + 亥 (phonetic).
entries.氧: Phono-semantic compound: 气 (gas, semantic) + 養 (to nourish, phonetic).
entries.氨: Phono-semantic compound: 气 (gas, semantic) + 安 (phonetic).
entries.氪: Phono-semantic compound: 气 (air; gas, semantic) + 克 (phonetic).
entries.氫: Phono-semantic compound: 气 (air; gas, semantic) + 輕 (light; of low density, phonetic).
entries.氮: Phono-semantic compound: 气 (gas, semantic) + 淡 (dilute, phonetic).
entries.氯: Phono-semantic compound: 气 (gas, semantic) + 彔 (phonetic). 彔* is also a reduced form of 綠*, serving as a semantic component.
entries.氰: Phono-semantic compound: 气 (gas, semantic) + 青 (phonetic).
entries.水:
Pictogram – of water flowing; sometimes written as the variant 氺 (e.g., 泰, 录, and 黎). Next to a character, it is compressed and stylized into 氵 (which is unrelated to 冫).

Compare 川 and its variant 巛. Compare also 永 and its cognate 𠂢. See also the bottom part of 原 in its original version (厡).
entries.永:
Pictogram – of a long river with tributaries. Cognate with 𠂢, 派. 

Alternatively, Pictogram – of a person swimming in the water. Original form of 泳.
entries.氿: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 九 (phonetic).
entries.汀: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (river, semantic) + 丁 (phonetic).
entries.汁: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 十 (phonetic). It expresses the idea of a liquid.
entries.求: Pictogram – of a centipede. Original form of 蛷.
entries.汇: Simplified from 滙., the variant form of 匯.
entries.汈: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 刁 (phonetic).
entries.汉: Simplified from 漢. (elimination of right component to 又) in the 1956 Chinese Character Simplification Scheme by the People's Republic of China. Not known to have existed prior to that.
entries.汊: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 叉 (to intersect, phonetic)
entries.汏: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 大 (phonetic)
entries.汐: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 夕 (phonetic).
entries.汒: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 亡 (phonetic).
entries.汕: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 山 (phonetic).
entries.汝: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (river; water, semantic) + 女 (phonetic).
entries.汞: Phono-semantic compound: 工 (phonetic) + 水 (water, semantic)
entries.江: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 工 (phonetic).
entries.汨: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 日 (phonetic).
entries.汩: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 曰 (phonetic).
entries.汪: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 王 (phonetic).
entries.汰: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 太 (phonetic).
entries.汲: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 及 (phonetic).
entries.汶: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 文 (phonetic).
entries.汽:
Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 气 (phonetic).

Also ideogrammic compound 氵 (water) and 气 (air), representing water in air form.
entries.汾: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 分 (phonetic).
entries.沂: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (river, semantic) + 斤 (phonetic).
entries.沃: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 夭 (phonetic) – to irrigate with water.
entries.沅: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 元 (phonetic).
entries.沈:
In the oracle bone script, it was an Compound ideogram: 水 (water) + 羊 (sheep) — to submerge a sheep into the water (as a form of sacrifice to the river god). Other forms included 牛 or 玉 instead of 羊.

Starting from the bronze inscriptions, it became a Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 冘 (phonetic).

This character was later borrowed to signify the surname, and the variant 沉 was adopted for the original meaning.
entries.沉: Variant of 沈, see there for more.
entries.沋: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 尤 (phonetic).
entries.沐: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 木 (phonetic).
entries.沔: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 丏 (phonetic).
entries.沖: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 中 (phonetic).
entries.沙: Compound ideogram: 水 (water) + 少 (dots) — sand on a shoreline.
entries.沛: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 巿 (phonetic).
entries.沝: Compound ideogram: 水 (water; river) + 水 (water; river). Compare 淼 and 㵘.
entries.沟: Simplified from 溝. - Compare 购*, simplified from 購*.
entries.没: Variant of 沒. Also used in Japanese shinjitai and simplified Chinese.
entries.沢: Japanese shinjitai character. Simplified from 澤.
entries.沫: A Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 末 (phonetic)
entries.沭: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 朮 (phonetic).
entries.沱: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 它 (phonetic)
entries.沸: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 弗 (phonetic).
entries.油: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 由 (phonetic).
entries.沺: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 田 (phonetic)
entries.治: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 台 (phonetic) — name of a river.
entries.沼: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 召 (phonetic).
entries.沽: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 古 (phonetic).
entries.沾:
Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 占 (phonetic).

Ganlu Zishu considers this glyph to be an unorthodox variant of 霑*.
entries.沿: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 㕣 (phonetic). The character originally referred to the edge of a river, and by extension, it came to represent the idea of "following along" or "accompanying."
entries.況: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (river, semantic) + 兄 (phonetic).
entries.泃: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 句 (phonetic).
entries.泅: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 囚 (phonetic).
entries.泆: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 失 (phonetic)
entries.泉: Pictogram – or Compound ideogram: 白 (spring mouth) + 水 (water) – water flowing from the source of a spring. See also 原.
entries.泊: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 白 (phonetic) – a ship stays still after running aground in shallow water.
entries.泌: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 必 (phonetic).
entries.泓: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 弘 (phonetic)
entries.泔: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 甘 (phonetic).
entries.泖: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 卯 (phonetic).
entries.泗: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 四 (phonetic).
entries.泡: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 包 (phonetic). It conveys the meaning of “foam.”
entries.波: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 皮 (surface, phonetic).
entries.泣: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 立 (phonetic). The character originally meant "tears," and by extension, it came to represent the act of "crying."
entries.泥: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 尼 (phonetic).
entries.注: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 主 (phonetic).
entries.泰: Originally a Phono-semantic compound: 大 (phonetic) + 廾 (two hands, semantic) + 水 (water, semantic). A more conservative variant is 𡙌. The 大 and 廾 later fused into 𡗗. The original meaning according to Shuowen Jiezi was "to slip", perhaps with a reference to seize something wet or to seize a liquid with bare hands. Then it became "too ", which was written either as 太 or 𡙌 > 泰 or as its variant 冭, perhaps due to the influence of its pronunciation and/or the top component of the character, which has a reference to a great quantity. As a result of the changed meaning, it may have been reinterpreted as an Compound ideogram: 大 (big; great, semantic) + 廾 (two hands, semantic) + 水 (water, semantic).
entries.洈: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (river, semantic) + 危 (phonetic).
entries.洋: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 羊 (phonetic).
entries.洒: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 西 (phonetic).
entries.洓: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 朿 (phonetic)
entries.洔: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 寺 (phonetic)
entries.洗: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 先 (phonetic).
entries.洙: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 朱 (phonetic).
entries.洛: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 各 (phonetic).
entries.洞: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 同 (phonetic).
entries.洡: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 耒 (phonetic).
entries.洣: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 米 (phonetic).
entries.津:
Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 盡 (phonetic).

The phonetic component 𦘔 is, according to Ji Xusheng (2014), a simplified form of 盡. It further corrupted into 聿 in the clerical script.

entries.漢:
漢: semantic 水 (“water”) + phonetic 熯. Earliest attested in early Western Zhou bronze inscriptions, e.g. the 京師畯尊 (銘圖 11784), where it is used as a river name: 王涉漢伐楚.

熯 (⿱𦰩火) depicts a person bound behind the back, mouth open toward the sky, over fire. It may be related to 灘, 歎, 嘆, 熯, 暵, and 難, in senses connected with drought, burning, or exclamation. From the middle Western Zhou onward, 𦰩 may have been confused with 黃.

The use as a name for the Chinese ethnicity is generally dated to the Northern Dynasties. It was promoted by the Tuoba-Xianbei-led Northern Wei as a political exonym to deny the legitimacy of the Eastern Jin court and dissolve the residual 晉人 (Jin People) identity in the former Western Jin lands, while appealing to the prestige of the Han dynasty. The appellation was initially resisted as pejorative and was still avoided in the early Tang, only gradually becoming widely accepted as an ethnic name from the mid-to-late Tang onward. Prior to this period, the Chinese referred mostly their land as 華夏 and referred themselves as 諸華/諸夏, and from the Qin dynasty onwards as 華人 or simply as subjects of the ruling dynasty (e.g. 秦人, 漢人, 魏人, 晉人, 宋人, 齊人...)

Shuowen Jiezi interprets the character as a representation of the female macaque.
