entries.精: Phono-semantic compound: 米 (rice, semantic) + 青 (phonetic) – polished rice.
entries.粿: Phono-semantic compound: 米 (rice, semantic) + 果 (phonetic)
entries.糊: Phono-semantic compound: 米 (rice, semantic) + 胡 (phonetic).
entries.糋: Phono-semantic compound: 米 (rice, semantic) + 前 (phonetic).
entries.糕: Phono-semantic compound: 米 (rice, semantic) + 羔 (lamb, phonetic) – food made from rice flour. The phonetic component 羔 ("lamb", hence an animal prone to be cooked) may also have a reference to food and cooking as well.
entries.糖: Phono-semantic compound: 米 (rice, semantic) + 唐 (phonetic).
entries.糗: Phono-semantic compound: 米 (rice, semantic) + 臭 (phonetic).
entries.糛: Phono-semantic compound: 米 (rice, semantic) + 堂 (phonetic).
entries.糜: Phono-semantic compound: 麻 (phonetic) + 米 (rice, semantic).
entries.糞:
Oracle bone: Pictogram: 3 dots + 𠀠 + 廾 + optional 帚.

Small seal: Pictogram: 釆 + 𠦒 + 廾.

The current glyph is from the small seal script.
entries.糟: Phono-semantic compound: 米 (semantic) + 曹 (phonetic). The original version is 𥽾. The radical of the rice perhaps is a reference to the liquor made out of fermented rice (see for instance 鬯) and the original meaning is "unfiltered", referred for instance to liquor and wine.
entries.糠: Phono-semantic compound: 米 (rice, semantic) + 康 (phonetic).
entries.糨: Phono-semantic compound: 米 (rice, semantic) + 強 (phonetic).
entries.糫: Phono-semantic compound: 米 (rice, semantic) + 睘 (phonetic)
entries.糬: Phono-semantic compound: 米 (rice, semantic) + 署 (phonetic).
entries.糰: Phono-semantic compound: 米 (rice, semantic) + 團 (ball, phonetic).
entries.糴: Compound ideogram: 入 (in, semantic) + 䊮 (grain, phonetic)
entries.糶: Compound ideogram: 出 (out, semantic) + 䊮 (grain, phonetic)
entries.糾: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 丩 (to entangle, phonetic). 丩 originally referred to this word, 糸 was added later.
entries.紀: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 己 (phonetic).
entries.約: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (rope, semantic) + 勺 (phonetic).
entries.紅: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 工 (phonetic).
entries.紆: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 于 (phonetic).
entries.紇: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 乞 (phonetic).
entries.紊: Phono-semantic compound: 文 (phonetic) + 糸 (silk, semantic)
entries.紋: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (thread, semantic) + 文 (phonetic) – a line of thread. Specialised character from 文.
entries.納: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, thin thread, semantic) + 内 (phonetic).
entries.紐: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 丑 (phonetic) – a handle. However, the phonetic component indicates either an animal claw or a hand, hence it adds part of the meaning.
entries.純: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (thread, semantic) + 屯 (phonetic). It conveys the meaning of "without any impurities," and also "exclusively."
entries.紗: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (thread, semantic) + 沙 (phonetic).
entries.紙: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 氏 (phonetic).
entries.級: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (thread, semantic) + 及 (phonetic). According to Shuowen Jiezi, the original meaning was referred to a "sequence" related to silk (絲的次第), however Xu Shen didn't specify the exact kind of sequence he was talking about.
entries.紜: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk; thread, semantic) + 云 (phonetic)
entries.素:
Pictogram – hands 廾 braiding thread 糸.

In modern form, top component looks like 生 without the diagonal stroke – compare 責, 青.
entries.紡: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 方 (phonetic).
entries.索:
Compound ideogram: 糸 (thread) + 𣎳 (strip fibres off a hemp stalk). Threads (rope) being removed from a fabric.

糸 visually represents the middle interior of the small seal script form, whereas 𣎳 is the three-pointed top part and the left and right lines.
entries.紬: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 由 (phonetic).
entries.累:
Simplified from 纍.

Folk etymology considers this character as an ideographic compound representing the tiredness after work. In ancient China, men were working in the field (田) while women sewed (糸).
entries.細: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (semantic) + 囟 (phonetic). The right component is etymologically unrelated to 田 in which it was corrupted to after the Han dynasty.
entries.紲: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 世 (phonetic).
entries.紳: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (thread, semantic) + 申 (phonetic). It represents a large sash used for formal dress, called a "large obi."
entries.紵: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 宁 (phonetic)
entries.紺: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk; thread, semantic) + 甘 (phonetic).
entries.絃: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 玄 (phonetic).
entries.組: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 且 (phonetic).
entries.絆: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 半 (phonetic).
entries.経: Simplified from 經. Also a Japanese shinjitai. Current form 糸 + 圣, but not etymologically related to 圣.
entries.絕:
Originally Compound ideogram: 刀 (knife) + 幺 (silk) or Compound ideogram: 刀 (knife) + 𢆶 (silk) — to cut silk threads.

Now Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 刀 (knife, semantic) + 卪 (phonetic).

Most likely unrelated to 色.
entries.絝: Phono-semantic compound: 糹 (silk, semantic) + 夸 (phonetic) – pants.
entries.絞: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (thread, semantic) + 交 (phonetic). Shuowen interprets it as an ideogrammic compound.
entries.絡: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (thread, semantic) + 各 (phonetic) – wrapped in thread, a web of thread.
entries.給: According to Shuowen Jiezi, Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (semantic) + 合 (phonetic) – "rich, abundant", perhaps with a reference to precious silk; today it also means "to give". The phonetic component means "to join, to unite", however it is likely unrelated to the original meaning.
entries.絮: Phono-semantic compound: 如 (phonetic) + 糸 (silk, semantic).
entries.絳: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 夅 (phonetic)
entries.絹: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (thread, semantic) + 肙 (phonetic). The character conveys the meaning of "silk."
entries.絿: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 求 (phonetic)
entries.綁: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (thin silk; thread, semantic) + 邦 (phonetic).
entries.綏: Compound ideogram: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 妥 (to comfort, phonetic).
entries.經: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk; thread, semantic) + 巠 (phonetic).
entries.綢: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 周 (phonetic).
entries.綬: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, thread, semantic) + 受 (phonetic).
entries.綱: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (rope, semantic) + 岡 (phonetic).
entries.網: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (rope, semantic) + 罔 (phonetic).
entries.綴: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 叕 (phonetic).
entries.綵: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk; thread, semantic) + 采 (phonetic).
entries.綸: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 侖 (phonetic).
entries.綹: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 咎 (phonetic).
entries.綺: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 奇 (phonetic)
entries.綻: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (thread, semantic) + 定 (phonetic).
entries.綿: A compound of 糸 + 帛 reorganized from 緜 (系 became 糸 and moved to the left).
entries.緋: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 非 (phonetic).
entries.緌: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 委 (phonetic).
entries.総: Variant of 總. Simplified from 總. It can be analysed as inheriting the variant 忩 of component 悤.
entries.緜:
Geometrically evolved from 縣 into 帛 + 系 (; Chen, 2018).

The glyph would furtherly develop into 綿 and also give rise to an offspring character 棉.
entries.緝: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 咠 (phonetic).
entries.緧: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (thread, semantic) + 酋 (phonetic).
entries.編: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (thread, semantic) + 扁 (phonetic) – to knit together a book (with thread).
entries.緩: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 爰 (phonetic).
entries.緬: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 面 (phonetic).
entries.緯: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (thread, semantic) + 韋 (phonetic).
entries.練: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 柬 (phonetic).
entries.緼: An unorthodox variant Simplified from 縕. which can be found in various historical dictionaries such as the Ming dynasty 《重訂直音篇》.
entries.縋: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 追 (phonetic).
entries.縐: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 芻 (phonetic)
entries.縖: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 害 (phonetic)
entries.縛: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (rope, semantic) + 尃 (phonetic).
entries.縞: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 高 (phonetic).
entries.縣:
Compound ideogram: 目 + 木 + 糸 - to hang with the string 糸 by the head 目 (using an eye to represent a head) on a tree 木. Originally referred to 懸; later Phonetic loan – for 縣.

In Qin bamboo slip scripts, some of 目 + 木 were corrupted to 県 (with one straight horizontal line rather than 𠃊) which interpreted to a reversed head 𥄉 by Shuowen, and 糸 was corrupted to 系.
entries.縮: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (string, thread, semantic) + 宿 (phonetic).
entries.縳: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (rope, semantic) + 專 (phonetic).
entries.縴: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 牽 (phonetic).
entries.縵: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 曼 (phonetic)
entries.績: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (thread, semantic) + 責 (phonetic) – to spin thread.
entries.繁: Phono-semantic compound: 敏 (phonetic) + 糸 (silk, semantic)
entries.繇: Originally written 䌛. Now Phono-semantic compound: 䍃 (phonetic) + 系 (semantic).
entries.織: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 戠 (phonetic).
entries.繕: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (thread; textile, semantic) + 善 (good, phonetic). Also Compound ideogram: to repair; to make good.
entries.繖: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 散 (phonetic).
entries.繜: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 尊 (phonetic)
entries.繞: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (rope, semantic) + 堯 (phonetic).
entries.繠: Phono-semantic compound: 惢 (phonetic) + 糸 (silk, semantic).
entries.繡: Earliest seen in Warring States Period texts. Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 肅 (phonetic)
entries.繫: Phono-semantic compound: 毄 (phonetic) + 糸 (thread, semantic)
entries.繭: Compound ideogram: 糸 (silk) + 虫 (insect) + 黹 (needlework).
entries.繯: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (rope, semantic) + 睘 (phonetic)
entries.繰: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (thread, semantic) + 喿 (phonetic). It refers to dark blue silk. By extension, it is used to mean "to wind" or "to twist" thread.
entries.繲: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (semantic) + 解 (phonetic). Not recorded in Shuowen.
entries.繳: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 敫 (phonetic) – raw silk thread.
entries.繹: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 睪 (phonetic).
entries.繼:
Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (rope, semantic) + 㡭 (phonetic).

The original form may have depicted four 幺.
entries.繽: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 賓 (phonetic).
entries.纂: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, thread, semantic) + 算 (phonetic).
entries.纅: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 樂 (phonetic).
entries.纍: Phono-semantic compound: 畾 (phonetic) + 糸 (fine silk, semantic). The original meaning is "rope; to bind", hence any reference to being tired after hard work in the fields or after sewing is a folk etymology based on modern meaning.
entries.纏: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 廛 (phonetic).
entries.纓: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 嬰 (phonetic).
entries.纖: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 韱 (phonetic).
entries.纜: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 覽 (phonetic).
entries.纞: Phono-semantic compound: 糸 (silk, semantic) + 戀 (phonetic).
entries.纩: Simplified from 纊. in simplified Chinese.
entries.继: Simplified from 継. 継* is a variant of 繼*.
entries.缶:
Pictogram – an earthenware jar with a lid. See also the bottom part of the original versions of 由.

Unrelated to the top component of 鬱, in which it represents a stylized man (大).
entries.缺: Phono-semantic compound: 缶 (earthen pot, semantic) + 夬 (phonetic).
entries.缽: Phono-semantic compound: 缶 (pot, semantic) + 本 (phonetic). Originally written as 鉢 or 盋.
entries.罄: Phono-semantic compound: 殸 (phonetic) + 缶 (pottery, semantic).
entries.罅: Phono-semantic compound: 虖 (phonetic) + 缶 (pot, semantic)
entries.罌: Phono-semantic compound: 賏 (phonetic) + 缶 (pottery, semantic).
entries.罐: Phono-semantic compound: 缶 (pottery, semantic) + 雚 (phonetic).
entries.网: Pictogram – a net. Sometimes, the web on top is stylized as 罒, which is unrelated to the eye 目: see 買, 罵, 詈 (used in 罰), 罷, and 羅 (> 罗), in which it represents a net.
entries.罔: Phono-semantic compound: 网 (net, semantic) + 亡 (phonetic).
entries.罕: Phono-semantic compound: 网 (net, semantic) + 干 (phonetic)
entries.罜: Phono-semantic compound: 网 (net, semantic) + 主 (phonetic).
entries.罝: Phono-semantic compound: 网 (net, semantic) + 且 (phonetic).
entries.罠: Phono-semantic compound: 网 (net, semantic) + 民 (phonetic).
entries.罢: Simplified from 𮊒. Officially adopted as the simplified form of 罷 in the Chinese Character Simplification Scheme (s:漢字簡化方案) in 1956.
entries.罥: Phono-semantic compound: 网 (net, semantic) + 肙 (phonetic).
entries.罧: Phono-semantic compound: 网 (net, semantic) + 林 (phonetic).
entries.罪: Compound ideogram: 网 (net) + 非 (mistake). The original version is 𦋛 and its original meaning was a net for fishing, then used instead of 辠 due to the similarity of the latter character to 皇, which represents the Emperor.
entries.罫: Phono-semantic compound: 網 (net, semantic) + 卦 (phonetic).
entries.罰: Compound ideogram: 詈 (abuse verbally, semantic) + 刀 (knife, semantic). To abuse verbally and to use a knife improperly represent a crime. The original version is 𠟑, in which the left component is 𧧧.
entries.署: Phono-semantic compound: 网 (net, semantic) + 者 (phonetic).
entries.罵: Phono-semantic compound: 网 (semantic) + 馬 (phonetic). The original version is 𦋻. See also 詈 (< 𧧧).
entries.罷: Compound ideogram: 网 + 能 - catch a bear with a web. According to Shuowen Jiezi, it originally means "catch criminals"; according to Zhang Shunhui (張舜徽), it means "tired" with a reference to a bear being caught while tired after a chase. The web at the top of the character is well visible in its original version 𦋼.
entries.罹:
Compound ideogram: 网 (net) + 心 (heart) + 隹 (bird).

The senses represented by this character were often written with the character 離 in ancient times.
entries.罺: Phono-semantic compound: 网 (net, semantic) + 巢 (phonetic).
entries.罽: Phono-semantic compound: 网 (net, semantic) + 㓹 (phonetic).
entries.罾: Phono-semantic compound: 网 (net, semantic) + 曾 (phonetic).
entries.羂: Phono-semantic compound: 网 (net, semantic) + 絹 (phonetic).
entries.羅: Compound ideogram: 网 (net) + 維 (bird (tied with string)) — net for catching birds. The original version is 𦌴.
entries.羆: Phono-semantic compound: 罷 (phonetic) + 熊 (bear, semantic); the common part 能 is shared.
entries.羊: Pictogram – picture of a ram's head. See also the original version of 沈.
entries.羋: Ideogram: 羊 with a mark indicating its bleating.
entries.羌: A man 人 with two sheep horns 羊 on his head - barbarian. The character 羊 also indicates the pronunciation. See also 茍 and 美.
entries.美:
Pictogram – a person (大) wearing a headdress (now written 羊) of feathers or ram's horn.

The modern form could be considered an Compound ideogram: 羊 (ram or feathers) + 大 (person).

See also 敖, 冒, and 免.
entries.羔:
Compound ideogram: 羊 (caprid) + 火 (fire) – a lamb being cooked on a fire. The definition may have come from animals like lambs being apt for cooking and eating.

According to the Shuowen Jiezi, Phono-semantic compound: 羊 (semantic) + 照 (phonetic).
entries.羛: The 弗 on the bottom was a deformation of 我 in Warring States scripts. The Shuowen mentions its attestation in the works of Mozi.
entries.羜: Phono-semantic compound: 羊 (sheep, semantic) + 宁 (phonetic)
entries.羝: Phono-semantic compound: 羊 (sheep; goat, semantic) + 氐 (phonetic).
entries.羞: Phono-semantic compound: 羊 (semantic) + 丑 (phonetic); phonetic previously 又. Not related to 差 or 着.
entries.群: Phono-semantic compound: 君 (phonetic) + 羊 (semantic) – a herd of sheep; a group.
entries.羥:
Phono-semantic compound: 羊 (sheep, goat, semantic) + 巠 (phonetic) ― a kind of sheep or goat.

For the sense “hydroxy” in organic chemistry, the glyph is a blend of 氫 and 氧, using the phonetic components of both characters (巠 and 羊).
entries.羧: For the organic compound, Compound ideogram: 羊 (oxygen, from 氧) + 夋 (acid, from 酸).
entries.義: Phono-semantic compound: 我 (phonetic) + 羊 (semantic). The component 羊 here signifies "good; beautiful; auspicious" and not "sheep". See 祥, 善 and 幸.
entries.羭: Phono-semantic compound: 羊 (sheep; goat, semantic) + 俞 (phonetic).
entries.羯: Phono-semantic compound: 羊 (sheep; goat, semantic) + 曷 (phonetic).
entries.羼: Compound ideogram: 尸 (shelter, semantic) + 羴 (a crowd of sheep or goat, phonetic).
entries.翁: Phono-semantic compound: 公 (phonetic) + 羽 (wings, semantic). Originally representing the meaning “feathers”, it was later loaned to mean “old man” and similar senses, by association with the semantic 公.
entries.翅: Phono-semantic compound: 支 (phonetic) + 羽 (feathers, semantic).
entries.翆: Unorthodox variant of 翠. The phonetic component 卆 is a variant of 卒.
entries.翎: Phono-semantic compound: 令 (phonetic) + 羽 (feather, semantic).
entries.習:
Compound ideogram: 羽 (wings) + 日 (sun) – to learn to fly, to practice flying.

In the current form, 日 has changed to 白, so the present form is 羽 (wings) + 白 (white).

Alternatively, the original form may have been a Phono-semantic compound: 彗 (phonetic) + 日 (sun, semantic).
entries.翔: Phono-semantic compound: 羊 (phonetic) + 羽 (feathers, semantic)
entries.翕: Phono-semantic compound: 合 (phonetic) + 羽 (wings, semantic)
entries.翠: Phono-semantic compound: 羽 (wing, semantic) + 卒 (phonetic).
entries.翡: Phono-semantic compound: 羽 (wing, semantic) + 非 (phonetic).
entries.翥: Phono-semantic compound: 者 (phonetic) + 羽 (wings; feathers, semantic).
entries.翫: Phono-semantic compound: 習 (learn, become familiar, semantic) + 元 (phonetic).
entries.翮: Phono-semantic compound: 鬲 (phonetic) + 羽 (feather; wing, semantic).
entries.翰: Phono-semantic compound: 倝 (phonetic) + 羽 (feather, semantic).
entries.翹: Phono-semantic compound: 堯 (phonetic) + 羽 (feather, semantic).
entries.翻: Phono-semantic compound: 番 (phonetic) + 羽 (wings, semantic) – to flutter.
entries.翾: Phono-semantic compound: 睘 (phonetic) + 羽 (wings, semantic)
entries.耀: Phono-semantic compound: 光 (light; beam; ray, semantic) + 翟 (phonetic).
entries.老:
Compound ideogram: 人 (man) + 毛 (hair) + 匕 (cane) – a man with long hair (an old man), leaning on a cane. Compare top component to 孝.

Cognate to 考; the most commonly cited example of 轉注.
entries.耂: A bent-over figure with long hair, an old man, as component of 老 and 孝.
entries.考:
Variant of 老 – Compound ideogram: 耂 (an old man with long hair, bent over) + 丂 (a walking cane) originally drawn as 匕 – an old man, leaning on a cane. Compare top component to 孝.

Structurally related to 老; the most commonly cited example of 轉注.
entries.者:
Pictogram – a sugarcane with full stems, with some points around (either leaves or drops of sweet liquid) and an open and smiling mouth at the bottom. This is the original character for either 蔗 or 煮. Phonetically loaned for abstract meanings.

Top component 耂 is unrelated to 老, 考, and 孝.

The variant form with an additional 丶 stroke below 耂 is influenced by Shuowen, which considered 白 as the bottom component of 者.
entries.耇: Phono-semantic compound: 老 (old, semantic) + 句 (phonetic).
entries.而: Pictogram – a beard. Original form of 耏 or 髵. See also 冄.
entries.耎: Originally the same character as 需. The characters diverged during the Han dynasty.
entries.耑: Pictogram: The initial leaves and branches of a plant on top, and its roots on the bottom. Alternatively, a person's feet and hair, signifying ends or extremity.
entries.耒: Pictogram – a wooden bifurcated plow with originally three cross lines (彡 and 丯) for the furrows of the plow, later simplified to two. This character is sometimes known as "harrow", which is slightly different from a plow.
entries.耕: Phono-semantic compound: 耒 (tilling tool, semantic) + 井 (phonetic).
entries.耙: Phono-semantic compound: 耒 (plow, semantic) + 巴 (phonetic)
entries.耜: Phono-semantic compound: 耒 (plow, semantic) + 㠯 (phonetic).
entries.耤: Phono-semantic compound: 耒 (plow, semantic) + 昔 (phonetic).
entries.耦: Phono-semantic compound: 耒 (tilling tool, semantic) + 禺 (phonetic), paired working in the fields.
entries.耨: Phono-semantic compound: 耒 (plough, semantic) + 辱 (phonetic).
entries.耴: Pictogram – possibly drooping ears or an earlobe.
entries.耵: Phono-semantic compound: 耳 (ear, semantic) + 丁 (phonetic).
entries.耺: Phono-semantic compound: 耳 (ear, semantic) + 云 (phonetic).
entries.耿: Phono-semantic compound: 烓 (phonetic) + 耳 (semantic). Alternatively Phono-semantic compound: 聖 (phonetic) + 火 (semantic).
entries.聊: Phono-semantic compound: 耳 (ear, semantic) + 卯 (phonetic). According to Shuowen, the original meaning was "tinnitus".
entries.联: Variant of 聯. Simplified from 聯. Compare 関 from 關.
entries.聖: Phono-semantic compound: 耳 (ear, semantic) + 呈 (phonetic). Compare 聽.
entries.聚: Phono-semantic compound: 取 (phonetic) + 乑 (three men, semantic).
entries.聝: Phono-semantic compound: 耳 (ear, semantic) + 或 (halberd; weapon, phonetic). Largely displaced by 馘.
entries.聞: Phono-semantic compound: 門 (phonetic) + 耳 (ear, semantic). Compare 問.
entries.聟: From the composition of 夫 (semantic) + 咠 (phonetic), with 夫 geometrically evolved into 矢 (Zhen and Cao, 2025).
entries.聢: Kokuji (created in Japan). 耳 + 定
entries.聬: Phono-semantic compound: 耳 (ear, semantic) + 翁 (phonetic).
entries.聯:
Compound ideogram: 耳 (ear) + 絲 (silk).

According to Duan Yucai, 聯 and 連 are two characters for the same word, with the former used in the Zhou dynasty and the latter in the Han dynasty.
entries.聰:
The character derives from its proto-form 悤, which represents a heart/mind with a big dot on top indicating a hole. According to Qiu Xigui and Shen Pei, it indicates an open heart and an open mind. Its original meaning was “intelligent”. Later, it became a Phono-semantic compound: 囪 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic), hence the dot on top became the pictogram of a window.

Eventually, the character evolved into, i.e. a Phono-semantic compound: 耳 (ear, semantic) + 悤 (phonetic), in which the ear symbolizes somebody willing to listen and learn quickly through hearing.
entries.聲: Phono-semantic compound: 殸 (phonetic) + 耳 (ear, semantic) and ideogramic compound—an ear hearing a chime being struck.
entries.聵: Phono-semantic compound: 耳 (ear, semantic) + 貴 (phonetic).
entries.職: Phono-semantic compound: 耳 (ear, semantic) + 戠 (phonetic).
entries.聹: Phono-semantic compound: 耳 (ear, semantic) + 寧 (phonetic).
entries.聺: Phono-semantic compound: 耳 (ear, semantic) + 察 (phonetic).
entries.聽:
Originally 𦔻, hence Compound ideogram: 耳 (ear) + 口 (mouth(s)) – to listen. Compare the top component of 聖.

Later, rewritten as Phono-semantic compound: 𡈼 (phonetic) + 耳 (ear, semantic) + 㥁 (semantic) on the right.

The simplified version, 𠯸 (later stylized as 听), is totally unrelated to the original character and it originally means "smiling".
entries.聾: Phono-semantic compound: 龍 (phonetic) + 耳 (ear, semantic) – deaf.
entries.聿:
Pictogram – or

Compound ideogram: hand (又) holding a brush (𰀁). Originally referred to 筆; later Phonetic loan – for 聿.

Unrelated to 建, in which the hand is holding a pole.
entries.肅: Unclear; a compound of 𦘒 + 𣶒. Shuowen interprets it as a person sweeping or walking with a staff near an abyss, trembling in fear.
entries.肇: Phono-semantic compound: 肁 (phonetic) + 攴 (hand action, semantic).
entries.肉: Pictogram – ribs of an animal’s torso or simply a physical representation of a slice of meat. Stylized into 月 when next to a phonetic component and 𱼀 and/or 夕 inside some characters.
entries.肋: Phono-semantic compound: 力 (phonetic) + 肉 (meat; body part, semantic).
entries.肖:
Phono-semantic compound: 小 (phonetic) + 月 (moon, semantic). The character may have been the original form of 宵.

Shuowen Jiezi has erroneously analyzed the character as a Phono-semantic compound: 小 (phonetic) + 肉 (meat, semantic).
entries.肛: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (flesh; body, semantic) + 工 (phonetic).
entries.肝: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (flesh; body part, semantic) + 干 (phonetic).
entries.股:
Originally written 夃, according to 趙平安. Later the 夃 component came to be written 殳, and a 肉 component was added, making the modern form an Compound ideogram: 肉 (body, semantic) + 夃 (thigh, phonetic).

Shuowen incorrectly considered it Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (body, semantic) + 殳 (action, phonetic) – the hips as an active part of the body.
entries.肢: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (flesh, semantic) + 支 (phonetic).
entries.肤: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (flesh, semantic) + 夫 (phonetic).
entries.肥:
Shuowen Jiezi: Compound ideogram: 肉 (meat) + 卪 (person kneeling).

 posits that its actually a Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (semantic) + 妃 (phonetic).
entries.肨: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat; flesh, semantic) + 丰 (phonetic).
entries.肪: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat/flesh, semantic) + 方 (phonetic).
entries.肯: Compound ideogram: 冎 (bone) + 肉 (meat) – meat attached to the bone. Originally 肎 or 𦘫; the top component was later corrupted to 止.
entries.肰: Compound ideogram: 肉 (meat, semantic) + 犬 (dog, semantic).
entries.肱: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat, semantic) + 厷 (phonetic). 厷 is the original form of this character.
entries.育:
Evolved geometrically from 胄 in Han dynasty era.

Before that, Pronunciation 1 was written as 毓; see there for more.
entries.肴:
Phono-semantic compound: 爻 (phonetic) + 肉 (meat, semantic) – meat dishes.

Current form resembles 乂 + 有 – the lower of has moved to the side and down.
entries.肺: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat; flesh, semantic) + 巿 (phonetic).
entries.胃:
Pictogram: a stomach with food inside, originally appearing as 𱕻. A semantic 肉 was added later to differentiate.

The bronze script form merely consisted of two concentric circles. An inner portion of the character was later added, namely a mutated form of the seal script character of 米 ("rice"), representing grains within the stomach (see also 鬯).

The character looked like 𦞅 in the small seal script. In the clerical script form, the upper component was simplified to the unrelated 田 as an instance of libian simplification.

The ancient form of the character can be seen within the lower component of 𦳊.
entries.胄: Diverged from a variant of 冑. Now a Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (semantic) + 由 (phonetic).
entries.胆: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (body part, semantic) + 旦 (phonetic).
entries.背: Phono-semantic compound: 北 (phonetic) + 肉 (meat, semantic). Originally written as 北, semantic 肉 was added to be distinguished from the derived meaning of 北 (“north”).
entries.胐: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (flesh; meat, semantic) + 出 (phonetic).
entries.胑: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (flesh, semantic) + 只 (phonetic).
entries.胓: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (flesh, semantic) + 平 (phonetic).
entries.胘: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat; flesh, semantic) + 玄 (phonetic).
entries.胛: Phono-semantic compound: 甲 (phonetic) + 肉 (flesh, semantic).
entries.胞: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (flesh, semantic) + 包 (a shape representing a pregnant figure, phonetic). It conveys the meaning of the membrane that encloses the fetus.
entries.胡: Phono-semantic compound: 古 (phonetic) + 肉 (meat, semantic).
entries.胤:
Compound ideogram: 八 (divide) + 幺 (thread) + 肉 (flesh). 

肉 represents the bloodline, 幺 represents its extension, 八 represents the split of the bloodline.
entries.胥: Phono-semantic compound: 疋 (phonetic) + 肉 (flesh, semantic)
entries.胳: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (flesh, semantic) + 各 (phonetic).
entries.胴: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (flesh, semantic) + 同 (phonetic). It expresses the meaning of a large intestine.
entries.胸: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat, semantic) + 匈 (phonetic). 匈 is the original form of this character, with 肉 added later.
entries.胺: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat, semantic) + 安 (phonetic).
entries.能: Pictogram: a bear. Compare 熊. In the character, two paws are visible as a pair of 匕 and the face with the open mouth is stylized as 月.
entries.胿: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat, semantic) + 圭 (phonetic).
entries.脁:
Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat, semantic) + 兆 (phonetic).

Note that the left component is not 月, distinguish 朓.
entries.脂: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat, semantic) + 旨 (phonetic).
entries.脊: Originally a Pictogram – of a fish spine. 肉 was added later to distinguish it. The top component corrupted into 𠦬, making it a Phono-semantic compound: 朿 (phonetic) + 肉 (flesh, semantic).
entries.脖: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (flesh, semantic) + 孛 (phonetic).
entries.脙: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (flesh; meat, semantic) + 求 (phonetic)
entries.脛: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat, semantic) + 巠 (phonetic)
entries.脣: Phono-semantic compound: 辰 (phonetic) + 肉 (flesh, semantic).
entries.脧: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (flesh; meat, semantic) + 夋 (phonetic).
entries.脩: Phono-semantic compound: 攸 (phonetic) + 肉 (meat, semantic)
entries.脪: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (flesh, semantic) + 希 (phonetic)
entries.脰: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat; flesh, semantic) + 豆 (phonetic).
entries.脷: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat, semantic) + 利 (phonetic). Specialization of 利.
entries.脹: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat, semantic) + 長 (phonetic).
entries.脺: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat, semantic) + 卒 (phonetic).
entries.脾: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (organ, semantic) + 卑 (phonetic).
entries.腊: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat, semantic) + 昔 (phonetic).
entries.腋:
Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (flesh, semantic) + 夜 (phonetic).

Originally written 亦, see there for more.
entries.腍: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (flesh; meat, semantic) + 念 (phonetic).
entries.腎: Phono-semantic compound: 臤 (phonetic) + 肉 (meat; flesh, semantic) – a body part, the kidneys.
entries.腐: Phono-semantic compound: 府 (phonetic) + 肉 (flesh; body, semantic).
entries.腓: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (flesh, semantic) + 非 (phonetic).
entries.腔: Compound ideogram: 肉 (meat; flesh, semantic) + 空 (empty; hollow, phonetic).
entries.腕: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat, body part, semantic) + 宛 (phonetic) – a part of the body.
entries.腚: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (flesh, semantic) + 定 (phonetic).
entries.腡: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (body, semantic) + 咼 (phonetic).
entries.腥: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat; flesh, semantic) + 星 (phonetic)
entries.腦: Originally 匘, an Compound ideogram: 匕 + 巛 (hair) + 囟 (head; fontanel). 匕 was later replaced with 肉.
entries.腩: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat; flesh, semantic) + 南 (phonetic).
entries.腫: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat, flesh, semantic) + 重 (phonetic).
entries.腬: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat, semantic) + 柔 (phonetic).
entries.腰: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (flesh, semantic) + 要 (phonetic).
entries.腱: Originally 䇟. Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat; flesh, semantic) + 建 (phonetic).
entries.腳: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat, body, semantic) + 卻 (phonetic) – part of the body, the foot or leg.
entries.腵: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (flesh, semantic) + 叚 (phonetic).
entries.腸: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (body, semantic) + 昜 (phonetic).
entries.腹: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat; flesh, semantic) + 复 (phonetic) – a part of the body.
entries.腿: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (flesh, semantic) + 退 (phonetic).
entries.膀: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat; flesh, semantic) + 旁 (phonetic).
entries.膊: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (body, semantic) + 尃 (phonetic).
entries.膋: Phono-semantic compound: 勞 (phonetic) + 肉 (meat, semantic).
entries.膏: Phono-semantic compound: 高 (phonetic) + 肉 (meat, semantic).
entries.膓: This is the unorthodox form (俗字) of 腸 according to the Kangxi dictionary.
entries.膘: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (flesh, meat, semantic) + 票 (phonetic)
entries.膚: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat, semantic) + 盧 (phonetic).
entries.膛: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (flesh, meat, semantic) + 堂 (phonetic). A post-classical character that appears in the 玉篇.
entries.膝:
Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat, body, semantic) + 桼 (phonetic) – the knee.

Originally 厀, a Phono-semantic compound: 桼 (phonetic) + 卩 (kneeling person, semantic).
entries.膞: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (body, semantic) + 專 (phonetic).
entries.膟: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat, semantic) + 率 (phonetic).
entries.膠: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat; flesh, semantic) + 翏 (phonetic).
entries.膣:
Simplified from 窒.

Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (flesh, semantic) + 窒 (phonetic).
entries.膤:
Kokuji (created in Japan). 

Compound ideogram: 肉 (flesh) + 雪 (snow).
entries.膥:
Compound of 未成肉.

See also 𣚺.
entries.膨: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat; flesh, semantic) + 彭 (phonetic).
entries.膩: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat, semantic) + 貳 (phonetic).
entries.膫: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (body, semantic) + 尞 (phonetic).
entries.膮: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat, semantic) + 堯 (phonetic).
entries.膽: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (body part, semantic) + 詹 (phonetic).
entries.膿: Current form in the regular script is Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat, semantic) + 農 (phonetic).
entries.臀: Phono-semantic compound: 殿 (phonetic) + 肉 (flesh, semantic).
entries.臂: Phono-semantic compound: 辟 (phonetic) + 肉 (meat; flesh, semantic).
entries.臄: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat, semantic) + 豦 (phonetic).
entries.臆: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (body, semantic) + 意 (phonetic).
entries.臈: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat, semantic) + 葛 (phonetic).
entries.臉: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (body part, semantic) + 僉 (phonetic).
entries.臊: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat; flesh, semantic) + 喿 (phonetic)
entries.臍: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat; flesh, semantic) + 齊 (phonetic).
entries.臓:
Japanese shinjitai Simplified from 臟.

In current form Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (body, semantic) + 蔵 (phonetic) – a kind of body part.
entries.臘: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (meat, semantic) + 巤 (phonetic).
entries.臞: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (flesh, semantic) + 瞿 (phonetic).
entries.臟: Phono-semantic compound: 肉 (flesh, semantic) + 藏 (phonetic).
entries.臠: Phono-semantic compound: 䜌 (phonetic) + 肉 (meat, semantic).
entries.臣:
Pictogram – A vertical eye of a man looking downwards. As an individual character it has taken on the meanings “slave; servant; minister”, while the meaning relating to eyes appears when used as a radical, such as in 臨 and 監.

Compare 目. Unrelated to 𦣞.
entries.臥: Compound ideogram: 臣 (eye pointing down) + 人 (person).
entries.臦: Compound ideogram: from two ministers (臣) back to back – to go against.
entries.臧:
Compound ideogram: 臣 (eye) + 戈 (spear/weapon) – "slave; prisoner of war" (slaves in ancient China were blinded, hence the 臣 component.) Hence, the original version is 𦣣.

The phonetic component 爿, absent in the oracle-bone script, was added at a later stage (see, and references therein), leading Shuowen to interpret the character as a Phono-semantic compound: 戕 (phonetic) + 臣 (semantic).

Perhaps borrowed phonetically to mean "generous".

See also 童, 民, and 盲.
entries.臨:
Compound ideogram: 臣 (eye, semantic) + 人 (person, semantic) + 品 (objects, phonetic) – a person looking down at some objects.

Alternatively analyzed as a Phono-semantic compound: 臥 (semantic) + 品 (phonetic).
entries.自:
Pictogram: a nose — original form of 鼻. Later phonetically borrowed as an instance of Phonetic loan – for 自.

Folk etymology considers the meaning to arise from a habit of pointing at one’s nose to indicate oneself.
entries.臬: Compound ideogram: 自 (nose) + 木 (wood). Various explanations exist. Originally used to mean “target”.
entries.臭: Compound ideogram: 犬 (dog) + 自 (nose), referring to the dog's strong sense of smell. Original form of 嗅.
entries.臮: Phono-semantic compound: 自 (phonetic) + 乑 (three men, semantic).
entries.臱:
Original form of 邊. In oracle bone inscriptions, Phono-semantic compound: 自 (since; from, semantic) + 丙 (phonetic). It's possible that 自 was also a sound component as the original form of 鼻. In bronze inscriptions 方 was added as a semantic or phonetic component.

In the modern form, 丙 has corrupted into 穴. In the seal script form, 方 corrupted into 𠔽.
entries.至:
Ideogram: an arrow stuck into the ground. Some folk etymologies interpret the whole pictogram as an eagle catching a prey.

Compare 畀 and 矢. See also the bottom component of 睪, the original versions of 弗 and the top component of 𢦏.
entries.臼: Pictogram: a mortar. See the original version of 舂, in which a pestle is visible on top. Unrelated to the top component of 學, 兒, 䳔, 鼠, and 叟.
entries.臽:
In the oracle bone script, an Compound ideogram: 鹿 (deer) + 凵 (pit) – a deer falling into a trap.

From the Chinese bronze inscriptions, now an Compound ideogram: 人 (person) + 臼 (trap) – a person falling into a trap.

Original form of 陷.
entries.臾: Compound ideogram: 𦥑 (two hands) + 人 (person) – two hands dragging a person. Compare 曳.
entries.臿: Compound ideogram: 干 (pestle) + 臼 (mortar) meaning "to grind".
entries.舀: Compound ideogram: 爪 (hand) + 臼 (mortar, vessel).
entries.舁: Compound ideogram: 𦥑 (a pair of hands) + 廾 (a pair of hands). Many modern forms corrupt the top component into the unrelated 臼 (“mortar”).
entries.舂: Compound ideogram: 廾 (both hands) + 午 (pestle) + 臼 (mortar) – using both hands to pound with a mortar and pestle. See also the top component of 秦.
entries.舄: Pictogram: a kind of bird. A more conservative variant is 舃.
entries.舅: Phono-semantic compound: 臼 (phonetic) + 男 (male; man, semantic).
entries.與: Phono-semantic compound: 舁 (phonetic) + 牙 (phonetic). Both components are phonetic. The closest version to the original is 𦥸.
entries.興:
Compound ideogram – four hands (舁) lifting an object. 

In oracle bone script and early bronze inscriptions, the central object had various shapes (such as a lifting tray, sometimes resembling 井). It eventually standardized into 同 in later scripts.
entries.舉: Phono-semantic compound: 與 (phonetic) + 手 (hand, semantic) as 擧. The 手 component became 𰀁. Related to 奉.
entries.舍: Phono-semantic compound: 余 (phonetic) + 口 (semantic). 余 is the original pictogram for this word; 口 was added later to distinguish.
entries.舐:
Phono-semantic compound: 舌 (tongue, semantic) + 氏 (phonetic).

The glyphs recorded in Shuowen are 舓 (with phonetic 易) and 𦧇 (with phonetic 也).
entries.舔: Phono-semantic compound: 舌 (tongue, semantic) + 忝 (phonetic).
entries.舖: Phono-semantic compound: 舍 (house, dwelling, semantic) + 甫 (phonetic).
entries.舗: The original character is 鋪. Phono-semantic compound: 金 (metal, semantic) + 甫 (phonetic). It originally referred to a metal fitting used to attach a metal ring to a door. Its phonetic component is related to 布 and 敷, and had their meanings ("spreading" or "laying out") borrowed, which later extended to mean "store" or "shop." The modern standard form of the character had its semantic component changed to 舎 (meaning "house" or "building") to emphasize its meaning as a "store" or "shop."
entries.舛:
Compound ideogram: 夊 + 𡕒 (second character roughly ヰ) – two feet facing in the same direction. Compare ⽨, with feet in different directions (and hence divergent); compare 夅, with feet pointing down; compare feet in 步. Compare also footprint in 夂, 夊, 𡕒, and 韋.

Note that the left foot has changed shape rather more than the right foot, which still resembles the form in earlier script.
entries.舜: Altered from seal script form 䑞.
entries.舞: Phono-semantic compound: 無 (phonetic) + 舛 (steps, feet in convergent direction, semantic). This character was coined to preserve the original meaning of 無, which is "dancing"; hence, the upper component also adds part of the meaning. A conservative variant is 𦨅.
entries.舟:
Pictogram – a boat.

Later sometimes written as 月, 肉 or 凡 in components.
entries.航: Phono-semantic compound: 舟 (boat, semantic) + 亢 (phonetic).
entries.舫: Phono-semantic compound: 舟 (boat, semantic) + 方 (phonetic).
entries.般: The proto-form of 盤 + 攴. The proto-form of 盤 was later corrupted into 舟, and 攴 evolved into 殳.
entries.舯: Phono-semantic compound: 舟 (boat, semantic) + 中 (phonetic).
entries.舵: Phono-semantic compound: 舟 (boat, semantic) + 它 (phonetic).
entries.舶: Phono-semantic compound: 舟 (boat, semantic) + 白 (phonetic).
entries.舷: Phono-semantic compound: 舟 (boat, semantic) + 玄 (phonetic).
entries.船: Phono-semantic compound: 舟 (boat, semantic) + 㕣 (phonetic).
entries.舺: Phono-semantic compound: 舟 (boat, semantic) + 甲 (phonetic)
entries.艇: Phono-semantic compound: 舟 (boat, semantic) + 廷 (phonetic)
entries.艘: Phono-semantic compound: 舟 (boat, semantic) + 叟 (phonetic).
entries.艙: Considered a 後起字. Phono-semantic compound: 舟 (boat, semantic) + 倉 (phonetic).
entries.艚: Phono-semantic compound: 舟 (boat, semantic) + 曹 (phonetic).
entries.艮: Compound ideogram: 目 (eye) + 人 (person) — a person looking back to introduce the concept of disobedience and/or limit. Similar but unrelated to 見.
entries.色:
Compound ideogram: 爪 (claw; hand) + 卩 (kneeling person). It depicts a hand pressing down on a kneeling person. 色 was an ancient form of 印; they both originally meant "to press down", meaning now written with 抑. The character was later borrowed phonetically to mean "color".

Shuowen interprets this character as an Compound ideogram: 人 (person; human) + 卪, which refers to the expression, vitality or complexion of a person's face.

Sometimes, especially in folk etymology, the character is misinterpreted as a proto-form of 絕. The bottom part is unrelated to 巴.
entries.艸:
Pictogram – grass blades.

屮 (grass). See also the top component of 春 in its original version (萅).

䒑, used in 前, is sometimes presented as a variant of this character, but it actually represents a foot 止 over a boat.
entries.艺:
Simplified from 藝.

Under simplification, Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (semantic) + 乙 (phonetic).
entries.艾: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass, semantic) + 乂 (phonetic).
entries.芃: 艸 (grass) + 凡 – growth (of plants, grass).
entries.芋: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass; plant, semantic) + 于 (phonetic) – taro.
entries.芍: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass; plant, semantic) + 勺 (phonetic).
entries.芐: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass; plant, semantic) + 下 (phonetic).
entries.芒: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass, semantic) + 亡 (phonetic); perhaps, its original form was 方.
entries.芙: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass, semantic) + 夫 (phonetic).
entries.芝: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass, semantic) + 之 (phonetic) – a type of plant.
entries.芡: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass, semantic) + 欠 (phonetic).
entries.芣: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass; plant, semantic) + 不 (phonetic).
entries.芥: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass, plant, semantic) + 介 (phonetic) – a type of plant.
entries.芦: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (plant, semantic) + 户 (phonetic).
entries.芫: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass; plant, semantic) + 元 (phonetic).
entries.芬: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass, semantic) + 分 (phonetic)
entries.芭: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass, semantic) + 巴 (phonetic).
entries.芮: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass, semantic) + 內 (phonetic).
entries.芯: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass; plant, semantic) + 心 (phonetic).
entries.花: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass; plant, semantic) + 化 (phonetic). Originally 𠌶 or 華 before the Han dynasty.
entries.芳: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass, semantic) + 方 (phonetic)
entries.芻: Compound ideogram: 勹 (hand) + 屮 (grass), a hand plucking grass.
entries.芼: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass, semantic) + 毛 (phonetic)
entries.芽: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass, semantic) + 牙 (phonetic).
entries.苊: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass; plant, semantic) + 厄 (phonetic).
entries.苏: Simplified from 蘇. via the Cursive script (East Asia).
entries.苒: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass, plant, semantic) + 冉 (phonetic).
entries.苓: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass, plant, semantic) + 令 (phonetic).
entries.苜: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass; plant, semantic) + 目 (phonetic).
entries.苟: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (semantic) + 句 (phonetic) – a kind of grass, in original sense.
entries.苤: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass; plant, semantic) + 丕 (phonetic).
entries.若:
Pictogram – a person combing their hair; obedient.

Later 口 was added and the original component came to be written 叒.
entries.苦: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass, semantic) + 古 (phonetic) – bitter (as in bitter plants).
entries.英: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass, semantic) + 央 (phonetic).
entries.苴: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass, semantic) + 且 (phonetic).
entries.苸: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass, semantic) + 乎 (phonetic).
entries.苽: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass; plant, semantic) + 瓜 (phonetic).
entries.茂:
Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass, semantic) + 戊 (phonetic).

Applying this character to mean “cyclopentadiene” in organic chemistry results from the decomposition of the character as an Compound ideogram: 艸 (radical for aromatic compounds) + 戊 (five-carbon ring), since the conjugate base of cyclopentadiene (cyclopentadienyl anion) is aromatic.
entries.范: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass, semantic) + 氾 (phonetic).
entries.茄: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass; plant, semantic) + 加 (phonetic).
entries.茅: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (plant, semantic) + 矛 (phonetic).
entries.茉:
Simplified from 末.

Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass, semantic) + 末 (phonetic).
entries.茍:
May represent a sitting dog, hence a dog showing respect and obedience.

Alternatively, Compound ideogram: 羊 (sheep) + 卩 (kneeling person), hence it represents a barbarian while kneeling perhaps as a form of respect. The character is similar to 羌, in which however the man is standing.

See 敬. Perhaps unrelated to 狗 according to the earlier versions.
entries.茐:
Simplified from 蔥.

Simplified from 葱.
entries.茓: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass, semantic) + 穴 (phonetic).
entries.茗: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass; plant, semantic) + 名 (phonetic).
entries.茜: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass; plant, semantic) + 西 (phonetic).
entries.茫: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass; plant, semantic) + 汒 (phonetic).
entries.茭: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass; plant, semantic) + 交 (phonetic)
entries.茱: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass, semantic) + 朱 (phonetic).
entries.茴: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass; plant, semantic) + 回 (phonetic).
entries.茶:
Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (semantic) + 余 (phonetic).

茶, then slightly modified into a more conservative 茶, originates as a graphical modification of archaic 荼, used for “tea” in classical sources. The modern version is unrelated to the bottom right component of 條.
entries.茸: Shuowen: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass, semantic) + 聰 (phonetic) (Shuowen).
entries.茹: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass, plants, semantic) + 如 (phonetic) – plant roots, part of a plant.
entries.茻: Ideogram – - 艸 (grass) written two times, representing a multitude of grass.
entries.茿: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass, semantic) + 筑 (phonetic).
entries.荃: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass/plant, semantic) + 全 (phonetic).
entries.荅: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass; plant, semantic) + 合 (phonetic).
entries.荇: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass, semantic) + 行 (phonetic).

entries.莅:
Found in various historical dictionaries such as Yupian 《玉篇》 and Guangyun 《廣韻》.

In the 1956 first round revision table of variant Chinese characters (第一批异体字整理表) by the People's Republic of China, 蒞 and 涖 were listed as Variant Chinese characters that were replaced by 莅 as the orthodox form.

The bottom was later distorted into 大.

entries.虍:

Compare 虎 which includes the body.
entries.虐: In the oracle bone script, an Compound ideogram: 虎 (tiger) + 人 (person) — a tiger about to eat a person. Meaning later extended to mean "cruel", "tyrannical".
entries.虔:

According to, the phonetic component is instead 虍.
entries.處: Phono-semantic compound: 虍 (phonetic) + 夂 (semantic) + 几 (table, semantic).
entries.虛: Phono-semantic compound: 虍 (phonetic) + 丘 (hill, semantic). The lower component retains the shape of 丠, the ancient form of 丘.
entries.虞: Phono-semantic compound: 虍 (tiger, semantic) + 吳 (phonetic).
entries.號:
Originally an Ideogram – of a tiger with a line representing exhaled air while roaring, thus meaning "to roar; to shout". Later forms added 口 or 言 to emphasize the act of crying or calling. 号 derives from 口 and the line 丂.

In the current form, an Compound ideogram: 号 (to wail, phonetic) + 虎 (tiger, semantic).
entries.虠: Phono-semantic compound: 交 (phonetic) + 虎 (tiger, semantic).
entries.虢:
爪 + 攴 + 虎.

One theory considers this character a Pictogram: two hands (寽) opening tiger (虎)'s fur, thus an original glyph of 鞹. (Lin Yiguang)

Shuowen: Phono-semantic compound: 寽 (phonetic) + 虎 (tiger, semantic). However, this is not generally considered likely.
entries.虧: Phono-semantic compound: 雐 (phonetic) + 亏 (exhale, semantic).
entries.虫:
Pictogram: a snake.

The character originally represented a type of venomous snake, while the derivative 蟲 represented worms and insects (or insect-like things). 虫 was later borrowed for 蟲 (possibly via simplification), and the character 虺 was created to represent the original meaning.

The non-contracted form is 蜑. In the current version, 延 is abbreviated to 疋.

This character was coined at a late stage in Chinese, since it is unattested on oracle bones, bronzes, Shuowen Jiezi and Guangyun.

entries.蜀:
The upper component 𦉶 is attested independently in Shang oracle bone script, showing a large 目 with a short hooked stroke. Jiang Yubin (蔣玉斌) identifies it as the original character for 獨, while Chen Jian (陳劍) and Guo Yongbing (郭永秉) read it as 矚, taking the non-目 portion as a figure leaning on a staff. Both words belong to a *dok family associated with focused vision and conspicuousness (cf. 燭). The form with added 虫 first appears in Western Zhou inscriptions for the Shu place name; Shuowen Jiezi reanalyzes it as a pictogram of a silkworm.

Attested as early as in Western Zhou oracle bone H11:68: 伐蜀 (attack Shu), H11:97: 克蜀 (defeat Shu).
