entries.闐: Phono-semantic compound: 門 (gate, semantic) + 眞 (phonetic)
entries.闑: Phono-semantic compound: 門 (door, semantic) + 臬 (phonetic).
entries.闖: Compound ideogram – a horse (馬) rushing through a gate (門).
entries.關:
The bronze inscription was in the form of 門 + 卝. 卝 might also serve as a phonetic component. The whole character represents a door locked with two wooden sticks.

Then, the character slightly evolved into Phono-semantic compound: 門 (door, semantic) + 𢇅 (phonetic), in which two couples of rings similar to 幺幺 are visible on top of the two wooden sticks.
entries.闟: Phono-semantic compound: 門 (door, semantic) + 翕 (phonetic).
entries.闡: Phono-semantic compound: 門 (double door, semantic) + 單 (phonetic).
entries.闢:
In the bronze script, an Compound ideogram: 門 (door) + 𠬜 (two hands pushing open the door) – to open.

Since the seal script, now a Phono-semantic compound: 門 (semantic) + 辟 (phonetic).

Compare 開.
entries.闤: Phono-semantic compound: 門 (door, semantic) + 睘 (phonetic)
entries.队: Under simplification, Compound ideogram: 阜 (mound, abundant, rich, many) + 人 (people) many people = team.
entries.阡: Phono-semantic compound: 阜 (soil mountain, semantic) + 千 (phonetic).
entries.阪: Phono-semantic compound: 阜 (mound, semantic) + 反 (phonetic) – hill, slope.
entries.阳:
An unorthodox variant Simplified from 陽. which can be found in various historical dictionaries such as the Kangxi dictionary. 

Eventually adopted as an official simplified character by the People's Republic of China in 1956.
entries.阴:
An unorthodox variant Simplified from 陰. which can be found in various historical dictionaries such as the Kangxi dictionary. 

Eventually adopted as an official simplified character by the People's Republic of China in 1956.
entries.阿: Phono-semantic compound: 阜 (semantic) + 可 (phonetic): Originally meaning a big mound.
entries.陁:
Simplified from 陀.

Phono-semantic compound: 阜 (soil mountain, semantic) + 㐌 (phonetic)
entries.陂: Phono-semantic compound: 阜 (soil mountain, semantic) + 皮 (phonetic).
entries.降: Phono-semantic compound: 阜 (hill, wall, semantic) + 夅 (to descend, phonetic) – descending a hill.
entries.限: Phono-semantic compound: 阜 (mound, semantic) + 艮 (phonetic). It conveys the meaning of "limit" or "boundary."
entries.陗: Phono-semantic compound: 阜 (soil mountain, semantic) + 肖 (phonetic)
entries.陟: Compound ideogram: 阜 (mound; hill; raised ground) + 步 (step; two feet pointing upwards). Cf. 降, with two feet pointing downwards.
entries.陣: Derivation from 敶, itself derived from an Compound ideogram: 東 (sack?) + 東 + 攴; later, one 東 was abbreviated, and a 阜 added on the left.
entries.陪:
Phono-semantic compound: 阜 (soil mountain, semantic) + 咅 (phonetic)

The 阜 suggests, by extension from the meaning of “pile up soil”, to join up with, to be close to: to accompany.
entries.陯: Phono-semantic compound: 阜 (mound, semantic) + 侖 (phonetic)
entries.陰: According to Shuowen, a Phono-semantic compound: 阜 (semantic) + 侌 (phonetic).
entries.陲: Phono-semantic compound: 阜 (soil mountain, semantic) + 垂 (phonetic)
entries.陳: Phono-semantic compound: 阜 (mound, semantic) + 東 (phonetic) – to display; to arrange.
entries.陵: Compound ideogram: 阜 (mound, semantic) + 夌 (mound; hill, phonetic). Originally written 夌.
entries.陶:
In oracle bone and bronze inscriptions, Compound ideogram: 阜 (mound of dirt) + 勹 (two people) + 土 (earth) – "to dig", original character of 掏. The shapes beneath the outermost 勹 were corrupted in bamboo slips, arriving at the modern form 缶 in seal script. 

Now a Phono-semantic compound: 阜 (soil mountain, semantic) + 匋 (make pottery, phonetic).
entries.陷: Phono-semantic compound: 阜 (semantic) + 臽 (to fall into a trap, phonetic). 臽 is the pictographic protoform of this character; 阜 was added later to differentiate.
entries.陽: Phono-semantic compound: 阜 (hill, semantic) + 昜 (sunshine, phonetic). 昜 is the original character for this word, 阜 was added later.
entries.隆: Phono-semantic compound: 降 (phonetic) + 生 (semantic), with 𡕒 later dropped.
entries.隋:
Phono-semantic compound: 隓 (phonetic) + 肉 (meat, semantic).

The use of this character for the dynasty name was created by Emperor Wen of Sui from the character 隨.
entries.隔: Phono-semantic compound: 阜 (wall, semantic) + 鬲 (phonetic) – to separate with a wall.
entries.隗: Phono-semantic compound: 阜 (soil mountain, semantic) + 鬼 (phonetic).
entries.隬: Phono-semantic compound: 阜 (mound, semantic) + 爾 (phonetic).
entries.隱: Shuowen: Phono-semantic compound: 阜 (semantic) + 㥯 (phonetic).
entries.隸: Phono-semantic compound: 柰 (phonetic) + 隶 (arrest, semantic).
entries.隹:
Pictogram: a short‐tailed bird (e.g. a sparrow). In addition to referring to 隹, it also is the original form of 鷕 with the intermediate form 唯.

Compare 鳥.
entries.隻:
Compound ideogram: 隹 (short-tailed bird) + 又 (hand).

To hold one bird is 隻; to hold two birds is 雙.
entries.隼: The upper component is a reference to a bird with a short tail, in this case a falcon, and is used both as a semantic and phonetic component. Originally, it was written as 鵻. Then it became 隼 and eventually 鶽.
entries.难:
Unorthodox variant Simplified from 難. (elimination of left component to 又) found in the Ming dynasty orthographic dictionary 《俗書刊誤》. 

Originally part of the 324 simplified characters introduced by the Republic of China (Kuomintang government) in 1935 but was later retracted in 1936. 

Eventually adopted as an official simplified character by the People's Republic of China in the 1956 Chinese Character Simplification Scheme.
entries.雀:
Compound ideogram: 小 (small) + 隹 (bird) – a small bird, a sparrow.

In the current form, the upper part looks like 少, but what looks like the bottom stroke of 少 is actually the upper left stroke of 隹, extended.
entries.雁: Phono-semantic compound: 厂 (phonetic) + 人 (semantic) + 隹 (semantic).
entries.雅: Phono-semantic compound: 隹 (a short-tailed bird, semantic) + 牙 (phonetic). It represents the meaning of a rook, which is a type of crow. By extension, it is used metaphorically to mean "elegant" or "refined."
entries.集:
Compound ideogram: 隹 (bird) + 木 (tree).

The variant 雧 shows three birds instead.
entries.雍: Variant form of 雝. It is likely that the phonetic component 邕 corrupted into 玄 at some point since their shapes looked similar in pre-Qin scripts.
entries.雎: Phono-semantic compound: 且 (phonetic) + 隹 (bird, semantic).
entries.雑:
Unorthodox variant of 雜. Compare 卆 from 卒.

The modern Japanese usage is of reform (shinjitai) nature.
entries.雖:
Phono-semantic compound: 虫 (semantic) + 唯 (phonetic). Hence, the variant which represents the correct division of component is 𧐌.

Originally meaning "a lizard-like reptile", the character has been phonetically borrowed to represent the sense "although".
entries.雗: Phono-semantic compound: 倝 (phonetic) + 隹 (pheasant, semantic)
entries.雙: Compound ideogram: 雔 (two birds) + 又 (hand) – Represents two birds (隹) in someone's right hand (又).
entries.雚: Pictogram – a stork. Now written 鸛. Originally the same character as 雈, but 吅 was added as early as the Shang dynasty. considers the phonetic component of 雚 to be 雈, while the Shuowen Jiezi considers it to be 吅.
entries.雛: Phono-semantic compound: 芻 (phonetic) + 隹 (bird, semantic).
entries.雜: Phono-semantic compound: 衣 (semantic) + 集 (phonetic) with an original reference to a combination of various colours put together, perhaps linked to dyed clothes. A more comprehensible variant is 襍.
entries.雝: Original meaning unknown. In oracle bone inscriptions, Phono-semantic compound: 宮 (phonetic) + 隹 (bird, semantic). The phonetic component is not 吕, but ancient form of 宮. Some variants also contained 水. In the Warring States period the 吕 below 水 had corrupted into 邑, making 邕 the new phonetic component.
entries.雞: Phono-semantic compound: 奚 (phonetic) + 隹 (short-tailed bird, semantic).
entries.難: Phono-semantic compound: 暵 (phonetic) + 隹 (bird, semantic) – a type of bird. Phonetically borrowed for other senses.
entries.雩: Phono-semantic compound: 雨 (rain, semantic) + 于 (phonetic).
entries.雪: Ancient simplification of 䨮, which is in turn Phono-semantic compound: 雨 (rain, semantic) + 彗 (phonetic).
entries.雫:
Simplified from 霞.

Phono-semantic compound: 雨 (rain, semantic) + 下 (phonetic).
entries.雰: Phono-semantic compound: 雨 (rain, semantic) + 分 (divide, small, phonetic).
entries.雲: Compound ideogram: 雨 (rain, semantic) + 云 (cloud, phonetic). Originally written 云, with the 雨 radical added to 云 to distinguish from the borrowed sense of “to speak”.
entries.零: Phono-semantic compound: 雨 (rain, semantic) + 令 (phonetic). On the oracle bone script, only thick raindrops are depicted falling from the sky.
entries.雷: Ancient simplification of 靁, which was a Phono-semantic compound: 雨 (rain, semantic) + 畾 (phonetic).
entries.雹: Phono-semantic compound: 雨 (rain, semantic) + 包 (phonetic).
entries.雺: Phono-semantic compound: 雨 (rain, semantic) + 矛 (phonetic).
entries.電: Phono-semantic compound: 雨 (rain, semantic) + 申 (phonetic); also Compound ideogram: 雨 + 申.
entries.需: Compound ideogram: 天 (person) + 雨 (rain) — a person getting wet in the rain. Original character of 濡. The component 天 corrupted into 而 during the Han dynasty.
entries.霂: Phono-semantic compound: 雨 (rain, semantic) + 沐 (phonetic).
entries.霄: Phono-semantic compound: 雨 (rain, semantic) + 肖 (phonetic).
entries.霆: Phono-semantic compound: 雨 (rain, semantic) + 廷 (phonetic).
entries.霉: Phono-semantic compound: 雨 (rain, semantic) + 每 (phonetic).
entries.霓: Phono-semantic compound: 兒 (phonetic) + 雨 (rain, semantic)
entries.霗:
The original form of this character is 𩆼, a historical Variant Chinese character of 零 found in the Song dynasty Chinese dictionary, Jiyun 《集韻》.

The character 𩆼 was then erroneously printed as 霗 (霝 mistakenly substituted by 雨) in the Japanese Dai Kan-Wa Jiten and subsequently found in Zhongwen Da Cidian 《中文大辭典》, a dictionary published in Taiwan from 1962 to 1968 based on the character found in the Japanese Dai Kan-Wa Jiten.

This character can also be found in the Zhonghua Zihai 《中華字海》 which cites Jiyun 《集韻》 as its source of reference.
entries.霚: Phono-semantic compound: 雨 (rain, semantic) + 敄 (phonetic).
entries.霜: Phono-semantic compound: 雨 (rain, semantic) + 相 (phonetic).
entries.霞: Phono-semantic compound: 雨 (rain, semantic) + 叚 (phonetic).
entries.霧: Phono-semantic compound: 雨 (rain, semantic) + 務 (phonetic).
entries.霱: Phono-semantic compound: 雨 (rain, semantic) + 矞 (phonetic).
entries.霸:
In oracle bone script, Compound ideogram: 革 (change) + 月 (moon) – changes in moonlight.

Bronze inscriptions added 雨 to make 䨣 a phonetic component.
entries.霺: Phono-semantic compound: 雨 (rain, semantic) + 微 (phonetic).
entries.霽: Phono-semantic compound: 雨 (rain, semantic) + 齊 (phonetic).
entries.靄: Phono-semantic compound: 雨 (rain, semantic) + 謁 (phonetic).
entries.靈:
Found as 𩆜 in Shuowen: Phono-semantic compound: 霝 (phonetic) + 玉 (jade, semantic).

The semantic component 玉 may be replaced with 巫, as in the current form, or with 心 or 示 in the ancient bronze inscription forms.
entries.靉: Phono-semantic compound: 雲 (cloud, semantic) + 愛 (phonetic)
entries.靖: Phono-semantic compound: 立 (to stand; to establish, semantic) + 青 (phonetic).
entries.非:
Pictogram – - two wings facing opposite directions. Originally, it represented wings; then, according to Xu Shen, its meaning changed into "leave; disobey" (違). Eventually, it was used perhaps as a phonetic loan to mean "not to be".

Unrelated to the Kangxi radical 韭.
entries.靡: Phono-semantic compound: 麻 (phonetic) + 非 (semantic) - to scatter.
entries.靨: Phono-semantic compound: 厭 (phonetic) + 面 (face, semantic).
entries.革: Pictogram – a stretched animal hide: the upper is head, the bottom is the tail and legs. The hands 臼 around the hide were briefly added later.
entries.靬: Phono-semantic compound: 革 (leather, semantic) + 干 (phonetic).
entries.靴: Phono-semantic compound: 革 (leather, semantic) + 化 (phonetic).
entries.鞄: Phono-semantic compound: 革 (leather, semantic) + 包 (phonetic).
entries.鞋:
Phono-semantic compound: 革 (leather, semantic) + 圭 (phonetic) – leather shoes. Originally written as 鞵.

Originally, the phonetic component is not related to the concept of earth (土) since in its original form it represents a pair of ritual axes perhaps made of jade 士. Hence, the link to the concept of earth in this character either comes from folk etymology or its appearance in the Small Seal script.
entries.鞍: Phono-semantic compound: 革 (leather, semantic) + 安 (secure).
entries.鞔: Phono-semantic compound: 革 (leather, semantic) + 免 (phonetic)
entries.鞠: A Phono-semantic compound – composed of 𥲩 (phonetic) + 米 (semantic). An earlier written form of 麴.
entries.鞦: Phono-semantic compound: 革 (leather, semantic) + 秋 (phonetic)
entries.鞧: Phono-semantic compound: 革 (leather, semantic) + 酋 (phonetic)
entries.鞪: Phono-semantic compound: 敄 (phonetic) + 革 (leather, semantic)
entries.鞭: Phono-semantic compound: 革 (leather, semantic) + 便 (phonetic).
entries.鞮: Phono-semantic compound: 革 (leather, semantic) + 是 (phonetic).
entries.鞵: Phono-semantic compound: 革 (leather, semantic) + 奚 (phonetic).
entries.鞻: Phono-semantic compound: 革 (leather, semantic) + 婁 (phonetic).
entries.韋:
Compound ideogram: 舛 + 囗 – footsteps around an enclosure. Possibly the original character for 圍 and 衛. Phonetically borrowed to indicate "tanned leather".

The footprint on top is stylized as 𫝀, which is similar but unrelated to 五.
entries.韓: Phono-semantic compound: 倝 (phonetic) + 韋 (surround, semantic).
entries.韔: Phono-semantic compound: 韋 (surround, semantic) + 長 (phonetic)
entries.韣: Phono-semantic compound: 韋 (to surround; to enclose, semantic) + 蜀 (phonetic)
entries.韭: Pictogram – leek in the ground (一). Unrelated to 非.
entries.音:
Ideogram – based on the structure of 言, with an additional short horizontal stroke inside the 口, forming a shape similar to 甘. The Shuowen Jiezi describes the structure as 从言含一 ("from 言 containing 一").

The added stroke graphically seals the mouth, likely representing partially closed or muffled vocalization, in contrast with 言. This is consistent with the *ʔəm word family, which clusters around meanings of covering and closure: compare homophones 瘖 and 喑, and 韽.

See also 言.
entries.響: Phono-semantic compound: 鄉 (phonetic) + 音 (sound, semantic).
entries.頁:
Pictogram: 首 + 卩 – head of a kneeling person, emphasising “head”.

頁 and 首 were originally the same pictographic character with the same meaning of “head”, and the graphical difference was that 頁 also included the body in addition to the head of the person.

頁 was later used as an alternative popular form of 葉 to mean “sheet; page (of paper)”, which is its main meaning today.

The original sense of “head” is preserved in the radical 頁, which is used in characters such as 頭 and 頸.
entries.頂: Phono-semantic compound: 丁 (phonetic) + 頁 (head, semantic).
entries.頃:
Compound ideogram: 匕 + 頁 (head).

The head is askew, the original meaning of 傾.
entries.項: Phono-semantic compound: 工 (phonetic) + 頁 (head, semantic).
entries.順:
Phono-semantic compound: 川 (phonetic) + 頁 (semantic).

Shuowen considers it to be an Compound ideogram: 川 (river) + 頁 (head) - flowing in the river, i.e. following/obeying the river's current. Compare the English phrase go with the flow.
entries.頇: Phono-semantic compound: 干 (phonetic) + 頁 (leaf, semantic)
entries.須: Pictogram: 彡 (hair) + 頁 (head) – a head with hair on its side – beard; whiskers — original character of 鬚. Originally a single picture, but abstracted in the seal script into a compound.
entries.頌: Phono-semantic compound: 公 (phonetic) + 頁 (head, semantic) – appearance. Now written 容.
entries.頑:
Phono-semantic compound: 元 (head, phonetic) + 頁 (head, semantic).

As 元 came to be used to mean “original”, rather than “head”, this character was formed from the original meaning of 元 + the semantic element 頁 to affirm the “head” meaning, but with the modification in meaning to “an intransigent head”; the head of a heady person.
entries.頒: Phono-semantic compound: 分 (phonetic) + 頁 (head, semantic).
entries.頓: Phono-semantic compound: 屯 (head of a kneeling person, phonetic) + 頁 (semantic). It expresses the meaning “to bow” or “to kowtow.”
entries.頜: Phono-semantic compound: 合 (phonetic) + 頁 (head, semantic).
entries.頞: Phono-semantic compound: 安 (phonetic) + 頁 (head, semantic).
entries.頟: Phono-semantic compound: 各 (phonetic) + 頁 (head, semantic).
entries.頡: Phono-semantic compound: 吉 (phonetic) + 頁 (head, semantic).
entries.頤: May have originally been written 𦣞, a Pictogram – of a chin, in which case the modern form is an Compound ideogram: 𦣞 (chin, phonetic) + 頁 (head, semantic).
entries.頪: Compound ideogram: 米 + 頁. Perhaps, according to an interpretation in the Shuowen Jiezi by Xu Shen, the first component is a contraction of 粉, which means that 頁 is the Kangxi radical.
entries.頫: Phono-semantic compound: 兆 (phonetic) + 頁 (head, semantic).
entries.頬:
Japanese shinjitai Simplified from 頰.

Phono-semantic compound: 夹 (phonetic) + 頁 (head, semantic) – part of the head.
entries.頭: Phono-semantic compound: 豆 (phonetic) + 頁 (head, semantic).
entries.頮: Pictogram: A human, head emphasised (頁), with both hands (廾) holding water (水).
entries.頰: Phono-semantic compound: 夾 (phonetic) + 頁 (head, semantic) – part of the head.
entries.頷: Phono-semantic compound: 含 (phonetic) + 頁 (head, semantic).
entries.頸: Phono-semantic compound: 巠 (phonetic) + 頁 (head, semantic).
entries.頻: Originally 瀕, Compound ideogram: a person 頁 near the water's edge 涉, extended to mean "on the verge". The water component 氵 was removed to distinguish its usage for "frequent".
entries.顆: Phono-semantic compound: 果 (phonetic) + 頁 (head, semantic).
entries.題: Phono-semantic compound: 是 (phonetic) + 頁 (head, semantic) – “forehead”.
entries.額: Phono-semantic compound: 客 (phonetic) + 頁 (head, semantic).
entries.顏:
Phono-semantic compound: 彥 (phonetic) + 頁 (head, semantic).

Bronze inscription forms: Phono-semantic compound: 产 (phonetic) + 面 (face, semantic).
entries.顔: Variant Chinese character of 顏 (彥 → 彦).
entries.顕: Japanese shinjitai character. Simplified from 顯.
entries.顙: Phono-semantic compound: 桑 (phonetic) + 頁 (head, semantic).
entries.顛: Phono-semantic compound: 真 (phonetic) + 頁 (head, semantic).
entries.顢: Phono-semantic compound: 㒼 (phonetic) + 頁 (leaf, semantic)
entries.顤: Phono-semantic compound: 堯 (phonetic) + 頁 (head, semantic)
entries.顥: Compound ideogram: 景 (daylight) + 頁 (head (hair)). According to the Shuowen Jiezi Zhu, it represents bright sunlight and the white hair in someone's head, signifying whiteness.
entries.顫: Phono-semantic compound: 亶 (phonetic) + 頁 (head, semantic).
entries.顯: Compound ideogram: 日 (sun) + 絲 (silk) + 頁 (person's head).
entries.顱: Phono-semantic compound: 盧 (phonetic) + 頁 (head, semantic).
entries.页: From cursive script (East Asia) of 頁.
entries.風:
Phonetic loan – of 鳳 borrowed for sound to represent 風, sometimes with 凡 added as a phonetic.

In Warring States Chu manuscripts the character is written as 凡 above 口 (or confused with 同) with one or two phoenix feathers beneath, or as 凡 above a single phoenix feather. In the Qin script the feather was corrupted into 虫, giving the character its modern structure of 凡 above 虫.

Shuowen misinterpreted the character 風 by associating it with insects.
entries.颪: Kokuji (created in Japan)., formed from 吹き下ろす and 風.
entries.颫: Phono-semantic compound: 風 (wind, semantic) + 夫 (phonetic)
entries.颽: Phono-semantic compound: 豈 (phonetic) + 風 (wind, semantic).
entries.飄: Phono-semantic compound: 票 (phonetic) + 風 (wind, semantic).
entries.飆: Phono-semantic compound: 猋 (phonetic) + 風 (wind, semantic).
entries.飛:
Pictogram: a bird flying upwards.

In its modern form, resembles a tasseled 升.
entries.飜: Phono-semantic compound: 番 (phonetic) + 飛 (to fly, semantic).
entries.飞: Simplified from 飛. Recorded from at least 1955 by Zhao Xi (趙曦).
entries.食:
Compound ideogram: 亼 (mouth) + 皀 (a bowl of rice on a stand). In the modern form, the bowl of rice has corrupted into the similar but unrelated 良 or 艮. The variant form 𠊊 preserves the original composition.

Shuowen interprets the 亼 as a phonetic component.
entries.飤: Compound ideogram: 食 (food; rice, phonetic) + 人 (person, semantic) – a person eating rice, feeding.
entries.飧: Compound ideogram: 夕 (night; evening; dusk) + 食 (food).
entries.飪: Phono-semantic compound: 食 (food, semantic) + 壬 (phonetic).
entries.飫: From 𩜈. Phono-semantic compound: 食 (food, semantic) + 夭 (phonetic).
entries.飯: Phono-semantic compound: 食 (food, semantic) + 反 (phonetic).
entries.飲:
In the oracle bone script, it was an Compound ideogram: 酉 (bottle (of alcoholic beverages)) + 人 (person) + 口 (mouth (occasionally with the tongue protruding)) – a person bending over a bottle to drink the alcoholic beverage. The droplets represented drops of the drink or saliva.

In the bronze script, the mouth separated from the body and corrupted into 今, while the rest of the body became 欠. These two components also acted as phonetic components. These changes were inherited in the seal script, leading Shuowen to interpret this character (㱃) as a Phono-semantic compound: 酓 (phonetic) + 欠 (yawn, semantic).

In the clerical script, 酓 has been modified to 食, which is inherited in the current form.
entries.飽:
Phono-semantic compound: 食 (food, semantic) + 包 (phonetic).

For etymology 2, the 食 radical specifies its dietary use (instead of just being a generic wrap).
entries.飾:
Phono-semantic compound: 飤 (phonetic) + 巾 (cloth, semantic).

The 人 has changed shape into 𠂉.
entries.餃: Phono-semantic compound: 食 (food, eat, semantic) + 交 (phonetic) – a kind of food.
entries.餅: Phono-semantic compound: 食 (food, semantic) + 并 (phonetic); traditional glyph form during Ming and Qing dynasty used to advocate (as in) based on the influence of Shuowen.
entries.餉: Phono-semantic compound: 食 (food, semantic) + 向 (phonetic).
entries.養: Compound ideogram: 羊 (sheep, phonetic) + 食 (to feed, semantic).
entries.餌: Phono-semantic compound: 食 (to eat, semantic) + 耳 (phonetic).
entries.餐: Phono-semantic compound: 𣦼 (phonetic) + 食 (to eat; meal; food, semantic). Its original meaning was "to swallow".
entries.餔: Phono-semantic compound: 食 (food, semantic) + 甫 (phonetic).
entries.餞: Phono-semantic compound: 食 (hand, semantic) + 戔 (phonetic)
entries.餡: Phono-semantic compound: 食 (food, semantic) + 臽 (phonetic) – a kind of food.
entries.餮: Phono-semantic compound: 殄 (phonetic) + 食 (food, semantic).
entries.餲: Phono-semantic compound: 食 (food, semantic) + 曷 (phonetic).
entries.餴: Phono-semantic compound: 食 (food, semantic) + 奔 (phonetic).
entries.餹: Phono-semantic compound: 食 (to eat, semantic) + 唐 (phonetic).
entries.餼: Phono-semantic compound: 食 (food, semantic) + 氣 (phonetic).
entries.饄: Phono-semantic compound: 食 (to eat, semantic) + 堂 (phonetic).
entries.饈: Phono-semantic compound: 食 (food, semantic) + 羞 (phonetic).
entries.饌: Phono-semantic compound: 巽 (phonetic) + 食 (food, semantic)
entries.饐: Phono-semantic compound: 食 (food; to eat, semantic) + 壹 (phonetic).
entries.饒: Phono-semantic compound: 食 (food, semantic) + 堯 (phonetic).
entries.饕: Phono-semantic compound: 號 (phonetic) + 食 (food, semantic).
entries.饙: Phono-semantic compound: 食 (food, semantic) + 賁 (phonetic)
entries.饜: Phono-semantic compound: 厭 (phonetic) + 食 (food, semantic)
entries.饞: Phono-semantic compound: 食 (to eat; food, semantic) + 毚 (phonetic).
entries.饟: Phono-semantic compound: 食 (to eat, semantic) + 襄 (phonetic)
entries.饠: Phono-semantic compound: 食 (eat, semantic) + 羅 (phonetic)
entries.饣: From cursive script (East Asia) of 飠.
entries.首: Simplified from 𩠐. Originally Pictogram – of the head of an animal with a long mouth and horns. In the oracle bone script, it appeared with or without hair (巛), but 𩠐, the form with hair, was the form that was perpetuated.
entries.馘: Phono-semantic compound: 首 (head, semantic) + 或 (phonetic). This character largely displaced 聝 in the received corpus of ancient classics. See also 𢦞.
entries.香:
In the oracle bone script, it was Compound ideogram: 黍 (glutinous millet) + 口 (mouth). The whole character perhaps indicate that millet was used to produce liquor from fermentation which could be drank and/or sacrificed.

In the seal script, the 口 was replaced with the related 甘. Hence, the most conservative variant is 𪏽.

Currently, the 黍 has simplified into 禾 and the form of the bottom component 甘 has become akin to the unrelated 曰.
entries.馝: Phono-semantic compound: 香 (fragrant, semantic) + 必 (phonetic)
entries.馥: Phono-semantic compound: 香 (fragrance, semantic) + 复 (phonetic).
entries.馦: Phono-semantic compound: 香 (fragrance, semantic) + 兼 (phonetic).
entries.馨: Phono-semantic compound: 殸 (phonetic) + 香 (sweet, semantic).
entries.馬:
Pictogram – a horse with its head facing the left, showing a flowing mane in the wind, standing vertically on two legs. In the bronze inscriptions, the head was often simplified into an eye (目). The legs eventually evolved into four dots (灬, unrelated to 火).

Contrast with 鹿, which saw a very different development, and 𢊁 (as in 薦), which is a hybrid: it has the legs of 馬 (灬) but the head of 鹿.
entries.馮: Phono-semantic compound: 仌 (phonetic) + 馬 (horse, semantic).
entries.馺: Phono-semantic compound: 馬 (horse, semantic) + 及 (phonetic)
entries.駁: Phono-semantic compound: 馬 (horse, semantic) + 爻 (phonetic). The phonetic component adds part of the meaning if interpreted as "marks".
entries.駎: Phono-semantic compound: 馬 (horse, semantic) + 由 (phonetic).
entries.駐: Phono-semantic compound: 馬 (horse, semantic) + 主 (phonetic). Cf. 住, with the 人 radical replacing 馬.
entries.駒: Phono-semantic compound: 馬 (horse, semantic) + 句 (phonetic).
entries.駝: Phono-semantic compound: 馬 (horse, semantic) + 它 (phonetic).
entries.駢: Phono-semantic compound: 馬 (horse, semantic) + 并 (phonetic)
entries.駭: Phono-semantic compound: 馬 (horse, semantic) + 亥 (phonetic)
entries.駱: Phono-semantic compound: 馬 (horse, semantic) + 各 (phonetic).
entries.騇: Phono-semantic compound: 馬 (horse, semantic) + 舍 (phonetic).
entries.騎: Phono-semantic compound: 馬 (horse, semantic) + 奇 (phonetic) – to ride horseback

entries.髭:
Originally a Pictogram – depicting a man with a prominent mustache.

Later written 頿 or 頾, a Phono-semantic compound: 須 (beard, semantic) + 此 (phonetic), where 須 is the original form of 鬚//.

In the modern form, a Phono-semantic compound: 髟 (hair, semantic) + 此 (phonetic).
entries.髮:

The original form 𩠙 was composed of 首 and 犬. According to Takashi Takada (高田忠周), 犬 is an abbreviation of 犮.

entries.鬯: Pictogram – of a vessel full of sacrificial wine made of fermented black millet and vanilla beans or “tulips” (the millet kernels are perhaps symbolized by four points). The small spoon at the bottom was added later.
entries.鬱: Compound ideogram: 林 (forest) + 大 (standing person) + 勹 (leaning person) — people hiding in a lush forest. Later, an abbreviated 爵 was added, leading to the current form.
entries.鬳: Phono-semantic compound: 虍 (phonetic) + 鬲 (cauldron, semantic).
entries.鬼:
Pictogram – a kneeling man or figure with an ugly face (甶). The ugly face could be a mask. The lower right “dot” is a small 厶; it is a residual tail that was added later – compare 离. Related to 畏 (variant 𠂽), which originally depicts a ghost standing with a stick in hand.

Compare 異, in which the 田 also derives from a face and indicates a mask. Compare also 禺, in which the top component represents either a mask or a monkey's head.

entries.鳥:
Pictogram: a bird with a dangling tail.

Compare 烏, which is very similar, of similar origin, and 隹, which originated from a similar image of a bird, but is today rather more abstract and less recognizable. Compare to Egyptian 𓄿
entries.鳧: Phono-semantic compound: 隹 (semantic) + 勹 (phonetic). The 隹 later changed to 鳥 and 勹 to 几.
entries.鳩: Phono-semantic compound: 九 (phonetic) + 鳥 (bird, semantic).
entries.鳳:
Pictogram: a bird with a prominent crest and tail feathers. The phonetic component 凡 (sometimes written as 戌) was often added. 

Bronze inscriptions record the presentation of live feng (中乎歸生鳳于王), indicating it originally referred to a real bird, likely the peacock (compare 皇, which depicts a peacock feather).

In the oracle bone script, it was borrowed for 風. The character 風 is actually a later corrupted abbreviation of 鳳, with its 虫 component evolving from the peacock's tail feathers.

entries.鹿:
Pictogram – a deer. Current form is highly abstracted – legs have transformed to 比 – note grouping of front and rear legs, which are bent – head has transformed to middle component (similar to 凸/曲), while antlers on top and extended lip/mouth on left transformed into 广. This transformation occurred during seal characters.

Contrast the very different development of 馬, and the transformation in 廌 (as in 薦), which has the head of 鹿 but the legs of 馬 (灬).

entries.黃:
In the oracle bone script, 黃 was written in two forms. One depicts a person 大 with a swollen abdomen, the more detailed forms adding a dot for the navel, representing an infirm person; it is read as 尪. With 火 added beneath, the character is used of the victim in the burning sacrifice.

The other form also depicts a person, with a 田 shape or a simplified 口 at the abdomen; it has been proposed as the original form of 璜. In the oracle bone script it is used for the former Shang minister 黃尹, for the color "yellow", and in place names; or, with 夕 appended, it denotes dusk.

In bronze inscriptions, and sporadically already in the late oracle bone script groups, 廿 is added above the 大, depicting a wide open mouth crying upward. Compare 堇.
entries.黎: Phono-semantic compound: 黍 (millet, semantic) + 利 (phonetic); however, the semantic component is contracted. A regularized but unused variant is 㴝, while a variant without contraction is 𥣥.

entries.黑: Pictogram – oracle bone form uncertain, perhaps the element in 𦰩 / 堇 without 口. Bronze inscriptions added dots to a prominent head, usually read as facial tattoos 墨刑.
entries.黒: Variant of 黑. Simplified from 黑., replacing two dots with one stroke. The modern Japanese usage is of reform (shinjitai) nature. Compare 毋, the shinjitai of 母.

Also phonetically (and perhaps semantically) borrowed to indicate "to divine" (then written as 鼑 > 貞). See also the original version of 具 and 則.

entries.鼘: Phono-semantic compound: 鼓 (drum, semantic) + 淵 (phonetic).
entries.鼚: Phono-semantic compound: 鼓 (drums, semantic) + 長 (phonetic)
entries.鼠: Pictogram – a mouse or rat. In the seal script form, which is inherited in the regular script, the upper component resembling 臼 represents the open mouth of a rat with teeth displayed, and the lower component represents the two feet of a rat on the left and a tail on the right.
entries.鼢: Phono-semantic compound: 鼠 (mouse; rat, semantic) + 分 (phonetic).
entries.鼣: Compound ideogram: 鼠 (mouse; rat) + 犬 (dog).
entries.鼩: Phono-semantic compound: 鼠 (mouse; rat, semantic) + 句 (phonetic).
entries.鼪: Phono-semantic compound: 鼠 (mouse; rat, semantic) + 生 (phonetic).
entries.鼬: Phono-semantic compound: 鼠 (rat, semantic) + 由 (phonetic)
entries.鼴: Phono-semantic compound: 鼠 (rat, semantic) + 匽 (phonetic).
entries.鼹: Phono-semantic compound: 鼠 (rat, semantic) + 晏 (phonetic).
entries.鼻:
Phono-semantic compound: 自 (nose, semantic) + 畀 (phonetic).

自 originally referred to this word, but came to be used to refer to 自 instead, so the sense of “nose” has been replaced by this character. Some scholars interpret 鼻* as a combination of a nose (自) and two lungs (畀), however 畀 on oracle bones represents an arrow.
entries.齂: Phono-semantic compound: 鼻 (nose, semantic) + 隶 (phonetic).
entries.齅: Compound ideogram: 鼻 (nose, semantic) + 臭 (smell, phonetic).
entries.齊:
Pictogram: multiple neatly arranged fruits or thorns. The oracle bone script of 櫅 depicts these growing on a tree.

Possibly related to 薺 (蒺藜, a plant with thorny fruits) and 櫅 (white jujube).
entries.齋: Phono-semantic compound: 齊 (phonetic) + 示 (god; deity, semantic).
entries.齎: Phono-semantic compound: 齊 (phonetic) + 貝 (cowry, semantic)
entries.齏: Originally 𠬘; Phono-semantic compound: 齊 (phonetic) + 韭 (leek, semantic).
entries.齐:
Rare and unorthodox variant of 齊, found in informal writing during the Ming and Qing dynasties period. This character is not a further simplification of 斉.

Unrelated to 喬 > 乔 and to the Kangxi radicals 儿 and 文.
entries.齒: Pictogram – a mouth full of teeth. Now Phono-semantic compound – with phonetic 止 added.
entries.齞: Phono-semantic compound: 齒 (tooth, semantic) + 只 (phonetic).
entries.齡: Phono-semantic compound: 齒 (tooth, semantic) + 令 (phonetic) – tooth being associated with age. Compare English long in the tooth and don't look a gift horse in the mouth.
entries.齣: Phono-semantic compound: 齒 (tooth, semantic) + 句 (phonetic).
entries.齩: Phono-semantic compound: 齒 (tooth, semantic) + 交 (phonetic).
entries.齪: Phono-semantic compound: 齒 (teeth, semantic) + 足 (phonetic).
entries.齭: Phono-semantic compound: 齒 (tooth, semantic) + 所 (phonetic).
entries.齲: Phono-semantic compound: 齒 (teeth, semantic) + 禹 (phonetic).
entries.齵: Phono-semantic compound: 齒 (tooth, semantic) + 禺 (phonetic).
entries.齷: Phono-semantic compound: 齒 (teeth, semantic) + 屋 (phonetic).
entries.齺: Phono-semantic compound: 齒 (tooth, semantic) + 芻 (phonetic).
entries.齼: Phono-semantic compound: 齒 (tooth, semantic) + 楚 (phonetic).
entries.齾: Phono-semantic compound: 獻 (phonetic) + 齒 (tooth, semantic).
entries.龐: Phono-semantic compound: 广 (house, semantic) + 龍 (phonetic).
entries.龕:
Shuowen: Phono-semantic compound: 合 (phonetic) + 龍 (semantic).

Duan Yucai consider it a corrupted form of 𪚕: Phono-semantic compound: 今 (phonetic) + 龍 (semantic).
entries.龜: Pictogram: A drawing of a turtle seen from the side and from above (Bronze inscriptions).
entries.龠:
Pictogram – a bamboo Pan flute in which two mouths (吅) perhaps indicate the round top of the bamboo pipes. In the bronze inscriptions, 亼 (a flipped 口) was added on top to show a mouth playing the instrument.

Shuowen interprets it as an Compound ideogram: 品 + 侖, however his analysis does not match the original appearance. The bottom component is identical but unrelated to 冊 since it originally represents bamboo slips. The whole character is similar but unrelated to 侖.
entries.龷: 龷 was originally written as ⿻巛一 (𡿧) the character for floodwaters. However, it has different meanings according to each character.
entries.𠀄:
Unorthodox variant of 衛* originally found in Zhongwen Da Cidian 《中文大辭典》, a Taiwanese dictionary based on the Japanese Dai Kan-Wa Jiten. 

This character is visually similar to 卫, the official simplified form of 衛* and its existence may have been influenced by the Japanese katakana ヱ.
entries.𠀉: 丘 with a stroke omitted, due to naming taboo of Confucius.
entries.𠀊: From part of 大 and part of 小 – not big, not small.
entries.𠀝: Compound ideogram: 下 (down; below) + 上 (up; above) – below the zenith and above the earth – the sky.
entries.𠁓: Phono-semantic compound: 不 (no, semantic) + 欲 (phonetic).
entries.𠁼: From Siddhaṃ script 𑖂 or 𑖃.
entries.𠂇: Pictogram – a left hand. 又 flipped. See also the top component of 灰, in which a left hand is barely visible.
entries.𠂢: Pictogram – of a long river with tributaries. The horizontal flip of 永.
entries.𠂤:
Pictogram – hills. According to Kato Tsuneken (加藤常賢), it could also represent buttocks.

In 官 it represents multiple rooms under a roof. See also 師 (> 师) and 追.
entries.𠃓: Simplified from 昜. in Cursive script.
entries.𠅘: Calligraphic variation, as with 高～髙. In this variation, the body of the tower is more visible and recognizable.
entries.𠅙: Calligraphic variation, as with 高～髙. In this variant, the body of the tower is more recognizable.
entries.𠅢: Calligraphic variation, as with 高～髙.
entries.𠆫: Simplified from 傳., by analogy with 团. Limited to Jiangsu and Guangdong. First attested in 1956.
entries.𠇑: Compound ideogram: 人 (human, semantic) + 父 (father, phonetic).
entries.𠈳: Found in the historical Yupian 《玉篇》 dictionary from the Liang dynasty (543 AD).
entries.𠊉: Ligature of 会 + 勿 mainly used in Northern Wu, cf. the Wu vernacular characters 覅 and 朆 first attested in Suzhounese literature.
entries.𠊩: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (human, semantic) + 孨 (phonetic).
entries.𠊬: Shuowen: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (human, semantic) + 卻 (phonetic).
entries.𠋴: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 剡 (phonetic).
entries.𠌢: Found in the historical Jiyun 集韻 and Leipian 類篇 dictionaries published during the Song dynasty.
entries.𠎺: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (person, semantic) + 嵬 (phonetic).
entries.𠐤: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (human, semantic) + 褢 (phonetic).
entries.𠐦: Phono-semantic compound: 人 (human, semantic) + 褱 (phonetic).
entries.𠑵: 弗* in 佛* replaced with 西域 + 哲.
entries.𠔼: Not attested as an individual character before the seal script. Shuowen considers it to be an Compound ideogram: 冖 + 一 (a cloth to cover something). Some consider it to be a variant of the nearly homophonous 冃 (a hat). See 冡.
entries.𠕇: Compound ideogram: 冇 + 丶. In Min Nan, 冇, which is 有 without the two inner strokes, is used to mean "empty, hollow", originally when describing grain kernels. Adding 丶 inside 冇 shows a full kernel in the hollow husk, therefore meaning "hard, solid".
entries.𠖫: Phono-semantic compound: 冖 (cover, semantic) + 贑 (phonetic).
entries.𠙹: Pictogram – a bamboo container. Attested since oracle bones script. (Lexi-MF)
entries.𠚩: Phono-semantic compound: 卜 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.𠚬: Phono-semantic compound: 卜 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.𠚺: Phono-semantic compound: 少 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife; blade; sword, semantic).
entries.𠛧: Possibly an Compound ideogram: 肉 (meat) + 刀 (knife).
entries.𠜺: Phono-semantic compound: 戾 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.𠞯: Phono-semantic compound: 雪 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.𠟶: Phono-semantic compound: 窟 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.𠠂: Phono-semantic compound: 盠 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.𠠍: Phono-semantic compound: 黎 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.𠠫: Phono-semantic compound: 麗 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.𠠻: 反 + 力. A typographical error. See 𠡀.
entries.𠢕: Phono-semantic compound: 敖 (phonetic) + 力 (strength, semantic).
entries.𠣘: Phono-semantic compound: 勹 (wrap, semantic) + 舟 (phonetic).
entries.𠥓: Recorded as the Zhòuwén (籀文) form of 匚 in Shuowen Jiezi 說文解字.
entries.𠦒: Pictogram – a hunting net. Original form of 禽 and 畢 in oracle bone script. Compare with 單
entries.𠧩: Phono-semantic compound: 每 (phonetic) + 卜 (to divine, semantic).
entries.𠨫: Phono-semantic compound: 䜌 (phonetic) + 卵 (egg, semantic).
entries.𠫑: Attested in the bronze script of the Warring States era. 容庚 speculates it to be a more complex form of 驫. The character may be alternatively transcribed as ⿸广驫.
entries.𠫓: Pictogram: inverted 子 — a newborn baby coming out of the womb head-first; see 毓. In the character 棄, it represents a newborn baby thrown out of a basket.
entries.𠬛: Simplified from 𠬸. — from seal script to clerical script.
entries.𠬝: Compound ideogram: 卩 (kneeling person) + 又 (hand) – a hand subduing a person. Original form of 服.
entries.𠬹: Possibly an Compound ideogram: 又 (hand) + 糸 (silk).
entries.𠭗: Compound ideogram: 𣦻 (to damage and penetrate, semantic) + 井 (well; pit; trap, phonetic).
entries.𠭴: Possibly a Phono-semantic compound: 叕 (connected, semantic) + 出 (phonetic).
entries.𠮄: Phono-semantic compound: 叕 (connected, semantic) + 兌 (phonetic).
entries.𠮙: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 乙 (phonetic).
entries.𠮟: Found in the historical Longkan Shoujian 《龍龕手鑑》 dictionary compiled in 997 AD.
entries.𠮷: Variant of 吉, where the component 士 has been replaced with 土.
entries.𠯸:
Phono-semantic compound: 口 (semantic) + 厅 (phonetic).

Corrupted into 听, which is now the standardized simplified form of 聽.
entries.𠰉: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 召 (phonetic).
entries.𠱂: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 凸 (phonetic).
entries.𠱓:
Simplified from 危.

Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 危 (phonetic).
entries.𠲎: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 伐 (phonetic).
entries.𠲱: Phono-semantic compound: 丯 (weed, semantic) + 各 (phonetic).
entries.𠳹: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 床 (phonetic).
entries.𠴔: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 呈 (phonetic).
entries.𠴕: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 妙 (phonetic).
entries.𠷇: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 施 (phonetic).
entries.𠺁: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 弱 (phonetic).
entries.𠺅: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 烈 (phonetic).
entries.𠼮: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 偽 (phonetic).
entries.𡀇: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 董 (phonetic).
entries.𡂏: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 巤 (phonetic).
entries.𡅘: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 臘 (phonetic).
entries.𡆇: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth; colloquial, semantic) + 鑊 (phonetic).
entries.𡆕: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 戀 (phonetic).
entries.𡆧: Pictogram: ironware. Original meaning is now written as 𨭗.
entries.𡈊: Compound ideogram: 囗 (enclosure) + 馬 (horse); a horse being contained.
entries.𡈼: Pictogram: A human (亻) standing on soil (土).
entries.𡊁: Possibly a Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 抑 (phonetic).
entries.𡊧: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 卯 (phonetic).
entries.𡊶: Possibly a Phono-semantic compound: 土 (earth, semantic) + 抑 (phonetic).
entries.𡍬: Phono-semantic compound: 圥 (phonetic) + 目 (eye, semantic).
entries.𡐑: Phono-semantic compound: 圥 (phonetic) + 目 (eye, semantic).
entries.𡐓: Phono-semantic compound: 土 (dirt; earth, semantic) + 康 (phonetic).
entries.𡚒: See 奮, where the 田 component is replaced by 臼, possibly due to unclear printing.
entries.𡡁: Phono-semantic compound: 女 (woman, semantic) + 悉 (phonetic).
entries.𡢢: Phono-semantic compound: 女 (woman, semantic) + 虞 (phonetic).
entries.𡤥: Phono-semantic compound: 女 (woman, semantic) + 儵 (phonetic).
entries.𡦼: Replacement of 宀 + 豕 with 宀 + 人.
entries.𡨄: Compound ideogram: 宀 (house) + 工 (two items) + 廾 (two hands) – stuffing the house with items. Similar but unrelated to 共 but partly related to 展.
entries.𡳬: Phono-semantic compound: 尸 (sitting person, semantic) + 盧 (phonetic).
entries.𡵀: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 亡 (phonetic).
entries.𡵙: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 卬 (phonetic).
entries.𡷧: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 吟 (phonetic).
entries.𡷴: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 岑 (phonetic).
entries.𡾻: Phono-semantic compound: 山 (mountain, semantic) + 臧 (phonetic).
entries.𡿧: Pictogram: a flood. One of the original forms of 災.
entries.𡿺: Pictogram: 巛 (hair, semantic) + 囟 (fontanel, semantic).
entries.𢀓: Liding; compare the gallery at https://zi.tools/zi/巨.
entries.𢀖: One of the 54 simplified radical components listed in the 1956 Chinese Character Simplification Scheme by the People's Republic of China.
entries.𢀜:
Simplified from 巩.

Phono-semantic compound: 工 (phonetic) + 丮 (semantic).
entries.𢃇: Phono-semantic compound: 巾 (cloth, semantic) + 里 (phonetic).
entries.𢄻: Phono-semantic compound: 巾 (square piece of cloth, semantic) + 散 (phonetic).
entries.𢅒: Phono-semantic compound: 巾 (cloth, semantic) + 亶 (phonetic).
entries.𢆡: Phono-semantic compound: 乳 (milk; breast, semantic) + 年 (phonetic).
entries.𢇇: Phono-semantic compound: 絲 (silk, semantic) + 卵 (phonetic).
entries.𢑓:
Pictogram – a pig with penis, meaning "male pig". Shuowen considered this character "pig with foot" (从彑，下象其足), which is incorrect.

See also 家. Compare 豖, in which the male pig is castrated since the penis is detached from his body.
entries.𢓋: Phono-semantic compound: 彳 (to step, semantic) + 卬 (phonetic).
entries.𢓕: Phono-semantic compound: 彳 (step, semantic) + 占 (phonetic).
entries.𢘽: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 曳 (phonetic).
entries.𢜫: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 省 (phonetic).
entries.𢜶: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 叜 (phonetic).
entries.𢟹: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 辱 (phonetic).
entries.𢡆: Phono-semantic compound: 豤 (phonetic) + 心 (heart, semantic).
entries.𢣩: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 銀 (phonetic).
entries.𢦅: Phono-semantic compound: 心 (heart, semantic) + 贛 (phonetic).
entries.𢦈: Phono-semantic compound: 忄 (heart, semantic) + 蠻 (phonetic).
entries.𢦏: Phono-semantic compound: 戈 (semantic) + 才 (phonetic). The original version is 𢦔, one of the original forms of 災.
entries.𢦞: Possibly as Compound ideogram: 戈 (halberd; weapon) + 爪 (hand; claw; fingers), dismembered body part of the slain enemy as trophy.
entries.𢩨: Phono-semantic compound: 手 (hand, semantic) + 丂 (phonetic).
entries.𢫨: Phono-semantic compound: 手 (hand, semantic) + 戎 (phonetic).
entries.𢫳: Phono-semantic compound: 手 (hand, semantic) + 斥 (phonetic).
entries.𢫸: Phono-semantic compound: 手 (hand, semantic) + 吳 (phonetic).
entries.𢬗: Phono-semantic compound: 手 (hand, semantic) + 耒 (phonetic).
entries.𢭂: Phono-semantic compound: 手 (hand, semantic) + 牢 (phonetic).
entries.𢮎: Phono-semantic compound: 手 (hand, semantic) + 虎 (phonetic).
entries.𢱉: Phono-semantic compound: 扌 (hand, semantic) + 歪 (phonetic).
entries.𢱤: Phono-semantic compound: 手 (hand, semantic) + 送 (phonetic)
entries.𢲛: Phono-semantic compound: 手 (hand, semantic) + 徒 (phonetic).
entries.𢳂: Phono-semantic compound: 扌 (hand, semantic) + 畢 (phonetic).
entries.𢴵: Phono-semantic compound: 手 (hand, semantic) + 焱 (phonetic).
entries.𢴿: Phono-semantic compound: 手 (hand, semantic) + 朝 (phonetic).
entries.𢸨: Phono-semantic compound: 手 (hand, semantic) + 橐 (phonetic).
entries.𢸪: Phono-semantic compound: 手 (hand, semantic) + 蚤 (phonetic).
entries.𢹓: Phono-semantic compound: 手 (hand, semantic) + 齋 (phonetic).
entries.𢹖: Phono-semantic compound: 手 (hand, semantic) + 馘 (phonetic).
entries.𢻴: Phono-semantic compound: 屯 (phonetic) + 攴 (to beat, strike, semantic).
entries.𢼍: Phono-semantic compound: 出 (phonetic) + 攴 (to beat, semantic).
entries.𢾏: Phono-semantic compound: 客 (phonetic) + 攴 (to rap, beat, semantic).
entries.𣂔: Compound ideogram: 片 (split wood) + 斤 (axe).
entries.𣎳: Pictogram: a hemp stalk (屮) with skin (八) being stripped off.
entries.𣏒: Found in the Qing dynasty Zihuibu 《字彙補》 dictionary.
entries.𣏟: Two hemp stalks with skin stripped off 𣎳 side by side. Similar but unrelated to 林.
entries.𣑀: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 吳 (phonetic).
entries.𣔼: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 竿 (phonetic).
entries.𣘠: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 笴 (phonetic).
entries.𣚎: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (wood, semantic) + 絫 (phonetic).
entries.𣚺:
Compound of 未成母.

See also 膥.
entries.𣟄: Phono-semantic compound: 木 (tree, semantic) + 橐 (phonetic).
entries.𣡌: Found in the Jiyun 《集韻》 dictionary from the Song dynasty.
entries.𣤜: Possibly a Phono-semantic compound: 欼 (phonetic) + 木 (tree, semantic).
entries.𣥂: A stylized reversed foot (止) that can be found at the bottom of the character 步, which indicates "footsteps". Unrelated to 少.
entries.𣦷: Phono-semantic compound: 歹 (death, semantic) + 乙 (phonetic).
entries.𣦻: Compound ideogram: 歺 (bone remnants) + 又 (hand). See 餐. Unrelated to 㱿 (variant of 𣪊).
entries.𣧔: Phono-semantic compound: 歹 (death, semantic) + 勾 (phonetic).
entries.𣧖: Phono-semantic compound: 歹 (death, semantic) + 尐 (phonetic).
entries.𣩓: Phono-semantic compound: 歹 (bone remains, semantic) + 巢 (phonetic).
entries.𣬭: Phono-semantic compound: 冉 (phonetic) + 毛 (hair, semantic).
entries.𣭲: Phono-semantic compound: 甬 (phonetic) + 毛 (fur, semantic).
entries.𣱄: Phono-semantic compound: 鹽 (phonetic) + 毛 (hair, semantic).
entries.𣱛: Phono-semantic compound: 气 (phonetic) + 火 (fire, semantic).
entries.𣱧: Compound ideogram: 气 (gas) + 重 (heavy), as it was the heaviest gaseous element (at room temperature) at that time. 重 is also the phonetic component.
entries.𣺤: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 甾 (phonetic) + 刀 (knife, semantic).
entries.𣻚: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 術 (phonetic).
entries.𣽆: Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 筑 (phonetic).
entries.𤆎: Phono-semantic compound: 才 (phonetic) + 火 (fire, semantic).
entries.𤇚: Phono-semantic compound: 火 (fire, semantic) + 斥 (phonetic).
entries.𤇢: Phono-semantic compound: 火 (fire, semantic) + 白 (phonetic).
entries.𤇾: Found in 《綴遺齋彝器款識考釋》 from the Qing dynasty period.
entries.𤈦: Phono-semantic compound: 火 (fire, semantic) + 尾 (phonetic) – fire.
entries.𤊶: Phono-semantic compound: 火 (fire, semantic) + 剌 (phonetic).
entries.𤋗: Phono-semantic compound: 昫 (phonetic) + 火 (fire, semantic).
entries.𤍞:
Naming taboo (避諱); the last stroke in 燁 was omitted to avoid using the same character in the Kangxi Emperor's personal name, which was.

This also produced 𤣥 < 玄.
entries.𤎝: Phono-semantic compound: 雁 (phonetic) + 火 (fire, semantic).
entries.𤏶: Phono-semantic compound: 火 (fire, semantic) + 麀 (phonetic) – “to stew in water”. Later written 爊 or 熬.
entries.𤐫: 𢍱 (A pair of hands holding and lifting up an object stylized as 囟, perhaps a nest) with the radical of the fire at the bottom.
entries.𤑟: Phono-semantic compound: 火 (fire, semantic) + 魯 (phonetic).
entries.𤒂: Phono-semantic compound: 光 (light, semantic) + 翟 (phonetic).
entries.𤔔: Compound ideogram: 糸 (silk, threads) + 冂 (beater, heddle, comb) + 𠬪 (two hands) — two persons disentangling a roll of threads using their hands with the help of a tool. Compositionally related to 受.
entries.𤔢: Phono-semantic compound: 爪 (claw, nail, semantic) + 蚤 (phonetic).
entries.𤖴: Phono-semantic compound: 片 (split wood, semantic) + 斥 (phonetic). Originally written 𤗙.
entries.𤗚: Phono-semantic compound: 片 (slice, semantic) + 畐 (phonetic).
entries.𤗭: Phono-semantic compound: 片 (slice, semantic) + 虖 (phonetic).
entries.𤘘:
Simplified from 口.

Phono-semantic compound: 牛 (cattle, semantic) + 口 (phonetic).
entries.𤘴: Compound ideogram: 牛 (cow) + 攴 (a whip).
entries.𤟧: Phono-semantic compound: 犬 (dog, semantic) + 思 (phonetic).
entries.𤣥:
Naming taboo (避諱); the last dot in 玄 was omitted to avoid using the same character in the Kangxi Emperor's personal name, which was.

This was also applied to derived characters; characters like 弦 and 畜 were also missing the last dot in 玄 during this time.

This also produced 𤍞 < 燁.

entries.𥁕:
Ideogram: a person (人) bathing in warm water (now written 囗) in a container (皿) full of warm water — original form of 溫. See also 攸.

Alternatively, according to Xu Shen, an Compound ideogram: 囚 (prisoner) + 皿 (dish) – feeding a prisoner from a dish. However, the shape in the oracle bones is different.

entries.𬡤: Pictogram: a 衣 with dots inside — original form of 繚. It later evolved graphically to a compound of 炏 + 衣.
entries.𬥐: Phono-semantic compound: 父 (phonetic) + 貝 (cowrie, semantic).
entries.𬮢:
One of the 324 simplified characters introduced by the Republic of China (Kuomintang government) in 1935 as a simplified form of 鬨 but was later retracted in 1936. 

This character is obsolete in modern use. In the 1956 first round revision table of variant Chinese characters (第一批异体字整理表) by the People's Republic of China, 鬨 and 閧 were listed as Variant Chinese characters that were replaced by 哄 as the orthodox form.
entries.𬮤: Simplified from 閤. Found in the 8th supplementary set of China's SJ/T 11239–2001 (Information technology: Chinese ideograms coded character set for information interchange) as a character designated for use in placenames.
entries.𬮦: Simplified from 關. from cursive script 門 → 门 and 𢇇 → 关.
entries.𬳩: Compound ideogram: 馬 (horse) + 攴 (to rap, hit).
entries.𬳬: Phono-semantic compound: 馬 (horse, semantic) + 更 (phonetic).
entries.𬵑: Kokuji (created in Japan). 魚 + 辺.
entries.𬺞: Unorthodox variant Simplified from 龜. found in the Ming dynasty orthographic dictionary 《俗書刊誤》. Also found in 《宋元以來俗字譜》, a Variant Chinese character dictionary compiled in 1930.
entries.𬽷: Simplified from 儣. in Japanese shinjitai.
entries.𭀦: Simplified from 耀., replacing 翟 with the more phonetically similar 夭 instead.
entries.𭃊: 刁; probably a variant form of 刕.
entries.𭌇: Phono-semantic compound: 口 (mouth, semantic) + 鄰 (phonetic).
entries.𭓤: Possibly a Phono-semantic compound: 宀 (roof, semantic) + 布 (phonetic).
entries.𭯹: Possibly a Phono-semantic compound: 水 (water, semantic) + 抑 (phonetic).
entries.𭸔: Phono-semantic compound: 犬 (dog, semantic) + 厖 (phonetic).
entries.𮄿:
Simplified from 龘. in Japanese shinjitai.

竜 (dragon).
entries.𮅔: Simplified from 簿. Compare 傳→伝 (專→云).
entries.𮑉: Phono-semantic compound: 艸 (grass, semantic) + 稈 (phonetic).
entries.𮡨: Compound ideogram: 金 (metal, semantic) + 五 (five, phonetic).
entries.𮪊: Phono-semantic compound: 馬 (horse, semantic) + 取 (phonetic).
entries.𮸽: 飞 (to fly); Simplified from 飝.
